nodes.title: Laptop OS and architecture are supported
nodes.assumption: The laptop is Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11 (x64/arm64), macOS 12+ (Intel or Apple silicon), or a glibc Linux desktop. process.platform is win32, darwin or linux. Ashley is native to each OS; it neither mirrors nor uses WSL (design rule of 2026-09-27).
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: read process.platform, process.arch and os.release(). Windows passes if [Environment]::OSVersion.Version.Build >= 17763 (PowerShell). macOS passes if `sw_vers -productVersion` >= 12. Linux passes if `ldd --version` prints glibc.
failure_signatures: Unable to install extension 'openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu' as it is not compatible with VS Code
'ssh' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.
nodes.manual_fix: Use a supported laptop (Windows 10 1809+/11, macOS 12+, or a mainstream Linux desktop). Ask the lead for a loaner if needed.
nodes.future_risk: Windows 10 went out of support in Oct 2025, and WSU C&IT may block unsupported builds from campus Wi-Fi or the VPN. VS Code and the Claude Code native binary drop old macOS releases over time.

nodes.title: VS Code is Microsoft's build, installed at a stable path
nodes.assumption: Ashley needs Microsoft's VS Code, installed normally. VSCodium, Cursor and Windsurf lack the Microsoft auth provider and Microsoft's Remote-SSH, and the getExtension ids differ there. The Flatpak build is sandboxed from the host's ssh and ~/.ssh. On macOS the app must run from /Applications, not from App Translocation. On Linux use the .deb/.rpm, not the snap. process.execPath is registered as the MCP runtime, and under the snap or translocation that path changes.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: vscode.env.appName starts with 'Visual Studio Code' and vscode.env.uriScheme is 'vscode' or 'vscode-insiders'. process.execPath contains none of '/snap/', '/AppTranslocation/' or a Flatpak prefix, and process.env.FLATPAK_ID is undefined.
failure_signatures: No authentication provider 'microsoft' is currently registered.
getExtension('ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh') undefined in a VS Code fork
MCP server ashley: Failed to connect (after a snap refresh or macOS relaunch)
spawn ssh ENOENT (Flatpak)
nodes.manual_fix: Install VS Code from code.visualstudio.com. On macOS drag it into /Applications. On Linux use the .deb/.rpm package.
nodes.future_risk: More students use AI-IDE forks. Microsoft may change appName or uriScheme, and snap or Flatpak packaging may change.

nodes.title: The home directory Ashley writes is the one ssh reads
nodes.assumption: os.homedir() is local and writable, and it is the directory whose .ssh the ssh client reads: %USERPROFILE% on Windows, $HOME elsewhere. expandHome() expands only a leading '~/', so ashley.identityFile must use tilde form or an absolute path ('~\' is not expanded).
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -G wsu-grid` has an identityfile line equal to <os.homedir()>/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu (normalise separators). In the extension host, fs.accessSync(os.homedir(), fs.constants.W_OK) succeeds. On Windows, %HOME% is unset or equal to %USERPROFILE%.
failure_signatures: no such identity: C:\Users\<user>/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu: No such file or directory
EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir
key created under C:\Users\<user>\.ssh while Git's ssh reads H:\.ssh (HOME redirected to a network share)
nodes.manual_fix: Remove a user-level HOME variable, or point it at %USERPROFILE%. Alternatively, set ashley.identityFile to an absolute path.
nodes.future_risk: University-managed Windows images with folder redirection or roaming profiles.

nodes.title: OpenSSH client installed (>= 7.6)
nodes.assumption: An OpenSSH client >= 7.6 is installed. It must support StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new, the '+' algorithm syntax, ProxyJump and `ssh -G`. On Windows that is the 'OpenSSH Client' optional feature in System32\OpenSSH (9.5p1 measured on Windows 11). macOS uses /usr/bin/ssh; Linux uses the openssh-client package.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -V` (prints to stderr) matches /OpenSSH[^_]*_([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)/ with version >= 7.6. On Windows also `Get-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client*` reports State Installed.
failure_signatures: 'ssh' is not recognized as an internal or external command
spawn ssh ENOENT (run() returns code 127)
Bad SSH2 Mac spec '+hmac-sha1'
command-line line 0: unsupported option "accept-new".
nodes.auto_repair: Only with the user's consent and a UAC prompt. Windows: `Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0`. Linux: `pkexec apt-get install -y openssh-client` (or dnf). macOS: nothing to install.
nodes.manual_fix: Windows: Settings > System > Optional features > Add a feature > OpenSSH Client, then restart VS Code.
nodes.future_risk: Windows moving to OpenSSH 10.x, whose new default KEX (mlkem768x25519) is untested against the grid's 7.4. Microsoft could ship OpenSSH from another path (winget, Program Files). A future client could drop hmac-sha1, which the grid has required from Windows.

nodes.title: spawn('ssh') resolves to the working OpenSSH
nodes.assumption: run('ssh'/'scp'/'ssh-keygen') in the extension host, the MCP server and the CLI resolves on PATH to the same working OpenSSH that Remote-SSH uses. On Windows, libuv tries only .exe/.com on PATH. resolveExecutable(), which prefers System32\OpenSSH, is applied only to terminals, not to run(), relay or scp.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: run('ssh', ['-V']) exits 0 with 'OpenSSH' in stderr. On Windows the first line of `where.exe ssh` is C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe or equals remote.SSH.path; on macOS/Linux use `command -v ssh`. Compare with resolveExecutable('ssh').
failure_signatures: spawn ssh ENOENT
run() code 127
C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\ssh.exe first on PATH (version string lacks 'for_Windows')
Unable to resolve your shell environment in a reasonable time (macOS VS Code)
terminal login works but the tree says 'Cannot reach the grid'
nodes.auto_repair: Before spawning, prepend %SystemRoot%\System32\OpenSSH to process.env.PATH in the extension host (safe, process-local). Code fix: route run(), scp and the relay through resolveExecutable().
nodes.manual_fix: Put C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH before Git's usr\bin in PATH, or set remote.SSH.path to the same ssh.exe.
nodes.future_risk: Git for Windows updating its bundled ssh. Windows moving OpenSSH out of System32. VS Code changing how it resolves the shell environment on macOS.

nodes.title: ssh-keygen creates an ed25519 key
nodes.assumption: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -C '<id>@wayne.edu ashley' -f <key>` works through spawn with an empty-string argument. On Windows it sets an owner-only ACL on the private key.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -q -f <scratch>/ashley_probe` exits 0 and <scratch>/ashley_probe.pub exists; delete both afterwards. Once the key exists: `ssh-keygen -l -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu.pub` prints '(ED25519)'.
failure_signatures: ssh-keygen failed: ...
Saving key "..." failed: No such file or directory
unknown key type ed25519
nodes.auto_repair: Run stepSshKey.run: it creates ~/.ssh and generates the key, and never overwrites an existing pair.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard step 'SSH key' again, or generate the key by hand with the command above.
nodes.future_risk: A FIPS-mode managed laptop may refuse ed25519, which would need an ecdsa fallback.

nodes.title: scp uploads the grid scripts into an existing ~/.ashley/bin
nodes.assumption: `scp -q <batch opts> <files...> wsu-grid:~/.ashley/bin/` copies the six grid files, and the target directory already exists. OpenSSH >= 9.0 clients use the SFTP protocol by default, which needs the grid's sftp-server subsystem; the 7.4 server lacks the expand-path extension. The upload has worked from Greg's laptop, where the directory existed. How the 9.x client treats '~/' against this server when the directory is missing is not recorded.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'test -d ~/.ashley/bin && echo ok'` prints ok. Then `scp -q -o BatchMode=yes <1-byte file> wsu-grid:~/.ashley/bin/.ashley_probe` exits 0, followed by `ssh wsu-grid 'rm -f ~/.ashley/bin/.ashley_probe'`.
failure_signatures: upload failed: scp: ...: No such file or directory
subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed
nodes.auto_repair: Create the directory with a shell-expanded command, `ssh wsu-grid 'mkdir -p ~/.ashley/bin ~/.ashley/log'`, and retry. If the SFTP subsystem is refused, retry with `scp -O` (legacy protocol).
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid' again after the directory exists. Send the log to the lead.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT disabling the SFTP subsystem. OpenSSH removing legacy scp (-O). A newer grid sshd adding expand-path (benign).

nodes.title: ~/.ssh and ~/.ssh/config are owner-only
nodes.assumption: ~/.ssh (700) and ~/.ssh/config (600) belong to the user and are not writable by others. Ashley writes config with mode 0o600 but never chmods an existing .ssh. On Windows Node ignores the mode, and OpenSSH enforces NTFS ACLs (only the user, SYSTEM and Administrators).
nodes.check: Laptop, macOS/Linux: `stat -c %a ~/.ssh ~/.ssh/config` (macOS: `stat -f %Lp`) gives 700 and 600 or stricter. Windows: `icacls %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config` lists only the user, SYSTEM and Administrators. Decisive on every OS: `ssh -G wsu-grid` exits 0 without a 'Bad owner' line.
failure_signatures: Bad owner or permissions on C:\\Users\\<user>/.ssh/config
Bad owner or permissions on /home/<user>/.ssh/config
nodes.auto_repair: POSIX: `chmod 700 ~/.ssh && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config`. Windows: `icacls "%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config" /inheritance:r /grant:r "%USERNAME%:F"`. Both touch only the user's own files.
nodes.manual_fix: Fix the permissions with the commands above, then rerun the doctor.
nodes.future_risk: Win32-OpenSSH tightening its ACL checks further.
nodes.source: extension/src/core/wizard.ts:303-313; docs/research/deep_research_2026-09-28.json (VS Code topic: Win32-OpenSSH ACL finding)

nodes.title: Grid key pair present, matching, unencrypted, protected
nodes.assumption: ashley.identityFile (default ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu) and its .pub exist and match. The key has no passphrase, because BatchMode must never prompt. The private key is owner-only.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh-keygen -y -P "" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu` exits 0, and the first two fields of its output equal the first two fields of id_ed25519_wsu.pub.
failure_signatures: incorrect passphrase supplied to decrypt private key
Load key "...id_ed25519_wsu": invalid format
WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!
Permissions for '...id_ed25519_wsu' are too open.
no such identity
nodes.auto_repair: If only the .pub is missing, regenerate it with `ssh-keygen -y -f <key> > <key>.pub`. If only the permissions are wrong, run chmod 600 (POSIX) or the icacls grant (Windows). A mismatch or a passphrase has no automatic fix: a new key needs the password and code once.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Reset this laptop' > SSH key, then the wizard again. The grid asks for the password and the six-digit code once.
nodes.future_risk: Low: only key format changes in OpenSSH.

nodes.title: Ashley's managed block in ~/.ssh/config is present, current and first
nodes.assumption: ~/.ssh/config holds exactly one managed block between the ashley markers, at the top of the file and equal to renderBlock(settings). Login host entry: Host wsu-grid [grid] with HostName warrior.grid.wayne.edu, User <AccessID>, IdentityFile, IdentitiesOnly yes, GSSAPIAuthentication no, AddressFamily inet, MACs +hmac-sha1, ServerAlive 60/5 and ConnectTimeout 20. Node entry: Host *.nas.grid.wayne.edu with ProxyJump wsu-grid and StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new.
nodes.check: Laptop: stepSshConfig.check holds (upsertBlock(text) === text). `ssh -G wsu-grid` prints hostname warrior.grid.wayne.edu, user <accessId>, addressfamily inet and gssapiauthentication no, and its macs list contains hmac-sha1. `ssh -G voh3.nas.grid.wayne.edu` prints proxyjump wsu-grid.
failure_signatures: block missing or outdated
ssh: Could not resolve hostname wsu-grid: No such host is known.
Unable to negotiate with <ip> port 22: no matching MAC found. Their offer: hmac-sha1
every ssh call takes ~13 s (AddressFamily line missing)
nodes.auto_repair: Run stepSshConfig.run: it rewrites the block and keeps the previous file as ~/.ssh/config.ashley.bak.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard step 'SSH configuration', or print the block with `node dist/ashley-cli.js ssh-config` and paste it at the top of ~/.ssh/config.
nodes.future_risk: WSU renaming the login host or node domain (ashley.loginHost and ashley.nodeDomain). OpenSSH builds rejecting GSSAPIAuthentication as unsupported. An earlier Host * in an Include file.

nodes.title: The student's own ssh settings keep their meaning after the block is inserted
nodes.assumption: upsertBlock puts the block first and appends the student's old file unchanged. ssh_config scopes each line to the most recent Host or Match, so top-level lines in the old file now fall under 'Host *.nas.grid.wayne.edu' and apply only to compute nodes. Examples: 'Include config.d/*', 'AddKeysToAgent yes', and the Include lines that OrbStack or 1Password write. This is safe only when the old file starts with Host or Match. It is traced in code (defect); sshConfig.test.ts has no case for top-level directives.
nodes.check: Laptop: in ~/.ssh/config, the first non-blank, non-comment line after the end marker starts with 'Host ' or 'Match ' (case-insensitive), or the file ends there. Confirm by comparing `ssh -G <one of the student's hosts>` with the output from ~/.ssh/config.ashley.bak (`ssh -F ~/.ssh/config.ashley.bak -G <host>`).
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname <alias from an Include file> (after Ashley setup)
options that used to apply everywhere (AddKeysToAgent, ServerAliveInterval) now apply only to *.nas.grid.wayne.edu
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the managed block with a final 'Match all' line before the end marker, so the student's later lines are global again. It is a text-only change, config.ashley.bak is kept, and the idempotence test needs updating.
nodes.manual_fix: Move the top-level lines (Include, global options) above the ashley block, or add 'Match all' directly after it.
nodes.future_risk: More tools (OrbStack, Colima, 1Password SSH agent) add a top-level Include to ~/.ssh/config.

nodes.title: Login node host key known and verified
nodes.assumption: warrior.grid.wayne.edu's host key is in ~/.ssh/known_hosts before the first BatchMode call. The wsu-grid block does not set StrictHostKeyChecking, so the default 'ask' fails under BatchMode. Only the terminal fallback (StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new) records the key. The in-panel ssh2 login has no hostVerifier: it neither records nor checks the host key, so the grid password and code go to whichever host answers. After a successful in-panel install, testConnection can therefore fail on the host key, and the wizard asks for the password and code a second time in a terminal (traced in code, not observed).
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh-keygen -F warrior.grid.wayne.edu` exits 0. The fingerprint from `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 warrior.grid.wayne.edu | ssh-keygen -lf -` matches a fingerprint pinned in the extension (none is pinned today).
failure_signatures: Host key verification failed.
WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
A terminal will ask for your grid PASSWORD ... (right after the in-panel login reported 'key installed')
nodes.auto_repair: With a pinned fingerprint shipped in the extension: append the ssh-keyscan line when it matches the pin, and pass a hostVerifier to ssh2 that checks the same pin. Without a pin there is no safe automatic repair.
nodes.manual_fix: On the campus network, run `ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new wsu-grid true` once, or confirm the fingerprint with hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT reinstalling or replacing the login node (CentOS 7 retirement) changes the host key, and every laptop's BatchMode calls fail at once.

nodes.title: Compute node host keys accepted and stable
nodes.assumption: Compute node keys are accepted on first use (StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new in the node block) and stay the same between connections.
nodes.check: Laptop, only to a node where the student has a running job: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu true` shows no 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED' on stderr, and `ssh-keygen -F <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu` lists at most one key per type.
failure_signatures: WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
Host key for asx1.nas.grid.wayne.edu has changed and you have requested strict checking.
Remote-SSH: Could not establish connection ... Host key verification failed
nodes.auto_repair: No silent repair: removing a changed key is safe only after C&IT confirms a reimage. After the user confirms, run `ssh-keygen -R <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu`.
nodes.manual_fix: Check with hpc@wayne.edu whether the node was reinstalled, then run `ssh-keygen -R <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu`.
nodes.future_risk: An OS migration or node reimage rotates every node key at once.

nodes.title: A browser opens for sign-ins and token pages
nodes.assumption: vscode.env.openExternal opens the default browser, and the CLI uses open, xdg-open or `cmd /c start`. The Microsoft, GitHub and claude.ai sign-ins, the Hugging Face token page and the KB links depend on it.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host, only on an explicit Troubleshoot click: openExternal(Uri.parse('https://ondemand.grid.wayne.edu/')) resolves true. For the CLI: `which xdg-open` (Linux) or `which open` (macOS) exits 0.
failure_signatures: openExternal resolved false
xdg-open: no method available for opening
sign-in waits until the student cancels
nodes.manual_fix: Set a default browser in the OS settings. Otherwise copy the URL from the Ashley log into a browser.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code moving Microsoft sign-in to a native broker (WAM on Windows), which changes where the sign-in appears.

nodes.title: The panel can read the clipboard
nodes.assumption: While a token prompt is open, the panel polls vscode.env.clipboard.readText() every second to spot a copied hf_ or sk-ant-oat token.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: save the clipboard, writeText('ashley-probe'), check readText() === 'ashley-probe', then restore it.
failure_signatures: 'Found a token on your clipboard' never appears
readText throws (swallowed at panel.ts:238-240)
nodes.manual_fix: Paste the token into the field in the panel.
nodes.future_risk: Wayland or OS clipboard-access prompts.

nodes.title: No conflicting credentials in the laptop's environment
nodes.assumption: The OS or user environment does not already set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Either would make the local Claude Code bill or authenticate with that value instead of the subscription. GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and HF_TOKEN are not set there either, so they cannot fight the ones Ashley injects.
nodes.check: Laptop: in the extension host, process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are undefined. In a new integrated terminal, `echo $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (PowerShell) or `printenv ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` prints nothing. Report variable names only, never values.
failure_signatures: Claude Code shows API usage billing / apiKeySource ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
gh or git act as a different GitHub account
nodes.manual_fix: Remove the variable from the user environment (Windows: System Properties > Environment Variables; macOS/Linux: the shell profile), then restart VS Code.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code changing which credential wins.

nodes.title: OS keychain backend available for VS Code secrets
nodes.assumption: VS Code SecretStorage has a working OS backend through Electron safeStorage: DPAPI on Windows, Keychain on macOS, and an unlocked libsecret or kwallet on Linux. keytar was removed in VS Code 1.83.
nodes.check: Laptop: vscode.secret-storage round-trips. On Linux, `secret-tool search xdg:schema org.freedesktop.Secret.Generic` exits 0.
failure_signatures: An OS keyring couldn't be identified for storing the encryption related data in your current desktop environment.
tokens show 'missing' after a Windows password reset (DPAPI master key lost)
repeated macOS keychain prompts for 'Code'
nodes.manual_fix: Linux: install and unlock gnome-keyring, or set "password-store": "gnome-libsecret" in argv.json (Preferences: Configure Runtime Arguments). Windows or macOS after a reset: re-enter the tokens with 'Ashley: Manage stored tokens'.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code changing its safeStorage fallback policy (basic_text). Linux desktop keyring changes.

nodes.title: Optional system Node >= 20 (MCP runtime preference, CLI requirement)
nodes.assumption: The extension does not need a system Node. A `node` >= 20 on PATH is preferred as the MCP runtime (nodeForMcp), and dist/ashley-cli.js requires it (esbuild target node20, global fetch). Maintainers building need Node 22.
nodes.check: Laptop: `node --version` prints vNN with NN >= 20 for CLI users, NN >= 22 for maintainers. A missing node passes for extension-only users.
failure_signatures: 'node' is not recognized as an internal or external command
ReferenceError: fetch is not defined (Node < 18)
MCP registered with 'node' that later resolves to an older nvm version
nodes.auto_repair: Offer `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` or `brew install node` only with consent. Nothing is installed silently.
nodes.manual_fix: Install Node LTS from nodejs.org, or use the extension (it runs the MCP server on VS Code's own runtime).
nodes.future_risk: Node 20 reached end of life in April 2026 but nodeForMcp still accepts it. The MCP SDK or esbuild may raise their minimum Node.

nodes.title: CLI settings and secrets files readable (ashley-cli only)
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley-local/settings.json and secrets.json are valid JSON. secrets.json has mode 600, which Windows ignores (the file inherits the profile ACL). Malformed JSON silently falls back to the defaults (the catch in loadJson).
nodes.check: Laptop: `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(require('os').homedir()+'/.ashley-local/settings.json','utf8'))"` exits 0 (a missing file is acceptable). On POSIX, secrets.json has mode 600.
failure_signatures: the CLI suddenly behaves as if never set up (accessId '')
SyntaxError: Unexpected token ... in JSON (hidden by loadJson)
nodes.auto_repair: On POSIX: chmod 600 ~/.ashley-local/secrets.json.
nodes.manual_fix: Fix or delete the malformed file, then run `node dist/ashley-cli.js setup` again.
nodes.future_risk: None from vendors.

nodes.title: ashley-cli runs in an interactive TTY
nodes.assumption: ashley-cli prompts through readline and mutes password echo by overriding stdout.write, and interactive children use stdio 'inherit'. Both need a real TTY.
nodes.check: Laptop, in the shell the student uses: `node -e "process.exit(process.stdin.isTTY&&process.stdout.isTTY?0:1)"` exits 0.
failure_signatures: prompts hang when stdin is piped
the password is echoed in mintty (Git Bash) without winpty
nodes.manual_fix: Run the CLI from Windows Terminal, PowerShell or Terminal.app, or use `winpty node ...` in Git Bash.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to Node's readline.

nodes.title: cli/ashley.ps1 may run (execution policy)
nodes.assumption: For Windows users of cli/ashley.ps1: the PowerShell execution policy allows local scripts, and ssh plus the wsu-grid alias work.
nodes.check: Laptop, PowerShell: `Get-ExecutionPolicy` is not Restricted or AllSigned.
failure_signatures: ashley.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled on this system.
nodes.auto_repair: With the user's consent: `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned` (user scope, no admin rights needed).
nodes.manual_fix: Run the command above, or call `ssh wsu-grid ~/.ashley/bin/ashley <verb>` directly.
nodes.future_risk: WSU-managed laptops enforcing AllSigned by Group Policy.

nodes.title: VS Code version supported by Ashley and by the grid's glibc workaround
nodes.assumption: VS Code satisfies engines ^1.100.0. The APIs used include shell-integration execution events (1.93+), authentication.getSession, environmentVariableCollection.description and Terminal.exitStatus. Its Remote-SSH server must still honour the custom-glibc escape hatch the CentOS 7 nodes rely on: VS Code >= 1.99 needs glibc 2.28 unless VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER is set, with patchelf >= 0.18.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: vscode.version satisfies ^1.100.0. Compare it with the last version that connected to a node successfully, which Ashley records in globalState after each successful connect.
failure_signatures: Unable to install extension 'openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu' as it is not compatible with VS Code
The remote host may not meet VS Code Server's prerequisites for glibc and libstdc++
Exit code 207
found GLIBC 2.17
nodes.auto_repair: If a new VS Code breaks the node connection, set remote.SSH.useExecServer to false, the documented first troubleshooting step.
nodes.manual_fix: Update VS Code. If a new release breaks the grid, install the last working version from code.visualstudio.com/updates and turn off updates until the lead confirms.
nodes.future_risk: Microsoft removing the custom-glibc path, or requiring a patchelf newer than /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/0.19.1. VS Code ships monthly.

nodes.title: The VSIX is built from tested sources (maintainer gate)
nodes.assumption: `npm run package` (vsce package --no-dependencies --out ../dist/) produces ashley-wsu-<version>.vsix containing dist/ and media/ only. Students install it by hand, so there is no Marketplace auto-update.
nodes.check: Maintainer laptop, in extension/: `npx vsce ls --no-dependencies` lists dist/extension.js, dist/mcp-server.js, dist/ashley-cli.js, dist/grid/VERSION, media/allowlist.json and media/manual.html.
failure_signatures: ERROR  Make sure to edit the README.md file before you package or publish your extension.
a listed file is missing from `vsce ls`
nodes.auto_repair: Run `npm run build` and then `npm run package`.
nodes.manual_fix: Build with Node 22, following docs/INSTALL.md 'Building from source'.
nodes.future_risk: vsce major versions. Signature requirements for side-loaded VSIX files.

nodes.title: The installed extension contains every file it loads by path
nodes.assumption: <extensionPath> contains dist/extension.js, dist/mcp-server.js, dist/ashley-cli.js, dist/grid/* (the six grid files plus phone.js), media/allowlist.json, media/manual.html, media/ashley.svg and media/walkthrough/*.md. esbuild bundles every runtime dependency, so the VSIX carries no node_modules.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: fs.existsSync(path.join(context.extensionPath, p)) for each path above.
failure_signatures: no grid scripts found in <ext>/dist/grid
The manual is not bundled in this build
Cannot find module '<ext>/dist/mcp-server.js'
Cannot find module 'ssh2'
nodes.auto_repair: If the lab's VSIX is on disk: `code --install-extension <vsix> --force`.
nodes.manual_fix: Reinstall the VSIX from the lead (Extensions view > ... > Install from VSIX).
nodes.future_risk: vsce changing .vscodeignore semantics. A change in esbuild's output layout.

nodes.title: Ashley is enabled in the current window (workspace trust)
nodes.assumption: package.json declares no capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces. VS Code's documented default for such an extension is to disable it in Restricted Mode (not tested here). Claude Code also ignores a project .mcp.json in an untrusted folder.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: log vscode.workspace.isTrusted. When it is false, check that vscode.commands.getCommands(true) still includes 'ashley.setup'.
failure_signatures: command 'ashley.setup' not found (only in some windows)
the Extensions view shows Ashley disabled in Restricted Mode
nodes.auto_repair: Code fix: declare "capabilities": {"untrustedWorkspaces": {"supported": true}}, since Ashley reads no workspace files. No runtime repair.
nodes.manual_fix: Trust the folder (Manage Workspace Trust), or run Ashley from an empty window.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code tightening Restricted Mode.

nodes.title: Ashley installed, enabled and activated
nodes.assumption: openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu is installed from the VSIX, enabled, and activated on onStartupFinished. activate() awaits no dialog and registers all 18 commands, including ashley.phone.
nodes.check: Laptop: `code --list-extensions --show-versions` contains openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu@<version>. The Output channel 'Ashley' has the line 'Ashley <version> active (build <ISO date>)'. getCommands(true) includes every command in package.json, as in the integration test.
failure_signatures: command 'ashley.setup' not found
Activating extension 'openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu' failed:
no Ashley icon in the activity bar
nodes.auto_repair: If the VSIX is on disk: `code --install-extension <vsix> --force`.
nodes.manual_fix: Extensions view > ... > Install from VSIX, then Developer: Reload Window.
nodes.future_risk: An org policy 'extensions.allowed' (VS Code 1.96+) blocking unlisted publishers. Stricter checks on unsigned side-loaded VSIX files.

nodes.title: Ashley runs on the laptop even in Remote-SSH windows
nodes.assumption: "extensionKind": ["ui"] keeps Ashley in the laptop's extension host. Without it VS Code would deduce ['workspace'] and install Ashley on the node, where SecretStorage, ~/.ssh and the laptop's ssh are missing. The user must not override this in remote.extensionKind.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host in a Remote-SSH window: vscode.extensions.getExtension('openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu').extensionKind === vscode.ExtensionKind.UI, and remote.extensionKind has no entry for it.
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname wsu-grid (Ashley running on the node)
tokens missing only in the remote window
nodes.auto_repair: After confirmation, remove the ashley entry from the user setting remote.extensionKind.
nodes.manual_fix: Delete the override from settings.json and reload the window.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to VS Code's extension-kind rules.

nodes.title: Grid scripts in the VSIX: complete, LF endings, versioned
nodes.assumption: dist/grid holds ashley, ashleyd.js, phone.js, bootstrap.sbatch, worker.sbatch.tpl, bashrc.block and VERSION. esbuild.mjs rewrites CRLF to LF, and .gitattributes sets eol=lf. VERSION equals the grid/VERSION the build came from (2 today). The build copies ../grid only when that folder exists, so a partial checkout silently ships no scripts.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: every file in <extensionPath>/dist/grid is present, none contains '\r' (fs.readFileSync(f,'latin1').includes('\r') is false), and VERSION is non-empty.
failure_signatures: no grid scripts found in <ext>/dist/grid
/usr/bin/env: 'bash\r': No such file or directory (on the grid)
$'\r': command not found
the grid has Ashley v1.0.0; this extension brings v2
nodes.manual_fix: Reinstall a correctly built VSIX. The lead rebuilds from a full checkout.
nodes.future_risk: A lead editing grid scripts on Windows reintroduces CRLF before a build that bypasses esbuild.mjs.

nodes.title: Bundled ssh2, MCP SDK and zod work in VS Code's runtime
nodes.assumption: ssh2 1.17.0, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.1 and zod 4.6.5 are pinned and bundled. ssh2's native pieces (sshcrypto.node, cpu-features) are externalised and absent, so ssh2 falls back to pure JS on the extension host's Electron crypto (BoringSSL), whose cipher and KEX set differs from Node's OpenSSL. The ssh2 handshake to warrior was proved with plain Node 22 (ashley-cli ssh2-probe), not inside VS Code's extension host.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host (Troubleshoot): probeWithKey(loginHost, accessId, <private key>) returns ok with the login node's hostname. Log crypto.getCiphers() (expect aes128-ctr) and crypto.getCurves().
failure_signatures: Handshake failed: no matching cipher
Handshake failed: no matching key exchange algorithm
Timed out while waiting for handshake
In-panel login did not work (...); falling back to a terminal.
nodes.auto_repair: The terminal login path is used automatically when the failure is not an authentication failure.
nodes.manual_fix: Use the terminal login the wizard opens. Report the log to the lead.
nodes.future_risk: Electron or BoringSSL dropping algorithms. ssh2 has a single maintainer. MCP SDK or zod breaking changes on the next rebuild (pinned until then).

nodes.title: ashley.* settings valid and writable
nodes.assumption: Settings are valid: accessId matches ^[a-z]{2}[0-9]{4}$, loginHost and nodeDomain resolve, sshAlias is one token, identityFile uses tilde form, and worker.qos is in its enum. Ashley writes them to the Global target, which must not be policy-locked. No workspace-level value overrides sshAlias or loginHost. Settings Sync may carry accessId and twoFactorDone to a new laptop that has no key.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: validate each value, and check that getConfiguration('ashley').inspect(k).workspaceValue is undefined for accessId, sshAlias, loginHost and nodeDomain.
failure_signatures: An AccessID looks like ab1234 (two letters, four digits).
ssh: Could not resolve hostname <alias>
a workspace setting silently overrides ashley.sshAlias
nodes.auto_repair: Normalise accessId with normaliseAccessId and rewrite it. Remove workspace overrides after confirmation.
nodes.manual_fix: Open Settings, search 'ashley', and correct the value.
nodes.future_risk: WSU renaming hosts, in which case the defaults need a new VSIX.

nodes.title: VS Code SecretStorage round-trips
nodes.assumption: context.secrets stores the four tokens on the laptop, unsynced, under ashley.github, ashley.huggingface, ashley.claudeOauth and ashley.anthropicApiKey.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: store('ashley.__probe', nonce), get() returns the nonce, then delete. Passes within 5 s.
failure_signatures: tokens show 'missing' in the Ashley view after a restart
secrets.store rejected
nodes.manual_fix: Fix laptop.os-keyring, then re-enter the tokens with 'Ashley: Manage stored tokens' > Replace.
nodes.future_risk: SecretStorage API changes. A new laptop has no secrets because Settings Sync does not carry them.

nodes.title: Terminal environment injection works (and where it persists)
nodes.assumption: The persistent environmentVariableCollection sets WSU_ACCESS_ID, ASHLEY_GRID and ASHLEY_GRID_HOME in every new integrated terminal, local and Remote-SSH. When ashley.injectTokensIntoTerminals is on it also sets GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and HF_TOKEN. It never sets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Unverified side effect: VS Code keeps persistent collections in its storage database (state.vscdb), so these token values may also sit on disk outside the OS keychain.
nodes.check: Laptop, in a new integrated terminal: ASHLEY_GRID equals the alias, and sha256(GITHUB_TOKEN) equals the hash of the SecretStorage value (never print it). Storage question: count rows in %APPDATA%/Code/User/**/state.vscdb whose value contains 'hf_' (names and counts only).
failure_signatures: variables missing in terminals opened before setup (warning icon on the terminal tab)
gh: HTTP 401: Bad credentials (a stale GITHUB_TOKEN injected)
token prefix found in state.vscdb
nodes.auto_repair: Call store.hydrateEnvironment(), which clears and re-applies the collection, then run workbench.action.terminal.relaunch on open terminals.
nodes.manual_fix: Close and reopen the terminal. If tokens must not persist on disk, turn off ashley.injectTokensIntoTerminals.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code changing how collections persist, or the terminal.integrated.environmentChangesRelaunch default.

nodes.title: Failures reach the Ashley log with enough context
nodes.assumption: Every failure lands in the Output channel 'Ashley'. reg() catches command errors, logs 'ERROR <command>: <msg>' and shows a notification with a 'Show log' button. The panel keeps a timestamped log and a 'Show the full log' button. Known gaps: some paths swallow errors (tree access lookup, allowlist fetch, clipboard, .mcp.json parse), GridApi logs the command but not ssh's stderr, and run() records exit codes nowhere.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: run ssh against the alias 'ashley-probe-nonexistent' through the same code path, and assert the channel gains a line with the node id and ssh's stderr.
failure_signatures: 'Cannot reach the grid' with only the first stderr line
an empty tree section with no log line
a notification without 'Show log'
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Check everything' and send the full Ashley log to the lead.
nodes.future_risk: None from vendors. It degrades whenever a new feature adds a silent catch, which is the pre-integration rule's job to stop.

nodes.title: The setup panel webview loads
nodes.assumption: The setup panel loads with enableScripts, a nonce CSP and retainContextWhenHidden, and exchanges postMessage with the extension. VS Code's webview service worker must register.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: open the panel, post {type:'steps'}, and receive any message back within 5 s (needs a 'ready' ping added to the page script).
failure_signatures: Error loading webview: Error: Could not register service workers: InvalidStateError: Failed to register a ServiceWorker: The document is in an invalid state.
blank Ashley setup panel
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to VsCodeUI (native input boxes) when the panel does not answer.
nodes.manual_fix: Close every VS Code window. Delete the 'Service Worker' folder under %APPDATA%\Code (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Code; Linux: ~/.config/Code), then restart VS Code.
nodes.future_risk: Webview CSP or sandbox changes. GPU driver issues (try --disable-gpu).

nodes.title: The Ashley view builds
nodes.assumption: The 'ashley.status' view builds from testConnection (BatchMode ssh), `ashley status --json`, `ashley access whoami --json` and secretSummary. Each refresh opens a fresh ssh per call, about 2.6 s each.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: tree.getChildren() resolves within 150 s, and its first item has the 'pass' icon.
failure_signatures: Cannot reach the grid
Ashley not installed on the grid
'Loading...' for minutes (status waits up to 90 s)
Grid installing (spinner never ends after approval)
nodes.auto_repair: Refresh once the failing dependency has been repaired.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Check everything'.
nodes.future_risk: Each new feature adds ssh round trips per refresh. Rate limits on the login node.

nodes.title: Terminals can run ssh/claude directly and report exit codes
nodes.assumption: createTerminal({shellPath, shellArgs}) runs ssh or claude as the terminal's own process, with no shell. Terminal.exitStatus reports the code; Ashley polls it every 500 ms with a 15-minute deadline.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: createTerminal({shellPath: resolveExecutable('ssh'), shellArgs: ['-V'], isTransient: true, hideFromUser: true}) reaches exitStatus.code === 0 within 10 s.
failure_signatures: The terminal process failed to launch: Path to shell executable "ssh.exe" does not exist.
runInteractive resolves null after 15 minutes
nodes.auto_repair: Use the absolute path from resolveExecutable (already done for terminals).
nodes.manual_fix: Fix laptop.openssh-on-path.
nodes.future_risk: Terminal API changes.

nodes.title: Shell integration lets Ashley read the setup-token output
nodes.assumption: Several things must hold. The default terminal profile activates shell integration within 6 s: PowerShell, pwsh, bash, zsh or fish (not cmd.exe), with terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled on. executeCommand(executable, args) quotes a path with spaces correctly for that shell. The printed token arrives unbroken: if the CLI wraps the long token in the narrow hidden terminal, only the first fragment matches /sk-ant-oat[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/ and a truncated token is stored. The flow is untested with a real Authorize click.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: in a hidden terminal, onDidChangeTerminalShellIntegration fires within 6 s. Then executeCommand(<claude path>, ['--version']) and read() yields output matching /[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/.
failure_signatures: This terminal has no shell integration; the token will be picked up from your clipboard instead.
the service rejected it (HTTP 401) right after 'Token captured from the terminal.'
PowerShell echoes the quoted path instead of running it
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to the clipboard/paste path (automatic). Code fix: create the hidden terminal with an explicit shellPath for PowerShell or bash so integration does not depend on the user's profile.
nodes.manual_fix: Copy the token the terminal prints; the panel picks it up from the clipboard.
nodes.future_risk: Shell-integration scripts change with VS Code releases. Claude Code could change setup-token's output (a new prefix such as sk-ant-oat02, wrapping, Ink UI).

nodes.title: Wayne State sign-in through VS Code's Microsoft provider
nodes.assumption: The built-in 'microsoft' provider returns a session for a work or school account with scopes ['VSCODE_TENANT:organizations','User.Read']. WSU's Entra tenant lets users consent to VS Code's client for User.Read. session.account.label is the UPN, AccessID@wayne.edu.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: getSession('microsoft', ['VSCODE_TENANT:organizations','User.Read'], {silent: true}) returns undefined (not signed in yet, not a failure) or a session whose label matches /@([a-z0-9-]+\.)*wayne\.edu$/i.
failure_signatures: No authentication provider 'microsoft' is currently registered.
AADSTS65001
AADSTS90094
AADSTS53003
<email> is not a Wayne State account; sign in with AccessID@wayne.edu
the Wayne State sign-in did not complete (...)
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to typing the AccessID; the step already asks when the email yields none. Make that fallback automatic on provider errors.
nodes.manual_fix: Sign in with AccessID@wayne.edu. If Microsoft says admin approval is needed, the lead asks C&IT to allow Visual Studio Code for User.Read.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code's MSAL migration (microsoft-authentication.implementation). The VSCODE_TENANT: scope convention changing. WSU Conditional Access or admin-consent policy.

nodes.title: GitHub sign-in through VS Code's GitHub provider
nodes.assumption: The built-in 'github' provider grants a session with scopes repo, workflow, read:org and gist in the browser. The OAuth token (gho_) is stored as the student's GitHub token without a pattern check. It belongs to VS Code's OAuth app: signing out of GitHub in VS Code can revoke it, and orgs with SAML SSO must authorise the app.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: getSession('github', GITHUB_SCOPES, {silent: true}) returns a session whose scopes include repo, workflow, read:org and gist. Then run account.github-token's check with it.
failure_signatures: User did not consent to login.
GitHub sign-in did not complete (...); you can paste a token instead.
Resource protected by organization SAML enforcement
no longer accepted (the service rejected it (HTTP 401)): press Renew
nodes.auto_repair: Rerun the github step, which asks for the session again. Pasting a token remains the fallback.
nodes.manual_fix: Press Renew next to GitHub in the panel. For SSO orgs, authorise 'Visual Studio Code' under GitHub Settings > Applications.
nodes.future_risk: GitHub OAuth scope changes. VS Code GitHub auth moving to fine-grained or device-flow tokens.

nodes.title: fetch from the extension host reaches vendor APIs
nodes.assumption: The extension host's global fetch (Electron's Node, patched by VS Code to honour http.proxy and system certificates) reaches the token-check, OnDemand and allowlist URLs. ashley-cli's plain-Node fetch uses neither VS Code's proxy settings nor the OS certificate store.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: fetch('https://api.github.com/zen') with a 15 s abort returns 200. For CLI users, run the same fetch with `node -e` and compare.
failure_signatures: this laptop's network refused the check (fetch failed)
unable to get local issuer certificate
self signed certificate in certificate chain
This operation was aborted
nodes.auto_repair: The token is kept and verified on the grid instead (existing behaviour).
nodes.manual_fix: Set http.proxy in VS Code. For the CLI behind TLS inspection, set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code proxy-agent changes (http.fetchAdditionalSupport). WSU TLS inspection.

nodes.title: Remote - SSH extension installed
nodes.assumption: ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh is installed and enabled. 'Open my grid files' needs it, and it is a lab-access requirement.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: vscode.extensions.getExtension('ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh') is defined; log its packageJSON.version.
failure_signatures: FAIL  Remote-SSH extension not installed (Ashley: Open my grid files needs it)
Still missing: the Remote-SSH extension
nodes.auto_repair: executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', 'ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh'), with consent (already offered).
nodes.manual_fix: Install 'Remote - SSH' from the Extensions view.
nodes.future_risk: Microsoft renaming or restructuring Remote-SSH. Forks using Open VSX, which does not carry it.

nodes.title: Remote-SSH settings agree with Ashley's ssh setup
nodes.assumption: Remote-SSH reads the same ~/.ssh/config (remote.SSH.configFile unset or equal) and uses the same ssh (remote.SSH.path unset or valid). remote.SSH.remotePlatform['<node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu'] is 'linux'. remote.SSH.connectTimeout is >= 300: the node's sshd takes about 25 s and the first connection downloads the server. The default exec-server and local-server modes must work with the sysroot.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: read getConfiguration('remote.SSH') and log configFile, path, connectTimeout (pass >= 300), the remotePlatform entry for the worker's node, useExecServer and useLocalServer.
failure_signatures: Could not establish connection to "asx1.nas.grid.wayne.edu": Connecting with SSH timed out
Select the platform of the remote host
ssh: Could not resolve hostname (Remote-SSH reading another configFile)
nodes.auto_repair: Write connectTimeout 300 and the remotePlatform entry (commandConnect already does). If configFile points elsewhere, offer to add the managed block there too. After repeated server-start failures, set remote.SSH.useExecServer to false.
nodes.manual_fix: Settings > Remote.SSH: set Connect Timeout to 300 and clear Config File.
nodes.future_risk: Remote-SSH renaming or removing settings and commands (Remote-SSH 0.92 removed opensshremotesexplorer commands). The exec server becoming mandatory.

nodes.title: Open my grid files: a VS Code window on a compute node
nodes.assumption: vscode.openFolder with vscode-remote://ssh-remote+<node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu<path> opens a window on a node where the student has a RUNNING job, found with `ashley worker node` or squeue. The node name is a single host, not a Slurm range such as voh[3-4]. The VS Code Server installs in the grid home and starts through the C&IT sysroot that the ~/.bashrc block exports.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=60 <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu hostname` prints the node within 120 s. After a connect, the newest '*Remote - SSH.log' under the VS Code logs folder contains 'Extension host agent started'.
failure_signatures: Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node
Connecting with SSH timed out
The VS Code Server failed to start
Exit code 207
remote host voh[3-4].nas.grid.wayne.edu
nodes.auto_repair: If no job runs, start a worker (commandWorkerStart with the saved spec, after confirmation). For a stale server, ssh to that node and run `pkill -u $USER -f vscode-server` (the student's own processes only), then reconnect.
nodes.manual_fix: Start a worker first. If a second window hangs, run 'Remote-SSH: Kill VS Code Server on Host...' and reconnect.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT changing the pam_slurm_adopt policy or the node domain, or removing /wsu/apps/vscode/sysroot after the OS migration. VS Code Server raising its glibc floor again.

nodes.title: Claude Code extension installed and signed in
nodes.assumption: anthropic.claude-code is installed and signed in with Claude Pro or Max. Its folder contains resources/native-binary/claude (claude.exe on Windows), which Ashley uses for setup-token and the mcp commands. That is a vendor-internal layout.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: getExtension('anthropic.claude-code') is defined and fs.existsSync(<extPath>/resources/native-binary/claude[.exe]) is true.
failure_signatures: WARN  Claude Code extension not installed
Still missing: the Claude Code extension (signed in to Claude Pro or Max)
nodes.auto_repair: With consent: executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', 'anthropic.claude-code').
nodes.manual_fix: Install Claude Code from the Extensions view and sign in with the Pro/Max account.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic moving or renaming the bundled binary, or changing the extension id.

nodes.title: A claude executable that spawn() can run
nodes.assumption: findClaudeExecutable() returns something spawn() can run without a shell: the bundled native binary, or else a real 'claude' executable on PATH. npm installs a claude.cmd shim, and Node will not spawn .cmd without shell:true: ENOENT through the PATH lookup, EINVAL for an explicit .cmd since the 2024 fix.
nodes.check: Laptop, extension host: run(findClaudeExecutable(), ['--version'], {timeoutMs: 30000}) exits 0 and prints /[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ \(Claude Code\)/.
failure_signatures: spawn claude ENOENT
spawn EINVAL
claude mcp add-json failed (...) and no workspace folder is open for a .mcp.json fallback
nodes.auto_repair: Prefer the bundled binary. On Windows, also try %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe (the native installer's location) when PATH has only a .cmd shim.
nodes.manual_fix: Install or update the Claude Code extension, or install Claude Code with the native installer.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code distribution changes. Node tightening spawn rules further.

nodes.title: claude setup-token mints a subscription token
nodes.assumption: `claude setup-token` needs a TTY; it printed nothing when piped (probed). It opens claude.ai, and after the account holder presses Authorize it prints a one-year token matching /sk-ant-oat[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/. Only Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise accounts get one.
nodes.check: Laptop: `<claude> setup-token --help` exits 0 (cheap, no login). The full flow runs only when the student asks. Afterwards, run external.anthropic-oauth-probe with the captured token.
failure_signatures: runCapturing returns no match after 15 min
the service rejected it (HTTP 401)
OAuth access token is invalid
the browser page shows a code to paste into a terminal
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to the clipboard or paste field (automatic).
nodes.manual_fix: Run `claude setup-token` in any terminal and paste the token into 'Ashley: Store or replace my Claude token for the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: A change to setup-token's output or prefix would stop the pattern matching. Token lifetime policy. Anthropic restricting subscription tokens for unattended use.

nodes.title: The MCP server's runtime (node or Electron-as-node) works
nodes.assumption: The registered command runs dist/mcp-server.js. It is either a system `node` >= 20 on the PATH Claude Code sees, or VS Code's own binary (process.execPath) with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1. The second needs Electron's RunAsNode fuse to stay enabled and the binary path to stay stable.
nodes.check: Laptop: spawn the registered command with the registered env and args ['-e', 'process.stdout.write(process.versions.node)']. It prints a Node version >= 20 within 10 s and opens no VS Code window.
failure_signatures: MCP server ashley: Connection closed
a VS Code window opens instead of the server (RunAsNode fuse disabled)
spawn node ENOENT
command path under /snap/code/<old revision>/ or .../AppTranslocation/... no longer exists
nodes.auto_repair: Run registerMcp() again: it recomputes nodeForMcp and the path.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Connect the Claude Code extension to the grid (MCP)'.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code/Electron disabling the RunAsNode fuse for hardening. Changes in the macOS helper-app layout of process.execPath.

nodes.title: The registered MCP server path is the current extension's
nodes.assumption: The registered args[0] equals <current extensionPath>/dist/mcp-server.js. That path contains the extension version (openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu-<version>), so a VSIX with a new version moves it. isMcpRegistered only checks that an 'ashley' entry exists.
nodes.check: Laptop: read mcpServers.ashley.args[0] from ~/.claude.json (or the output of `claude mcp get ashley`). It equals path.join(context.extensionPath,'dist','mcp-server.js') and the file exists.
failure_signatures: Error: Cannot find module 'C:\\Users\\<user>\\.vscode\\extensions\\openspineconsortium.ashley-wsu-1.0.0\\dist\\mcp-server.js'
Claude Code lists ashley as failed
nodes.auto_repair: On activation, if the paths differ: `claude mcp remove --scope user ashley`, then registerMcp().
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Connect the Claude Code extension to the grid (MCP)'.
nodes.future_risk: Every Ashley version bump. package.json is still 1.0.0 while grid VERSION is 2, so the first bump will trigger this.

nodes.title: Claude Code has the ashley MCP server (user scope)
nodes.assumption: `claude mcp add-json --scope user ashley <json>` writes the server to the user's Claude config: ~/.claude.json, or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR if the student set one. The Claude Code extension and CLI both read that config. `claude mcp get ashley` exits 0. Re-adding an existing name may be refused (not verified); registerMcp would then write .mcp.json in the first workspace folder instead.
nodes.check: Laptop: `<claude> mcp get ashley` exits 0 and its output contains 'Connected'. The wording ('Status: ✓ Connected' today) is not a stable contract.
failure_signatures: TODO  MCP bridge registered with Claude Code
Failed to connect
Could not register the MCP bridge: ...
the ashley_* tools are missing in a new Claude Code conversation
nodes.auto_repair: `<claude> mcp remove --scope user ashley`, then registerMcp(). Neither touches other servers.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Connect the Claude Code extension to the grid (MCP)'. Do not type the JSON by hand in PowerShell: it mangles quotes.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to `claude mcp` syntax or output. Claude Code moving the user MCP config. Enterprise managed-MCP allowlists.

nodes.title: Project .mcp.json fallback is sound
nodes.assumption: When the CLI registration fails and a folder is open, registerMcp adds mcpServers.ashley to .mcp.json in the first workspace folder, and Claude Code asks once to approve project servers. An existing .mcp.json that fails to parse is silently replaced by {} plus ashley, so its other servers are lost.
nodes.check: Laptop: if <workspace>/.mcp.json exists, JSON.parse succeeds and the file at mcpServers.ashley.args[0] exists.
failure_signatures: the ashley tools work in one folder only
an 'Approve MCP server' prompt
other project MCP servers disappeared
nodes.auto_repair: Repair vscode.mcp-registration at user scope, then remove the project entry after confirmation.
nodes.manual_fix: Restore .mcp.json from git and register at user scope.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to Claude Code's project-MCP approval model.

nodes.title: The ashley MCP server answers over stdio
nodes.assumption: dist/mcp-server.js starts a stdio MCP server with 11 ashley_* tools. It writes only JSON-RPC to stdout; relay and GridApi logs go to stderr. It reaches the grid through ssh with ASHLEY_GRID (default wsu-grid), using the PATH and env Claude Code gives it.
nodes.check: Laptop: pipe an MCP initialize and tools/list into '<command> <args>' with the registered env. A reply listing ashley_status ... ashley_sbatch arrives within 10 s. Then call ashley_status, which returns JSON containing "ready".
failure_signatures: ashley mcp server failed: ...
MCP server ashley: Connection closed
Ashley is not installed on the grid yet (tool result)
nodes.auto_repair: Re-register (vscode.mcp-registration); the relay reconnects by itself.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the doctor, then start a new Claude Code conversation.
nodes.future_risk: MCP protocol revisions (SDK pinned at 1.30.1). Claude Code MCP start-up timeouts (MCP_TIMEOUT, 30 s).

nodes.title: The persistent relay to the login node
nodes.assumption: Each process (extension, MCP server, CLI) keeps one `ssh <alias> -- ~/.ashley/bin/ashley relay`. It answers 'READY <ms> <version>' and speaks SEND/QUEUED, RESULT, PING/PONG and EVENT lines. A dropped session reconnects on the next call, and every call falls back to a fresh ssh. The relay is a long-lived loop on the login node.
nodes.check: Laptop: relay.ping() returns rttMs < 2000 and the READY version equals dist/grid/VERSION. CLI: `node dist/ashley-cli.js latency 1`.
failure_signatures: relay closed (ssh exit 255)
no QUEUED ack from the relay within 30 s
relay is not connected
relay send failed (...); using a fresh ssh
nodes.auto_repair: relay.close() then ensure(). Safe: the file on the grid is the message, so nothing already queued is lost.
nodes.manual_fix: None needed; slow answers mean the fallback ssh path is in use. Send the log if it persists.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT killing long-lived login-node processes (a process reaper or cgroup limits), idle-session timeouts (ClientAliveInterval, TMOUT), or sshd MaxSessions.

nodes.title: Remote command quoting in ssh() (tilde and $USER defects)
nodes.assumption: ssh() renders the argv as one remote command with POSIX single quotes, leaving only a leading '~/' of the FIRST argument unquoted, and the login shell is bash. Three consequences are traced in code and reproduced by emulating the renderer. (1) stepGridInstall.run sends `'mkdir' '-p' '~/.ashley/bin' ...`, which creates a directory literally named '~' in the grid home, so on a fresh account the following scp has no ~/.ashley/bin to copy into. (2) GridApi.squeue sends `'squeue' '-u' '$USER'`, so squeue gets the literal string and squeue() returns []. Connect's fallback, 'Grid status' and ashley_squeue use it. (3) readFile and listDir do not expand '~/...' paths. Strings passed through `bash -c` (pushTokens, sbatch) are expanded, but sbatch splices cwd into that string unquoted. None of this was observed on a fresh account, because Greg's account already had ~/.ashley/bin.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'test -d "$HOME/~" && echo LITERAL_TILDE_DIR'` prints nothing. Unit test: ssh() renders ['mkdir','-p','~/x'] with '~/' unquoted and ['squeue','-u','$USER'] with $USER expanded.
failure_signatures: upload failed: scp: ...: No such file or directory (first install on a fresh account)
squeue: error: Invalid user: $USER
head: cannot open '~/...' for reading: No such file or directory
a directory named '~' in the grid home
nodes.auto_repair: Runtime: before scp, run `ssh wsu-grid 'mkdir -p ~/.ashley/bin ~/.ashley/log ~/.ashley/accounts/default ~/.ashley/workers ~/.ashley/sessions'`. Show the student the contents of "$HOME/~" and remove it only with `rmdir` or `rm -r -- "$HOME/~"`, never `rm -rf ~`. Code fix: render '~/rest' as "$HOME"/'rest' for every argument, and send $USER as "$USER" (or use `id -un`) through bash -c.
nodes.manual_fix: Tell the lead. Never type `rm -rf ~` to clean up the '~' directory: that deletes the whole home.
nodes.future_risk: WSU changing the default login shell (tcsh, zsh) would change quoting and expansion again.

nodes.assumption: validateToken reads HTTP 401/403 as 'rejected', so the student is told to renew. Any other failure counts as 'network': the token is kept and verified on the grid. The daily check (20 s after start, at most once per 24 h) only warns on rejections. This works only while every vendor endpoint keeps those status meanings.

nodes.title: In-panel password + code login installs the key
nodes.assumption: installPublicKey connects to loginHost:22 with ssh2 using keyboard-interactive. Prompts are routed by /pass/i (the password) and /verification|code|token/i (the Authenticator code). HMACs are sha2-256, sha2-512 and sha1, with a 120 s timeout and three attempts. It appends the key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys under umask 077. Nothing is stored, and the host key is not verified (see laptop.ssh-known-hosts-login).

nodes.title: Ask the grid Claude (streamed answer)
nodes.assumption: commandAsk picks a RUNNING worker and sends the request over the relay, falling back to a fresh ssh. EVENT lines stream into an output channel until the RESULT line or 3600 s.

nodes.title: Phone access: Remote Control hosted by a worker
nodes.assumption: commandPhone runs `ashley phone on --worker <w>` and polls `ashley phone status --json` every 2.5 s for phase need_code, running or error. It opens the claude.ai URL the worker reports, captures the code the student copies (/^[A-Za-z0-9_\-#.~]{20,}$/), and sends it with `ashley phone code` over stdin. The worker must already be RUNNING.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley phone status --worker default --json'` exits 0 with JSON containing a phase.

Phone access did not start: <message>

nodes.title: Laptop reaches the login node's sshd
nodes.assumption: The laptop resolves warrior.grid.wayne.edu and reaches TCP 22 from where the student is, on campus or off. SSH to the login node is not VPN-gated today; OnDemand is. sshd answers with its banner and key exchange.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 wsu-grid true` ends in 'Permission denied (...)' within 25 s. That proves DNS, TCP, banner and key exchange without using credentials. Windows alternative: `Test-NetConnection warrior.grid.wayne.edu -Port 22` gives TcpTestSucceeded True.
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname warrior.grid.wayne.edu: No such host is known.
ssh: connect to host warrior.grid.wayne.edu port 22: Connection timed out
Connection refused
kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset
nodes.manual_fix: Check the network. Off campus, connect GlobalProtect and retry; if that works, WSU is blocking off-campus SSH. Contact hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT restricting SSH to campus or the VPN, renaming or replacing the login node during the CentOS 7 retirement, or adding a bastion host.

nodes.title: IPv4 path used (IPv6 attempt avoided)
nodes.assumption: The IPv4 route to the login node works. From Windows the IPv6 attempt times out first: 13.1 s per connection versus 2.0 s with IPv4, measured over nine runs each. Ashley therefore passes AddressFamily inet in the block, in SSH_BATCH_OPTS and to terminals.
nodes.check: Laptop: time three `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` runs; the median is < 5 s.
failure_signatures: every ssh call takes about 13 s
the tree view loads slowly
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the managed block (AddressFamily inet).
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard step 'SSH configuration' again.
nodes.future_risk: An IPv6-only network without CLAT (some hotspots) would fail with AddressFamily inet. WSU fixing IPv6 on the login node would make the option unnecessary.

nodes.title: Laptop ssh/ssh2 and the grid's sshd agree on algorithms
nodes.assumption: The laptop's ssh and ssh2 share KEX, cipher, MAC and host-key algorithms with the grid's sshd (OpenSSH 7.4). From Windows OpenSSH 9.5 the grid negotiated only once 'MACs +hmac-sha1' was added ('no matching MAC found' observed). The research found that a stock 7.4 offers hmac-sha2, so the grid's list is probably restricted by C&IT. Which MACs it offers today is not recorded.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -vv -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true 2>&1` exits 0. Record the 'kex: algorithm:' line and the 'kex: server->client cipher: ... MAC: ...' line in the report.
failure_signatures: Unable to negotiate with <ip> port 22: no matching MAC found. Their offer: hmac-sha1
no matching key exchange method found
no matching host key type found. Their offer: ssh-rsa
nodes.auto_repair: Add the offered algorithm with '+' in the managed block, but only if it is on an allowlist (hmac-sha1, diffie-hellman-group14-sha1). Never add ssh-dss.
nodes.manual_fix: Send the -vv output to the lead.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT upgrading sshd or tightening crypto policy. Windows OpenSSH dropping hmac-sha1. Electron BoringSSL (ssh2) and the grid drifting apart.

nodes.title: Windows TCP connections to the grid are reliable
nodes.assumption: Connections from a Windows laptop to the grid succeed consistently. On this project's own Windows machine, sockets have been seen to fail intermittently for git push and ssh, and the standing practice there is to route network work through WSL. The cause is unknown. Ashley deliberately does not use WSL.
nodes.check: Laptop (Windows): run `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` three times; pass if all three exit 0, and record stderr for each run.
failure_signatures: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset
Connection timed out during banner exchange
client_loop: send disconnect: Connection reset
nodes.auto_repair: Retry with backoff. ssh calls are idempotent, and send is idempotent by request id.
nodes.manual_fix: Record the times of failure and compare with `wsl -e ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` to separate the Windows stack from the network.
nodes.future_risk: Updates to the Windows network stack, the VPN client or antivirus.

nodes.title: The login node tolerates Ashley's connection pattern
nodes.assumption: sshd accepts Ashley's pattern without hitting MaxStartups or MaxSessions, a per-source rate limit or fail2ban-style blocking. The pattern is a fresh ssh per call (3–5 per tree refresh, plus the daily token check and the doctor), one long-lived relay per process, and Remote-SSH's own sessions. Failed authentications count against the student (hence IdentitiesOnly).
nodes.check: Laptop: five sequential `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` within 30 s all exit 0.
failure_signatures: kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
Connection timed out (after a burst)
Received disconnect from <ip> port 22:2: Too many authentication failures
nodes.auto_repair: Back off. Code fix: route status calls over the relay.
nodes.manual_fix: Wait a few minutes. If it persists, send the log to the lead.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT adding connection throttling, or an OpenSSH >= 9.8 sshd with PerSourcePenalties.

nodes.title: ProxyJump through the login node reaches a compute node
nodes.assumption: The login node allows stdio/TCP forwarding (direct-tcpip) and resolves <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu. The node's sshd admits the student only while a job of theirs runs there (pam_slurm_adopt). It takes about 23–25 s before running anything.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=60 <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu hostname`, with the node from `ssh wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley worker node --name default'`, prints the node within 120 s.
failure_signatures: channel 0: open failed: administratively prohibited: open failed
stdio forwarding failed
Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node
ssh: Could not resolve hostname voh3.nas.grid.wayne.edu (resolved on the login node)
nodes.auto_repair: If no job runs, start a worker. Raise remote.SSH.connectTimeout to 300 (already done).
nodes.manual_fix: Start a worker, wait until it is RUNNING, then connect.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT disabling AllowTcpForwarding on login nodes, changing the node domain, or changing the pam_slurm_adopt policy.

nodes.assumption: ondemand.grid.wayne.edu answers only from the campus network or the WSU VPN (GlobalProtect), so any HTTP answer means the laptop is on campus or the VPN. It is needed once, for the Authenticator enrolment (the 2FA Setup app).

nodes.title: AccessID pre-approved by the lab
nodes.assumption: The AccessID is on the lab's pre-approved list. The list is either media/allowlist.json in the VSIX (edited with tools/allow.py and a rebuild) or the JSON at ashley.allowlistUrl. If the URL fails, Ashley silently falls back to the bundled list. A null list means no restriction.

failure_signatures: <id> is not on the lab's pre-approved list; ask your lead to add you
nodes.auto_repair: Re-fetch when ashley.allowlistUrl is set (existing).
nodes.manual_fix: The lead runs `python tools/allow.py add ab1234`, rebuilds and redistributes the VSIX, or publishes the list at the URL.
nodes.future_risk: Every new student needs a rebuild unless the URL is used.

nodes.title: A Wayne State grid account exists
nodes.assumption: A grid account exists for the AccessID. The student applies with a sponsor, and approval takes about two business days.
nodes.check: Laptop, indirect: the in-panel login is not refused on every attempt. After the key is installed, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid id -un` succeeds.
failure_signatures: the grid rejected the password or the code (all three attempts)
Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive).
nodes.manual_fix: Request an account at tech.wayne.edu/kb/high-performance-computing, naming the lead as sponsor (hpc@wayne.edu, 313-577-4743).
nodes.future_risk: C&IT changing the request process or its URL.

nodes.title: WSU password valid, not expired, not locked
nodes.assumption: The password is valid, not expired, and the account is not locked. With key authentication, an expired password still blocks non-interactive logins through PAM.
nodes.check: Laptop, after the key is installed: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` exits 0 and stderr does not mention an expired password.
failure_signatures: WARNING: Your password has expired.
Password change required but no TTY available.
You are required to change your password immediately
Account locked
nodes.manual_fix: Change the password through WSU's account self-service, or wait out a lockout, then retry.
nodes.future_risk: WSU password-policy changes.

nodes.title: Google Authenticator enrolled for the grid
nodes.assumption: Google Authenticator is enrolled through OnDemand > Interactive Apps > 2FA Setup. The six-digit TOTP, from a phone with the correct time, is accepted at the verification-code prompt of password logins.
nodes.check: Human only. Ashley records ashley.twoFactorDone, and a successful installKey proves it.
failure_signatures: the grid rejected the password or the code
three rejected logins: check the account exists and redo the Authenticator setup
nodes.manual_fix: Redo 2FA Setup on OnDemand from campus Wi-Fi or the VPN, and check the phone's clock.
nodes.future_risk: WSU moving to Duo or another MFA would change the prompts and the wizard text.

nodes.title: The grid accepts the laptop's key without prompting
nodes.assumption: The public key is in the grid's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys with modes sshd accepts, so `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid hostname` answers with no prompt. A key alone is sufficient: the grid does not ask for a second factor after publickey.
nodes.check: Laptop: testConnection(alias) returns ok with a non-empty hostname (stepInstallKey.check).
failure_signatures: Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive).
Authenticated using "publickey" with partial success.
Cannot reach the grid
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard step 'Log in to the grid once' (password and code, once).
nodes.future_risk: If C&IT required publickey plus keyboard-interactive on every login, every BatchMode path would break at once: extension, relay, MCP and the Remote-SSH ProxyJump.

nodes.title: GitHub token valid with the needed scopes
nodes.assumption: The GitHub token (a VS Code sign-in gho_, or a pasted ghp_ or github_pat_) is accepted by api.github.com and has repo, workflow, read:org and gist. Ideally the account uses the WSU email.
nodes.check: Laptop: GET https://api.github.com/user with the Bearer token returns 200 with 'login', and the x-oauth-scopes header contains repo (classic and OAuth tokens).
failure_signatures: no longer accepted (the service rejected it (HTTP 401)): press Renew
Resource protected by organization SAML enforcement
nodes.auto_repair: Renew through VS Code's GitHub sign-in (one click).
nodes.manual_fix: Press Renew next to GitHub.
nodes.future_risk: GitHub token prefix or format changes (the paste pattern). Fine-grained tokens have no x-oauth-scopes header.

nodes.title: Hugging Face token valid and write-capable
nodes.assumption: The hf_ token is accepted by whoami-v2 (200 with 'name'). The wizard asks for a write token, but nothing checks the role today.
nodes.check: Laptop: GET https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 with the Bearer token returns 200, and auth.accessToken.role is 'write' (or fine-grained scopes include repo write).
failure_signatures: no longer accepted (the service rejected it (HTTP 401)): press Renew
403 Forbidden on `hf upload` from the grid (read-only token)
nodes.manual_fix: Create a Write token on the pre-filled page and press Renew.
nodes.future_risk: HF token format changes (pattern ^hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}$). whoami-v2 being deprecated.

nodes.title: Claude subscription token valid (setup-token, one year)
nodes.assumption: The student has Claude Pro or Max (assumed to be the AccessID@wayne.edu account) and a setup-token OAuth token valid for one year. It is not refreshed after a 401; it must be regenerated.
nodes.check: Laptop: validateToken(claudeOauth) returns ok. Record the date the token was stored in globalState and warn at 330 days.
failure_signatures: OAuth access token is invalid
no longer accepted (the service rejected it (HTTP 401)): press Renew
worker results with status rate_limited

nodes.manual_fix: Press Renew next to Claude, sign in on claude.ai and press Authorize.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic changing subscription-token policy for automation, the token lifetime or plan eligibility.

nodes.title: GitHub /user endpoint contract
nodes.assumption: GET https://api.github.com/user with 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' and a User-Agent returns 200 JSON with 'login' for a valid token, and 401 for an invalid one.
nodes.check: Laptop: an unauthenticated GET https://api.github.com/user returns 401 with JSON message 'Requires authentication'. This proves the contract without a token.
failure_signatures: an unauthenticated status other than 401
an HTML body instead of JSON
nodes.manual_fix: Update validate.url or expectField in services.ts and rebuild.
nodes.future_risk: GitHub API versioning (X-GitHub-Api-Version).

nodes.title: Hugging Face whoami-v2 contract
nodes.assumption: GET https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 with a Bearer token returns 200 JSON with 'name', and 401 when the token is invalid.
nodes.check: Laptop: an unauthenticated GET https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 returns 401.
failure_signatures: 404 (endpoint renamed)
an unauthenticated status other than 401
nodes.manual_fix: Update validate.url in services.ts and rebuild.
nodes.future_risk: The endpoint being renamed or retired.

nodes.title: Anthropic /v1/models accepts subscription tokens for the check
nodes.assumption: GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models with 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ant-oat…', 'anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20' and 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' returns 200 for a valid subscription token and 401 for an invalid or revoked one. API keys use X-Api-Key. This is the only automated proof that a subscription token works, on the laptop and on the grid (verify-tokens).

failure_signatures: 403 for a valid OAuth token (Ashley would call it rejected)
400 invalid beta flag

nodes.future_risk: Anthropic retiring the oauth beta flag, restricting OAuth tokens to Claude Code's own endpoints, or bumping anthropic-version.

nodes.title: WSU and vendor pages the wizard opens still exist
nodes.assumption: These pages still exist: tech.wayne.edu/kb/high-performance-computing, services.wayne.edu/TDClient/277/Portal/KB/Article/20242, ondemand.grid.wayne.edu, the Google Authenticator store pages, huggingface.co/settings/tokens/new?..., github.com/settings/tokens/new?... and console.anthropic.com/settings/keys.
nodes.check: Laptop: GET each URL with redirects followed returns 2xx or 3xx, and the KB article page contains 'Authenticator'. ondemand is checked by network.wsu-campus-or-vpn.
failure_signatures: 404 Not Found
redirect to a generic portal page
nodes.manual_fix: Update the URL constants in wizard.ts and services.ts and rebuild.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT reorganising the TeamDynamix knowledge base. Vendors moving their token pages.

nodes.title: Marketplace installs of Remote-SSH and Claude Code
nodes.assumption: Remote-SSH and Claude Code install from the Visual Studio Marketplace. That works in Microsoft builds only; forks use Open VSX, which does not carry Remote-SSH.

Failed Installing Extensions

nodes.title: npm registry (maintainers)
nodes.assumption: registry.npmjs.org serves every package in package-lock.json. Students never run npm.
nodes.check: Maintainer laptop: `npm ping` prints PONG.

npm ERR! 404 Not Found

nodes.title: VS Code download CDN (integration tests)
nodes.assumption: update.code.visualstudio.com serves the stable build that @vscode/test-electron downloads. The Remote-SSH server download on compute nodes also needs it, from the grid side.
nodes.check: Maintainer laptop: `curl -sI https://update.code.visualstudio.com/api/update/win32-x64-archive/stable/latest` returns HTTP 200 or 302.
failure_signatures: Failed to download VS Code
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND update.code.visualstudio.com
nodes.manual_fix: Retry later.

nodes.title: Ashley's grid CLI answers (as seen from the laptop)
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/bin/ashley exists and runs on the login node. The laptop's calls go through it: version, status --json, access, worker, relay, phone and verify-tokens. The grid subsystem owns the internals; this node is the laptop's view of it.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley version'` exits 0 and prints a version.
failure_signatures: bash: /wsu/home/.../.ashley/bin/ashley: No such file or directory
Ashley is not installed on the grid yet
nodes.auto_repair: Run stepGridInstall.run.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: A full home quota. Panasas outages.

nodes.title: The ~/.bashrc block exports the VS Code sysroot (as seen from the laptop)
nodes.assumption: ~/.bashrc carries Ashley's block before any interactive-only return guard. It exports VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER, VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_PATH and VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH pointing into /wsu/apps/vscode, which must exist on the compute nodes. Red Hat bash sources ~/.bashrc for non-interactive ssh.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'grep -c ">>> ashley" ~/.bashrc; test -x /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/0.19.1/bin/patchelf && echo patchelf-ok'` prints a count >= 1 and patchelf-ok.
failure_signatures: found GLIBC 2.17
Exit code 207
The remote host may not meet VS Code Server's prerequisites
nodes.auto_repair: Run `ashley install`, which rewrites the block (stepGridInstall.run).
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: An OS migration removing /wsu/apps/vscode: the variables would then point at missing files and the server would fail to start.

nodes.title: A worker job is RUNNING (as seen from the laptop)
nodes.assumption: At least one Ashley worker job is RUNNING on a single compute node and reports its node name.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley worker list --json'` has an entry with job_state RUNNING and a non-empty node.
failure_signatures: No Claude worker is running on the grid.
job_state PENDING (Priority)
