nodes.auto_repair: After confirmation, resubmit with the last spec (commandWorkerStart).
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Start a Claude worker on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: Partition or QoS changes. Wall-time policy.

nodes.title: Lab-folder access state (as seen from the laptop)
nodes.assumption: `ashley access whoami --json` reports admin, granted or a request state. Workers use the shared container only after access is granted.
nodes.check: Laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley access whoami --json'` exits 0 with JSON that has granted true or admin true (a pending state is reported, not failed).
failure_signatures: unknown command (old grid scripts)
denied: <message>
it comes with lab access
nodes.manual_fix: File the request from the wizard's last step; the lead approves it in 'Ashley: Lab access'.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to the access mechanism on the grid.

nodes.title: Managed Ashley block in ~/.ssh/config
nodes.assumption: ~/.ssh/config starts with the block between '# >>> ashley (managed; ...' and '# <<< ashley <<<' produced by renderBlock(). 'Host wsu-grid grid' maps to HostName warrior.grid.wayne.edu with User <AccessID>, IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu, IdentitiesOnly yes, PreferredAuthentications publickey,keyboard-interactive,password, GSSAPIAuthentication no, AddressFamily inet, MACs +hmac-sha1, ServerAliveInterval 60, ServerAliveCountMax 5 and ConnectTimeout 20. 'Host *.nas.grid.wayne.edu' adds ProxyJump wsu-grid and StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new. The block is inserted first so it wins over a student's own 'Host *'. Remote-SSH, cli/ashley, cli/ashley.ps1, tools/push_via_grid.sh and testConnection() pass no MAC option and rely on the block. The extension's own calls repeat most options (SSH_BATCH_OPTS).
nodes.check: On the laptop, with no network: first run the wizard's own test, hasBlock(text) && upsertBlock(text, targets(settings)) === text, on ~/.ssh/config. Then `ssh -G wsu-grid` must print 'hostname warrior.grid.wayne.edu', 'user <AccessID>', 'addressfamily inet' and a 'macs' line ending in hmac-sha1, and `ssh -G asx1.nas.grid.wayne.edu` must print 'proxyjump wsu-grid'. Pass = every line matches. Verified on Greg's laptop 2026-09-28.
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname wsu-grid: No such host is known.
block missing or outdated
Bad owner or permissions on .../.ssh/config
<config> line N: Bad configuration option: ...
Could not resolve hostname grid
nodes.auto_repair: Run stepSshConfig.run(). It rewrites only the managed block (upsertBlock), keeps ~/.ssh/config.ashley.bak and is idempotent, so it is safe to run unattended.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard's 'SSH configuration' step, or print the block with `node dist/ashley-cli.js ssh-config` and paste it at the TOP of ~/.ssh/config. Do not edit inside the markers. On Windows, if OpenSSH complains about permissions, remove inherited ACL entries on %USERPROFILE%/.ssh/config so that only your own user has access.
nodes.future_risk: OpenSSH turning deprecated options into errors; Windows OpenSSH tightening its ACL checks on config files; Wayne State renaming the login host or the node domain. The defaults are hardcoded in store.ts:27-30, cli/main.ts:40-42 and the package.json settings.

nodes.title: Login host name resolves (IPv4)
nodes.assumption: warrior.grid.wayne.edu (setting ashley.loginHost) resolves to at least one IPv4 address from the student's network. The laptop never resolves compute-node names: with ProxyJump, warrior resolves them.
nodes.check: On the laptop: PowerShell `Resolve-DnsName warrior.grid.wayne.edu -Type A` (POSIX: `getent hosts warrior.grid.wayne.edu`). Pass = one or more A records. Log the addresses, and any AAAA record for network.ssh-ipv4-only.
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname warrior.grid.wayne.edu: No such host is known.
ssh: Could not resolve hostname warrior.grid.wayne.edu: Name or service not known
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND warrior.grid.wayne.edu (in-panel ssh2 login)
nodes.auto_repair: Flush the resolver cache once and check again: `ipconfig /flushdns` on Windows, `resolvectl flush-caches` on Linux, `dscacheutil -flushcache` on macOS. Nothing else is safe to automate.
nodes.manual_fix: Check the network (captive portal, hotel Wi-Fi). If Wayne State renamed the login host, set ashley.loginHost to the new name and rerun the 'SSH configuration' step.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT retiring 'warrior' for a new cluster name, or putting several login nodes behind one name. The default name is hardcoded in store.ts:27, cli/main.ts:40 and package.json (ashley.loginHost).

nodes.title: TCP 22 to the login node is reachable from this network
nodes.assumption: Port 22 on warrior is reachable from wherever the student is: home, campus Wi-Fi or the WSU VPN. The design assumes SSH faces the internet and that only OnDemand needs the campus network or the VPN. The measurements in CHECKPOINT come from one Windows laptop. Networks that block outbound 22, such as hospital or guest Wi-Fi, were not tested.
nodes.check: On the laptop: PowerShell `Test-NetConnection warrior.grid.wayne.edu -Port 22` must show TcpTestSucceeded True (POSIX: `nc -vz -w 5 warrior.grid.wayne.edu 22`). Also read the server banner, e.g. `ssh -v -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` and look for 'remote software version'. Today it is OpenSSH_7.4. Log it: a change means the login node was rebuilt.
failure_signatures: ssh: connect to host warrior.grid.wayne.edu port 22: Connection timed out
ssh: connect to host warrior.grid.wayne.edu port 22: Connection refused
kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset
kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
timed out talking to the grid (in-panel login)
nodes.manual_fix: Try the WSU VPN (GlobalProtect, portal protect.wayne.edu) or another network. If it fails from every network including the VPN, the grid is probably down for maintenance (see external.grid-maintenance); write to hpc@wayne.edu. After many failed logins the address may be blocked for a while, so wait before retrying.
nodes.future_risk: WSU restricting SSH to campus and VPN, a common HPC hardening step. Every off-campus call, the relay and Remote-SSH would then time out, and the wizard's statement that only OnDemand needs the VPN would be wrong. sshd could also move to another port or behind a bastion host.

nodes.title: SSH forced to IPv4 (AddressFamily inet)
nodes.assumption: On Windows, the IPv6 attempt to warrior times out before IPv4 is tried. Measured 2026-09-28 over nine runs each: 13.1 s per connection with IPv6 allowed, 2.0 s with AddressFamily inet. The block sets it for both Host entries. SSH_BATCH_OPTS, testConnection() and the terminal fallback pass -o AddressFamily=inet. cli/ashley, cli/ashley.ps1 and push_via_grid.sh rely on the block.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh -G wsu-grid` prints 'addressfamily inet', and so does `ssh -G <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu`. Time `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true`: pass = under 5 s (baseline 2.0 to 2.7 s). Optionally, `Resolve-DnsName warrior.grid.wayne.edu -Type AAAA` shows whether an IPv6 address is published.
failure_signatures: every grid action takes about 13 s
ssh -v shows 'connect to address <IPv6> port 22: Connection timed out' before the IPv4 attempt
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the managed block with stepSshConfig.run(). Safe and idempotent.
nodes.manual_fix: Rerun the wizard's SSH configuration step. Do not put a 'Host *' block that sets AddressFamily above the Ashley block.
nodes.future_risk: If WSU fixes IPv6 routing the setting becomes harmless. An IPv6-only login address (unlikely) would break every call. A Remote-SSH update could also pass its own AddressFamily option.

nodes.title: SHA-1 MAC re-enabled for the grid's sshd
nodes.assumption: The login node's sshd (OpenSSH 7.4 on CentOS 7) offers only hmac-sha1 to Windows OpenSSH 9.5, whose default MAC list leaves it out. Verified locally: `ssh -G wsu-grid` shows the default list with hmac-sha1 appended by the block. The client must still implement hmac-sha1; OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p2 does (`ssh -Q mac`). The in-panel ssh2 client (npm ssh2 1.17.0) offers hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-512 and hmac-sha1. testConnection(), cli/ashley, cli/ashley.ps1 and push_via_grid.sh do not pass the MAC option and depend on the block.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh -Q mac` lists hmac-sha1, and the 'macs' line of `ssh -G wsu-grid` ends in hmac-sha1. After a successful connection, `ssh -vv -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` shows the negotiated MAC in its 'kex: server->client cipher: ... MAC: ...' line. Log it: a switch to hmac-sha2-* means WSU upgraded sshd and the option can go.
failure_signatures: Unable to negotiate with <ip> port 22: no matching MAC found. Their offer: hmac-sha1
no matching MAC found. Their offer: hmac-sha1
Bad SSH2 MAC spec '+hmac-sha1'
Handshake failed: no matching mac (ssh2, in-panel login)
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the managed block with stepSshConfig.run(). If the client no longer implements hmac-sha1, there is no safe automatic repair.
nodes.manual_fix: Rerun the SSH configuration step. If Windows OpenSSH has dropped SHA-1 MACs, install another OpenSSH (Git for Windows or a newer Win32-OpenSSH), put it first on PATH and set remote.SSH.path to it. Tell hpc@wayne.edu that the login node needs to offer hmac-sha2.
nodes.future_risk: Microsoft removing SHA-1 MACs from Win32-OpenSSH altogether; npm ssh2 dropping hmac-sha1. A login node rebuilt on RHEL 8 or 9 would offer sha2 under its crypto policy, which makes this line harmless.

nodes.title: Login node host key known before any BatchMode call
nodes.assumption: warrior's host key is already in ~/.ssh/known_hosts. The login Host entry sets no StrictHostKeyChecking, so it resolves to 'ask' (confirmed with `ssh -G wsu-grid`), and BatchMode turns 'ask' into a refusal. The in-panel ssh2 login sets no hostVerifier: it neither checks nor records the host key. On a fresh laptop this has a consequence. After a successful in-panel key install, testConnection() fails with 'Host key verification failed.', and stepInstallKey falls through to the terminal login (StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new), which asks for the password and the code a second time. Greg's laptop already had an ssh-rsa entry for warrior (known_hosts line 6), which is why this never showed. Because nothing checks the host key, the ssh2 path also sends the password and one-time code to whichever host answers.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh-keygen -F warrior.grid.wayne.edu` exits 0 and prints an entry. Log its key type (today ssh-rsa). Also `ssh -G wsu-grid` and read its stricthostkeychecking line.
failure_signatures: Host key verification failed.
WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
Host key for warrior.grid.wayne.edu has changed and you have requested strict checking.
still prompted: Host key verification failed. (wizard, right after the in-panel login succeeded)
nodes.auto_repair: Only when the key is missing, never when it has changed: record it on first use with `ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` (the key is stored before authentication). Better, compare it with a fingerprint published by C&IT. Code changes to consider: add 'StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new' to the login Host entry, and give ssh2 a hostVerifier that checks and writes known_hosts.
nodes.manual_fix: If the key CHANGED, confirm with hpc@wayne.edu that the login node was rebuilt. Then run `ssh-keygen -R warrior.grid.wayne.edu` and connect once in a terminal.
nodes.future_risk: An OS migration regenerates host keys. Every laptop then fails at once with REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED, and no automatic repair is safe. Several login nodes behind one name with different keys would cause the same symptom intermittently.

nodes.title: The grid accepts the key alone (no second factor on key logins)
nodes.assumption: sshd on warrior lets publickey authentication complete by itself; Google Authenticator is asked only on the password path. Everything after the one password-and-code login depends on this: BatchMode calls, the relay, the MCP bridge, Remote-SSH and ProxyJump.
nodes.check: On the laptop, run `ssh -v -o BatchMode=yes -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey wsu-grid true` and read stderr. FAIL if it contains 'partial success': sshd now requires a second factor after the key. PASS if it exits 0 after 'Authenticated to warrior.grid.wayne.edu ... using "publickey"'. WARN, not fail, if it says 'Permission denied' without 'partial success': the key is not accepted yet, so the policy cannot be judged.
failure_signatures: Authenticated using "publickey" with partial success.
Permission denied (keyboard-interactive).
Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive).
nodes.manual_fix: If WSU now requires a second factor even with keys, Ashley's prompt-free design no longer holds. Escalate to Greg. The likely route is one long-lived ssh2 session per laptop that answers the second factor once, because Windows OpenSSH has no ControlMaster.
nodes.future_risk: High. Policies that require MFA on every login (Duo, Microsoft MFA) are a common HPC hardening step, and they would break every non-interactive path at once.
nodes.source: extension/src/core/sshInstall.ts:1-5; extension/src/core/wizard.ts:254,316-358; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (Secrets table: password and code typed once)

nodes.title: This laptop's key is authorized on the grid
nodes.assumption: The public key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu.pub (comment '<AccessID>@wayne.edu ashley') is a line of ~/.ssh/authorized_keys in the grid home. sshd StrictModes must accept the permissions: home not writable by group or others, ~/.ssh 700, authorized_keys 600. With IdentitiesOnly, only this key is offered.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey wsu-grid true` exits 0. A password-expiry message in stderr also means the key was accepted (see account.wsu-password-current). Once a session works: `ssh wsu-grid "grep -c ashley ~/.ssh/authorized_keys; stat -c '%a %U' ~ ~/.ssh ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"` must show a count of 1 or more, modes no looser than 755, 700 and 600, and the AccessID as owner. The fingerprint from `ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu.pub` must appear in the output of `ssh wsu-grid ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.
failure_signatures: Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive).
Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive,password).
unexpected reply: ... (the in-panel install did not print ASHLEY-KEY-INSTALLED)
the grid does not accept the key yet
nodes.auto_repair: Only with a working session: `chmod go-w ~; chmod 700 ~/.ssh; chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` (the student's own files). Without a session, the repair is the wizard step 'Log in to the grid once', which needs the password and the Authenticator code from a person.
nodes.manual_fix: Rerun 'Log in to the grid once'. If it reports success but key logins still fail, open a shell through OnDemand and run the chmod line above.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT moving keys to a central store (AuthorizedKeysCommand) or forbidding user-managed keys. FIPS mode on a RHEL 9 login node would reject ed25519 keys; an ECDSA P-256 or RSA 3072 key would then be needed.

nodes.title: AccessID password not expired
nodes.assumption: sshd runs the PAM account phase even for key logins. An expired AccessID password forces a change, which a non-interactive session cannot perform, so key logins break although the key itself is fine.
nodes.check: On the laptop: the stderr of `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` contains neither 'password has expired' nor 'Password change required'. Pass = neither text present.
failure_signatures: WARNING: Your password has expired.
Password change required but no TTY available.
You are required to change your password immediately (password aged)
nodes.manual_fix: Change the AccessID password through Wayne State's password service (C&IT), then retry. An interactive `ssh wsu-grid` may also offer the change.
nodes.future_risk: WSU changing password rotation, or a directory migration (AD or Entra) that changes how expiry is enforced.
nodes.source: No explicit code; implicit in extension/src/core/wizard.ts:147-151 and extension/src/core/shell.ts:96 (BatchMode everywhere)

nodes.title: Every Ashley path uses an ssh that reads the same configuration
nodes.assumption: Up to three ssh executables can be involved. spawn('ssh') resolved through PATH serves the extension, the relay, the MCP server and the CLI. resolveExecutable() uses %SystemRoot%/System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe for interactive terminals. Remote-SSH uses remote.SSH.path. All of them must read %USERPROFILE%/.ssh/config and known_hosts and support the options in use. On Greg's laptop, PATH resolves only System32/OpenSSH/ssh.exe (9.5p2).
nodes.check: On the laptop: PowerShell `Get-Command ssh -All | % Source` (note the first entry and the count), then `ssh -V` for each entry. The VS Code setting remote.SSH.path must be empty or equal to the first entry. Pass = a single ssh, or all of them at 8.x or newer reading the same home directory. WARN when several different ones are present.
failure_signatures: spawn ssh ENOENT (run() returns code 127)
the panel works but Remote-SSH does not, or the reverse
Git Bash's ssh reads a different HOME and misses the block
nodes.manual_fix: Put %SystemRoot%/System32/OpenSSH first on PATH, or install Windows' 'OpenSSH Client' optional feature. Set remote.SSH.path to the same ssh.exe.
nodes.future_risk: Windows Update silently changing Win32-OpenSSH defaults; Git for Windows putting a newer ssh earlier on PATH.

nodes.title: SSH to the login node with no prompt (BatchMode)
nodes.assumption: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid <cmd>` authenticates with the key alone and runs the command within ConnectTimeout 20 s (2.0 to 2.7 s measured from Windows). Every laptop-to-grid path rides on it: GridApi.ashley(), testConnection(), gridInstalled(), pushTokens(), the scp upload, the relay, the MCP server, cli/ashley, cli/ashley.ps1, tools/push_via_grid.sh and Remote-SSH's ProxyJump.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 wsu-grid hostname` exits 0 and the first word of stdout is the login host (warrior). Record the elapsed time: the baseline is 2.0 to 2.7 s, and more than 10 s suggests the IPv6 timeout. This is exactly what testConnection() does.
failure_signatures: Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive).
Host key verification failed.
no matching MAC found. Their offer: hmac-sha1
ssh: connect to host warrior.grid.wayne.edu port 22: Connection timed out
Received disconnect from <ip> port 22:2: Too many authentication failures
This account is currently not available.
Password change required but no TTY available.
nodes.auto_repair: Check the children first and repair the first one that fails (block rewrite, first-use host key). Never retry authentication more than twice a minute: the grid counts failed attempts.
nodes.manual_fix: Run Ashley: Check everything and fix the root cause it names. If every local check passes and ssh still fails, check external.grid-maintenance and write to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: A login-node OS migration (CentOS 7 to RHEL 8 or 9) changes host keys, crypto policy and possibly the authentication methods all at once. The login host may also be renamed.
nodes.source: extension/src/core/shell.ts:94-108; extension/src/core/wizard.ts:147-151,464-469; extension/src/core/gridApi.ts:37-45; extension/src/vscode/tree.ts:64; cli/ashley:78-88; cli/ashley.ps1:1-12; tools/push_via_grid.sh:13-15

nodes.title: Grid home is /wsu/home/ab/ab12/ab1234
nodes.assumption: gridHome() builds /wsu/home/<first 2 characters>/<first 4 characters>/<AccessID>. The result becomes ASHLEY_GRID_HOME in local terminals and the default folder that commandConnect opens in Remote-SSH.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'id -un; echo $HOME'`. Pass = the first line equals ashley.accessId and the second equals gridHome(accessId).
failure_signatures: the Remote-SSH window opens an empty or non-existent folder
ASHLEY_GRID_HOME points to a path that does not exist
nodes.auto_repair: Use the $HOME the grid reports instead of the computed path. This is safe (read only) but needs a small code change wherever services.ts gridHome() is called.
nodes.manual_fix: Type the correct folder when Ashley asks which folder to open.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT reorganising home directories or moving homes off Panasas.

nodes.title: AccessID known and well formed
nodes.assumption: The AccessID matches /^[a-z]{2}\d{4}$/ and is the grid username. It comes from the Microsoft sign-in (the local part of AccessID@wayne.edu; subdomains allowed) or is typed by the student. It names the grid home and the ssh User. By lab convention, unverified, it also names the student's Claude and GitHub accounts.
nodes.check: On the laptop: the setting ashley.accessId (CLI: accessId in ~/.ashley-local/settings.json) matches the pattern, and ashley.wsuEmail ends in wayne.edu.
failure_signatures: An AccessID looks like ab1234 (two letters, four digits).
not signed in
<email> is not a Wayne State account; sign in with AccessID@wayne.edu
nodes.auto_repair: If ashley.wsuEmail is set and its local part matches the pattern, copy it into ashley.accessId. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Sign in with Wayne State' again, or type the AccessID when asked.
nodes.future_risk: WSU issuing AccessIDs in another format: the regex in services.ts:88, tools/allow.py:15 and the admin grant input in extension.ts would reject them. If UPNs became firstname.lastname@wayne.edu, the AccessID could no longer be derived from the sign-in and the wizard would fall back to asking.

nodes.title: VS Code's Microsoft sign-in is available
nodes.assumption: VS Code's built-in Microsoft authentication provider is present and enabled and accepts the scopes ['VSCODE_TENANT:organizations','User.Read'], which admit work or school accounts only. session.account.label is the account's e-mail. VSCodium and other forks do not ship this provider.
nodes.check: In the extension host: `vscode.authentication.getSession('microsoft', ['VSCODE_TENANT:organizations','User.Read'], { silent: true })` resolves without throwing. An undefined result only means the student is not signed in yet and is not a failure. `vscode.extensions.getExtension('vscode.microsoft-authentication')` is defined. Log the value of the setting microsoft-authentication.implementation.
failure_signatures: No authentication provider 'microsoft' is currently registered.
User did not consent to login.
the Wayne State sign-in did not complete (...)
the Windows account broker offers a personal Microsoft account
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to typing the AccessID. This is safe: the e-mail is used only to derive the AccessID.
nodes.manual_fix: Use Microsoft's build of VS Code, and sign in with AccessID@wayne.edu rather than a personal account.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code changing its Microsoft sign-in implementation (MSAL, the Windows broker), the VSCODE_TENANT scope convention, or the format of the account label.

nodes.title: Wayne State's tenant lets students sign in to VS Code
nodes.assumption: WSU's Microsoft Entra tenant allows students to consent to VS Code's first-party app for User.Read, no Conditional Access policy blocks the sign-in, and the account's MFA completes in the browser.
nodes.check: On the laptop, interactively, once: the step 'Sign in with Wayne State' returns an e-mail matching /@([a-z0-9-]+\.)*wayne\.edu$/i. After that, the silent getSession call returns the same account.
failure_signatures: AADSTS65001: The user or administrator has not consented to use the application
AADSTS90094: The grant requires admin permission
AADSTS50020: User account from identity provider does not exist in tenant
AADSTS53003: Access has been blocked by Conditional Access policies
nodes.manual_fix: Type the AccessID instead. If admin consent is required, ask C&IT to approve 'Visual Studio Code' for User.Read in the WSU tenant.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to the tenant's consent or Conditional Access policy, including device-compliance requirements for sign-ins from personal laptops.

nodes.title: AccessID is on the lab's pre-approved list
nodes.assumption: The AccessID is either in extension/media/allowlist.json, which ships in the VSIX (committed in a2e1f69; today it holds ['go2432']), or in the JSON at ashley.allowlistUrl. The URL is fetched with a 10 s timeout and the bundled list is the fallback. A missing or unreadable list means no restriction. The check runs only on the laptop and is not a security boundary.
nodes.check: On the laptop: read <extensionPath>/media/allowlist.json (CLI: dist/../media/allowlist.json or dist/allowlist.json) and test accessIds.includes(id). When ashley.allowlistUrl is set, `curl -s -m 10 <url>` must return JSON with an accessIds array. Report which list decided.
failure_signatures: <id> is not on the lab's pre-approved list; ask your lead to add you
<id> is not on the lab's pre-approved list; ask your lead to add you, then sign in again
nodes.auto_repair: Fetch ashley.allowlistUrl again. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: The lead runs `python tools/allow.py add <id>`, rebuilds the VSIX (`cd extension && npm run package`) and sends it, or updates the JSON behind ashley.allowlistUrl.
nodes.future_risk: The host behind allowlistUrl moving. A VSIX built from a checkout without the file silently admits everyone.

nodes.title: Grid account exists and is active
nodes.assumption: An HPC account exists for the AccessID and is neither expired nor disabled. It is requested at tech.wayne.edu naming the sponsor and takes about two business days.
nodes.check: If the key already works: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'id -un'` returns the AccessID (pass). Otherwise the laptop cannot tell, because sshd does not reveal unknown users, so return WARN 'unverified; log in at ondemand.grid.wayne.edu to prove it'. The lab admin can check from the login node with `getent passwd <id>`.
failure_signatures: the grid rejected the password or the code (on every attempt)
three rejected logins: check the account exists and redo the Authenticator setup ...
This account is currently not available.
Your account has expired; please contact your system administrator
nodes.manual_fix: Apply at tech.wayne.edu/kb/high-performance-computing, naming your lead as sponsor. Contact: hpc@wayne.edu, 313-577-4743.
nodes.future_risk: Renewal cycles (sponsors re-approving each semester or year), clean-ups at graduation, or a new cluster that needs new accounts.

nodes.title: Campus network or WSU VPN (for the OnDemand 2FA setup)
nodes.assumption: ondemand.grid.wayne.edu answers only from the campus network (WSU Wi-Fi) or through the WSU GlobalProtect VPN (portal protect.wayne.edu, with MFA, for current students and employees). onDemandReachable() treats any HTTP answer within 8 s as 'on campus or on the VPN'; it does not follow redirects. This is needed only for the one-time Authenticator setup.
nodes.check: On the laptop. Skip when ashley.twoFactorDone is true or the key already works. Otherwise run `curl.exe -s -o NUL -m 8 -w "%{http_code}" https://ondemand.grid.wayne.edu/`: any code other than 000 (typically 302) means reachable. VPN client state: `Get-NetAdapter | ? InterfaceDescription -match 'PANGP'` shows the adapter Up.
failure_signatures: Check again (OnDemand not reachable: join the WSU Wi-Fi on campus, or connect the WSU VPN)
fetch failed
This operation was aborted (the 8 s timeout)
a captive portal answers 200 for everything (false pass)
nodes.manual_fix: Connect GlobalProtect to protect.wayne.edu, or join the campus Wi-Fi, then choose 'Check again'.
nodes.future_risk: If OnDemand opens to the internet behind SSO, the check no longer detects the VPN (harmless for the setup). The OnDemand URL or the VPN portal could be renamed, or the VPN limited to employees.

nodes.title: Google Authenticator enrolled for the grid
nodes.assumption: The student enrolled Google Authenticator through OnDemand > Interactive Apps > 2FA Setup (a QR code). The grid's keyboard-interactive login asks 'Password:' and then a verification code. The in-panel client routes prompts by regex: /pass/i goes to the password field (once) and /verification|code|token/i to the code field. The phone's clock and the grid's clock agree within the TOTP window. ashley.twoFactorDone is the student's own claim; only a successful login proves it.
nodes.check: Skip when the key already works. Otherwise a person does one login in 'Log in to the grid once'. Once a session exists, a cheap clock check: the difference between `ssh wsu-grid date +%s` and the laptop's NTP time is under 30 s (the relay's PONG also carries the grid clock).
failure_signatures: the grid rejected the password or the code
The grid rejected that password or code (attempt N of 3). Try again.
three rejected logins: check the account exists and redo the Authenticator setup (the previous step opens OnDemand), then run the wizard again
Permission denied (keyboard-interactive).
nodes.auto_repair: After three rejected logins, set ashley.twoFactorDone back to false and route the student back to 'Grid account and Authenticator'. This is already implemented.
nodes.manual_fix: Redo 2FA Setup on OnDemand (campus Wi-Fi or VPN). On Android, turn on the Authenticator's time correction. Wait for a fresh code before typing it.
nodes.future_risk: WSU replacing Google Authenticator with Duo or Microsoft Authenticator push. The prompt texts would change, a push approval cannot be typed into a field, and the wizard's links and instructions would be wrong. The OnDemand 2FA Setup app could also be renamed, or the KB article moved.

nodes.title: The in-panel SSH client (npm ssh2) can talk to the grid
nodes.assumption: The bundled pure-JavaScript ssh2 1.17.0 negotiates with OpenSSH 7.4 on port 22 (MACs hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-512, hmac-sha1), answers the keyboard-interactive prompts, and runs the install command that prints ASHLEY-KEY-INSTALLED. On a failure that is not an authentication failure, the wizard falls back to ssh in a terminal. It verifies no host key.
nodes.check: On the laptop, once the key works: `node dist/ashley-cli.js ssh2-probe` prints 'ssh2 reached warrior.grid.wayne.edu as <id>: warrior'. This proves negotiation with the same library; the password half needs a person.
failure_signatures: ssh2 failed: timed out
timed out talking to the grid
exec failed: ...
unexpected reply: ...
In-panel login did not work (...); falling back to a terminal.
Handshake failed: no matching ...
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to the terminal login (existing behaviour).
nodes.manual_fix: Use the terminal fallback and report the ssh2 error text.
nodes.future_risk: ssh2 dropping SHA-1 MACs or older key-exchange methods; a login-node upgrade to algorithms ssh2 lacks; Node or Electron crypto changes that affect ed25519 key parsing.

nodes.title: Non-interactive ssh sessions print nothing
nodes.assumption: Red Hat's bash sources ~/.bashrc for commands run by sshd (SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC), so anything the student's startup files print to stdout arrives ahead of Ashley's output. The relay protocol, scp over SFTP, testConnection() (the first word of stdout is taken as the hostname) and parseLastJson() all need a clean stdout. The Ashley block itself prints nothing.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` writes 0 bytes to stdout (PowerShell: `(ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true | Out-String).Length -eq 0`; POSIX: `| wc -c` gives 0). To find the culprit: `ssh wsu-grid 'bash -x ~/.bashrc' 2>&1 | head -40`.
failure_signatures: Received message too long <n>
Ensure the remote shell produces no output for non-interactive sessions.
protocol error: ...
the Ashley view shows 'wsu-grid -> <text>' instead of warrior
status did not return JSON
nodes.manual_fix: Guard output in ~/.bashrc with `[[ $- == *i* ]] && echo ...`, or send it to stderr. Keep conda and module messages quiet.
nodes.future_risk: On a RHEL 8 or 9 login node whose bash no longer sources ~/.bashrc for ssh commands, the Ashley block (the VS Code sysroot variables and PATH) would no longer apply to Remote-SSH sessions.

nodes.title: SFTP subsystem available for scp
nodes.assumption: The scp in Windows OpenSSH 9.5 uses the SFTP protocol by default, so the grid's sshd must offer the sftp subsystem. '~/.ashley/bin/' works because scp in SFTP mode treats a leading ~/ as relative to the login directory, so OpenSSH 7.4 needs no expand-path extension. The grid install upload and push_via_grid.sh both use scp.
nodes.check: On the laptop, from Git Bash or with a batch file that has LF line endings: `printf 'pwd\n' | sftp -b - -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid` prints 'Remote working directory: /wsu/home/...' and exits 0.
failure_signatures: subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed
upload failed: ...
server expand-path extension is required for ~user paths in SFTP mode
nodes.auto_repair: Retry the copy with the legacy protocol, `scp -O`, which OpenSSH 9.x clients still support. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Rerun 'Install on the grid'. If sftp is disabled on the login node, ask hpc@wayne.edu, or copy with `ssh wsu-grid 'cat > file' < file`.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT disabling sftp on login nodes and moving transfers to a data node; OpenSSH eventually removing scp -O.

nodes.title: Several ssh sessions per user are allowed at once
nodes.assumption: The login node tolerates several concurrent sessions per user: one relay per VS Code window, one per MCP server process (Claude Code starts one per session), one per CLI, plus short-lived calls and Remote-SSH jumps. No maxlogins or MaxStartups limit is reached.
nodes.check: On the login node (cheap): `pgrep -u $USER -fc 'ashley relay'`, `who | grep -c "^$USER "` and `grep -hs maxlogins /etc/security/limits.conf /etc/security/limits.d/*`. Pass = fewer than 10 relays and fewer sessions than any maxlogins value.
failure_signatures: Too many logins for '<id>'.
kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer
ssh_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
relay closed (ssh exit 255), repeatedly
nodes.auto_repair: Kill only this user's stale relays on the login node with `pkill -u $USER -f 'ashley relay'`; clients reconnect on their next call. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Close unused VS Code windows and Claude Code sessions.
nodes.future_risk: Per-user session caps or idle-session reapers on the login node.

nodes.title: A relay process may run for hours on the login node
nodes.assumption: `ashley relay` is a bash `read -t 0.25` loop that uses almost no CPU, and it is allowed to run for hours on warrior. C&IT kills VS Code servers and heavy processes there, but not idle shells. The relay needs bash 4 or newer (associative arrays, fractional read timeout) and GNU date (%3N).
nodes.check: On the login node: `bash --version | head -1` shows 4 or newer, and `date +%s%3N` prints 13 digits. If a relay is running, `ps -o etimes=,pcpu= -p $(pgrep -u $USER -f 'ashley relay' | head -1)` shows elapsed seconds past 3600 at about 0 % CPU. WARN if no relay exists to observe.
failure_signatures: relay closed (ssh exit 255)
relay closed (ssh exit null) Killed
local: -A: invalid option
relay send failed (...); using a fresh ssh (repeated in the Ashley log)
nodes.auto_repair: Nothing is needed for correctness: GridApi falls back to a fresh ssh per call, at about 2 s instead of 40 ms.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask C&IT whether an idle-process policy applies to the login node.
nodes.future_risk: A process watchdog on the login node extended to long-lived processes; a restricted shell.

nodes.title: The prompt relay session answers (READY and PONG)
nodes.assumption: Each process holds one ssh session running `~/.ashley/bin/ashley relay`. The relay prints `READY <epoch ms> <version>`, answers PING with PONG in about 20 ms and SEND with QUEUED in about 40 ms (measured 2026-09-28), and pushes EVENT and RESULT lines. ServerAliveInterval=30 (with the block's CountMax of 5) detects a dead path. After 'close' the next call reconnects, and every GridApi call falls back to a fresh ssh on error. The READY version is parsed but never compared with the grid version bundled in the extension. The relay does not strip CR, so input sent with CRLF line endings is not understood.
nodes.check:
On the laptop, sending LF-only input: from Node (spawn ssh with stdin 'PING
QUIT
'), or from Git Bash `printf 'PING
QUIT
' | ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley relay'`. Pass = 'READY <13 digits> <v>' then 'PONG <13 digits>' within 5 s, with <v> equal to the extension's dist/grid/VERSION. Alternatively `node dist/ashley-cli.js latency 1` shows ping_relay under 500 ms. Do not use a PowerShell pipe: it sends CRLF, and the relay then answers 'ERROR unknown command'. The grid-side counterpart is the node grid.relay in `ashley diag --json`, which runs the relay locally rather than over ssh.
failure_signatures: relay closed (ssh exit 1) ashley: unknown command 'relay' (ashley help)
relay closed (ssh exit 255)
relay is not connected
no QUEUED ack from the relay within 30 s
ERROR bad request or unknown worker '<w>'
ERROR unknown command (CRLF input)
bad result line: ...
ashley_result takes 10 s for an unfinished request: relay.ts ignores the grid's 'PENDING <id>' reply and waits for its 10 s timer
an ERROR line is charged to the newest waiter, because the ERROR reply carries no id
nodes.auto_repair: Call relay.close() and then ensure(). Safe. On a version mismatch or 'unknown command relay', upload the grid scripts again with the gridInstall step (scp plus `ashley install`, idempotent).
nodes.manual_fix: Run Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid, then reload the window.
nodes.future_risk: Protocol changes without any version negotiation. After laptop sleep, a half-open session can linger for up to ServerAliveInterval times CountMax.

nodes.title: ProxyJump through the login node to compute nodes
nodes.assumption: 'Host *.nas.grid.wayne.edu' uses ProxyJump wsu-grid. This requires that warrior allows TCP forwarding (direct-tcpip), that warrior resolves node names (the short name from squeue %N plus nodeDomain), and that Windows OpenSSH can start its own ssh.exe for the jump. The laptop never reaches a node directly.
nodes.check: On the laptop: spawn `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid -W asx1.nas.grid.wayne.edu:22` (any node; use the worker's node when there is one) with stdin closed, and read the first line within 30 s. Pass = it starts with 'SSH-2.0-'. This proves forwarding, DNS on warrior and a listening node sshd, before pam_slurm_adopt is involved. On the login node, `getent hosts <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu` must resolve.
failure_signatures: channel 0: open failed: administratively prohibited: open failed
stdio forwarding failed
channel 0: open failed: connect failed: Name or service not known
CreateProcessW failed error:2
posix_spawnp: No such file or directory
Could not resolve hostname asx1: No such host is known. (a short name does not match the *.nas pattern)
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the managed block with stepSshConfig.run(). If Windows cannot start ssh for ProxyJump, write the equivalent 'ProxyCommand <absolute path to ssh.exe> -W %h:%p wsu-grid' inside the managed block. Same meaning, and reversible.
nodes.manual_fix: Rerun the SSH configuration step. If C&IT has disabled forwarding, Remote-SSH to nodes cannot work; escalate.
nodes.future_risk: AllowTcpForwarding disabled on login nodes (a common hardening step); the node domain renamed (the default nas.grid.wayne.edu is in store.ts:29 and cli/main.ts:42); Remote-SSH using a different ssh through remote.SSH.path.

nodes.title: ssh to a node works only while holding a job there
nodes.assumption: A compute node's sshd admits a user only while that user has a running job on the node (pam_slurm_adopt), and the session joins that job's cgroup with its CPU, memory and pids limits. Ashley connects only to the worker's node or to a node that squeue lists as RUNNING.
nodes.check: On the login node, `squeue -u $USER -h -t R -o %N` returns a node. From the laptop, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=120 <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu true` exits 0. This is slow, 23 to 101 s (see network.node-sshd-latency). Skip when no job is running.
failure_signatures: Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node
Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535
Authentication failed.
nodes.auto_repair: Offer to start a worker (commandWorkerStart), then wait for RUNNING and a node file. This spends the student's allocation, so ask first.
nodes.manual_fix: Start a worker, wait until the Ashley view shows its node, then use Open my grid files.
nodes.future_risk: ssh to nodes disabled in favour of `srun --pty` only; changes in how sessions are adopted for multi-node or requeued jobs.

nodes.title: Node ssh answers within Remote-SSH's timeout
nodes.assumption: A compute node's sshd takes about 23 s before it runs anything; 62 s and 101 s were observed later, also from warrior and with bash --norc. The first Remote-SSH connection also downloads the VS Code server. commandConnect raises remote.SSH.connectTimeout to 300 s. The diagnostics engine's default per-check timeout of 90 s is too short for this node: give it about 320 s and mark it slow.
nodes.check: On the laptop (slow): time `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=300 <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu true`. Pass = under 300 s; log the time (baseline 23 to 101 s). The VS Code setting remote.SSH.connectTimeout must be 300 or more.
failure_signatures: Connecting with SSH timed out
Could not establish connection to "<node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu": The connection timed out
a second window timed out twice at 302 s while an earlier VS Code server was still running on the node (not diagnosed)
nodes.auto_repair: Set remote.SSH.connectTimeout to 300; connect already does this. For a stale server, `ssh <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu pkill -u $USER -f vscode-server` kills only the student's own processes; ask first.
nodes.manual_fix: Wait and retry. Use 'Remote-SSH: Kill VS Code Server on Host', and read the newest 'Remote - SSH' output log.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to node sshd or PAM (slower or faster); the VS Code server download (update.code.visualstudio.com) being blocked from nodes.

nodes.title: Compute-node host keys learnt and stable
nodes.assumption: Node host keys are learnt on first use (StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new in the *.nas block) and do not change between visits.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `ssh-keygen -F <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu` finds an entry after the first connection, and its fingerprint equals the one the login node sees: `ssh wsu-grid ssh-keyscan -t ed25519,ecdsa,rsa <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu 2>/dev/null | ssh-keygen -lf -`.
failure_signatures: WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
Host key verification failed.
nodes.auto_repair: When the key fetched through the authenticated login node differs from known_hosts: `ssh-keygen -R <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu`, then append the keyscan line. The trust path is the already-authenticated jump host; log what changed.
nodes.manual_fix: Do the same by hand after confirming the node was reimaged.
nodes.future_risk: Reimaging nodes during an OS migration changes every node key at once.

nodes.title: Laptop HTTPS to the token services
nodes.assumption: The extension host's global fetch reaches api.github.com, huggingface.co, api.anthropic.com and ondemand.grid.wayne.edu with a trusted certificate chain. When it cannot (a proxy, TLS inspection, blocked hosts), validateToken() returns network:true, and the token is kept and verified on the grid instead.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `curl.exe -s -o NUL -m 10 -w "%{http_code} %{ssl_verify_result}" https://api.github.com/zen` returns '200 0'. https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 and https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models without credentials return 401. Repeat from the extension host, because fetch treats VS Code's proxy settings differently from curl.
failure_signatures: this laptop's network refused the check (fetch failed)
self-signed certificate in certificate chain
unable to get local issuer certificate
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.github.com
stored (could not check it online just now)
nodes.auto_repair: None. Verification moves to the grid (grid-login.verify-tokens), which is the designed fallback.
nodes.manual_fix: Try another network or the VPN. If a proxy is mandatory, set http.proxy in VS Code.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code changing proxy support for fetch in the extension host; TLS inspection on campus or hospital networks.

nodes.title: GitHub API contract (GET /user)
nodes.assumption: GET https://api.github.com/user with 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' and a User-Agent returns 200 JSON containing 'login'; 401 means a bad token. The laptop sends User-Agent 'ashley-wsu'. The grid extracts the login with grep '"login": *"..."'.
nodes.check: From the laptop or the login node, without a token: `curl -s -m 10 -H 'User-Agent: ashley-diag' https://api.github.com/user` returns HTTP 401 with 'Requires authentication'. That shows the endpoint is alive and unchanged. Any 5xx is an outage (see external.vendor-status).
failure_signatures: HTTP 401 Bad credentials
HTTP 403 Request forbidden by administrative rules. Please make sure your request has a User-Agent header
HTTP 403 API rate limit exceeded
nodes.manual_fix: Nothing for students. If the contract changed, update the validate entry in services.ts and cmd_verify_tokens in grid/ashley.
nodes.future_risk: API versioning (X-GitHub-Api-Version) or changes to the response shape; token prefix changes (the paste pattern accepts only ghp_ and github_pat_).

nodes.title: Hugging Face API contract (whoami-v2)
nodes.assumption: GET https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 with 'Bearer hf_...' returns 200 compact JSON whose first 'name' field is the user. The grid extracts it with grep '"name":"[^"]*"', which allows no space after the colon.
nodes.check: From the laptop or the login node, without a token: `curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2` returns 401.
failure_signatures: HTTP 401 Invalid credentials in Authorization header
HTTP 429 (whoami is rate-limited)
HF_TOKEN rejected or unreachable (on the grid, when the JSON is pretty-printed or its fields reordered)
nodes.manual_fix: If the response shape changed, update the grep in cmd_verify_tokens (grid/ashley), or parse the JSON with python3 or node.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to formatting or field order; stricter rate limits on whoami; the token page ignoring its query parameters.

nodes.title: Anthropic API contract (GET /v1/models)
nodes.assumption: GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models returns 200 with 'data' for a valid credential: either an API key in X-Api-Key with anthropic-version 2023-06-01, or a subscription OAuth token as Bearer with 'anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20'. An invalid credential returns 401. A 200 on the OAuth path has not been observed with a real setup-token (see account.claude-oauth-token).
nodes.check: From the laptop or the login node, without a credential: `curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models` returns 401, with a JSON error of type authentication_error.
failure_signatures: HTTP 401 authentication_error
HTTP 403 permission error
HTTP 400 invalid beta header
HTTP 429 or 529 overloaded
nodes.manual_fix: If the beta header or the endpoint changed, update services.ts:66 and grid/ashley:807 together.
nodes.future_risk: High. The oauth-2025-04-20 beta header could be retired, or OAuth tokens restricted to Claude Code's own traffic; anthropic-version could be bumped.

nodes.title: VS Code SecretStorage keeps tokens across restarts
nodes.assumption: context.secrets, under the keys ashley.github, ashley.huggingface, ashley.claudeOauth and ashley.anthropicApiKey, persists across restarts through the OS backend: Windows DPAPI via Electron safeStorage, the macOS Keychain, or libsecret or kwallet on Linux. The CLI instead keeps ~/.ashley-local/secrets.json with mode 600, which is not enforced on Windows.
nodes.check: In the extension host: store 'ashley.__diag' with a random value, read it back, confirm it is equal, then delete it. secretSummary() must report the same flags after a window reload.
failure_signatures: An OS keyring couldn't be identified for storing the encryption related data in your current desktop environment.
tokens show 'not set' after a restart
Error while decrypting the ciphertext provided to safeStorage.decryptString
nodes.manual_fix: On Linux, install and unlock gnome-keyring, or start VS Code with a supported --password-store. Then run the token steps again; GitHub is one browser click.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code changing its secret backends or flags. A new VS Code profile or --user-data-dir starts empty, and Settings Sync does not carry secrets.

nodes.title: VS Code's GitHub sign-in
nodes.assumption: VS Code's built-in GitHub authentication gets an OAuth token (gho_...) for the scopes repo, workflow, read:org and gist through the browser. Ashley copies the token into SecretStorage and to the grid as GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN.
nodes.check: In the extension host: `vscode.authentication.getSession('github', ['repo','workflow','read:org','gist'], { silent: true })` returns a session. GET /user with its token returns 200, and the X-OAuth-Scopes header contains 'repo'.
failure_signatures: No authentication provider 'github' is currently registered.
User did not consent to login.
GitHub sign-in did not complete (...); you can paste a token instead.
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to the pasted-token field with the prefilled token page (existing).
nodes.manual_fix: Sign in through the browser, or create a classic token on the prefilled page and paste it.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code's GitHub OAuth app switching to expiring user tokens, after which the copy on the grid would stop working within hours. Organisation OAuth-app restrictions could block VS Code's app on the lab organisation. Whether signing out of GitHub in VS Code revokes the copy is not known.

nodes.title: GitHub token present and accepted
nodes.assumption: A GitHub token is on the laptop, either gho_ from the sign-in or a pasted ghp_ or github_pat_ token. GET /user returns 200 with a login, and the token can push to the lab's repositories. The paste pattern accepts only ghp_ and github_pat_, so a pasted `gh auth token` value (gho_) is refused.
nodes.check: On the laptop: validateToken(github) succeeds and returns the login; a network failure counts as WARN, and the grid then verifies. Scopes: X-OAuth-Scopes includes 'repo'. Fine-grained tokens send no such header, so for them `GET /repos/<owner>/<repo>` must show permissions.push true. On the grid: `ashley verify-tokens` prints 'GITHUB_TOKEN ok (<login>)' (diag id grid.token-github).
failure_signatures: no longer accepted (the service rejected it (HTTP 401)): press Renew
That does not look like the right kind of token.
GITHUB_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
remote: Permission to <owner>/<repo>.git denied to <login>.
Resource protected by organization SAML enforcement
nodes.auto_repair: Renew through VS Code's GitHub sign-in (one click); pushTokens() then updates the grid. The daily checkTokensQuietly() already offers this.
nodes.manual_fix: Renew the token. For organisation repositories, ask an owner to approve VS Code's OAuth app, or create a fine-grained token with Contents: read and write.
nodes.future_risk: Deprecation of classic PATs; organisation token-lifetime policies (fine-grained tokens pending approval, a 366-day default); prefix changes.

nodes.title: Hugging Face token present, accepted and writable
nodes.assumption: An hf_ token with the write role is on the laptop, and whoami-v2 returns 200 with a name. Neither the laptop nor the grid checks the role, so a read token passes validation and only fails later, on upload.
nodes.check: On the laptop: validateToken(huggingface) succeeds, and in the whoami-v2 JSON auth.accessToken.role is 'write', or 'fineGrained' with write access to the repositories. On the grid: 'HF_TOKEN ok (<name>)' (diag id grid.token-hf).
failure_signatures: the service rejected it (HTTP 401)
HF_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
403 Forbidden: You don't have the rights to create a model under this namespace
HTTP 429
nodes.auto_repair: On a 429 or a timeout, retry once after 60 s. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Create a Write token on the prefilled page (name wsu-grid) and copy it; the panel picks it up.
nodes.future_risk: Hugging Face changing token types, the rate limits on whoami, or the query parameters of the token page.

nodes.title: Claude Pro or Max subscription on the student's own account
nodes.assumption: The student holds Claude Pro or Max; setup-token is issued only for Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise. By lab convention the account was made with AccessID@wayne.edu, but nothing verifies the e-mail: the admin queue says 'Claude account (assumed) <id>@wayne.edu'. One person, one token.
nodes.check: Ground truth that does not depend on the validator: a trivial worker request (`ashley ask`, mode plan, max_turns 1) returns status ok with account 'default'. Optionally, GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with the token and 'anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20' returns five_hour and seven_day windows (documented in RESEARCH.md, not used in the code). Otherwise report WARN 'unverified'.
failure_signatures: no enabled Claude account
rate_limited with retry_after soon after the worker starts
setup-token refuses a free plan (the exact message was not recorded)
nodes.manual_fix: Subscribe to Claude Pro (the minimum) with the WSU e-mail account, then run the Claude step again.
nodes.future_risk: Plan changes (setup-token limited to higher tiers); changes to the Consumer Terms on automated use of a subscription.

nodes.title: Claude Code extension and its bundled CLI
nodes.assumption: anthropic.claude-code is installed and signed in to Pro or Max, and its CLI lives at <extensionPath>/resources/native-binary/claude(.exe). If that path is missing, findClaudeExecutable() falls back to 'claude' on PATH, which students usually do not have. The extension reads user-scope MCP servers from the same configuration as the CLI.
nodes.check: In the extension host: vscode.extensions.getExtension('anthropic.claude-code') is defined (log its version), the native-binary path exists, and `& <claude.exe> --version` prints '<x.y.z> (Claude Code)'.
failure_signatures: WARN  Claude Code extension not installed
the Claude Code extension (signed in to Claude Pro or Max) (in the lab-access missing list)
spawn claude ENOENT
nodes.auto_repair: Run workbench.extensions.installExtension for anthropic.claude-code; this asks the user.
nodes.manual_fix: Install Claude Code from the Marketplace and sign in with the Pro or Max account.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic moving the native binary inside the extension, after which the fallback silently looks for a 'claude' that is not there; CLI subcommands being renamed.

nodes.title: Terminal shell integration (token capture)
nodes.assumption: A new hidden integrated terminal activates shell integration within 6 s (terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled and a supported shell). TerminalShellIntegration.executeCommand() and execution.read() can then stream the output of setup-token. These APIs need VS Code 1.100 or newer, which the engines field requires.
nodes.check: In the extension host: create a hidden terminal and wait at most 6 s for onDidChangeTerminalShellIntegration. The setting terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled must be true.
failure_signatures: This terminal has no shell integration; the token will be picked up from your clipboard instead.
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to a visible terminal plus clipboard detection (existing).
nodes.manual_fix: Copy the printed token and paste it into the panel.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to VS Code's shell-integration API; PowerShell execution-policy or profile changes that break the injection.

nodes.title: Clipboard readable for picking up tokens
nodes.assumption: vscode.env.clipboard.readText() works. While a token field is open, the clipboard is polled every second, and a value matching the service's pattern is offered with 'Use it'.
nodes.check: In the extension host: save the current clipboard, writeText(probe), confirm readText() returns the probe, then restore the original content.
failure_signatures: the panel never offers the copied token (troubleshooting table)
nodes.manual_fix: Paste the token into the field.
nodes.future_risk: Operating-system privacy limits on background clipboard reads (macOS paste notices, Wayland).

nodes.title: claude setup-token mints the token and hands it over
nodes.assumption: `claude setup-token` needs a TTY (it prints nothing without one; probed), opens claude.ai in the browser for Authorize, and prints a one-year sk-ant-oat... token. The panel runs it in a hidden terminal and captures the first match of /sk-ant-oat[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}/ in the stream after stripping ANSI codes. This has not been run with a real Authorize click. If the CLI's renderer hard-wraps the long token at the terminal width, the match stops at the wrap and a truncated token is stored, which would show up as HTTP 401. Not verified.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `& <claude.exe> setup-token --help` exits 0. After a capture, the token validates (account.claude-oauth-token) and its length equals that of the token printed in the terminal.
failure_signatures: If the browser page shows a code, paste it into the terminal that just opened below.
'Token captured from the terminal.' followed by 'the service rejected it (HTTP 401)'
spawn <path>/claude.exe ENOENT
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to clipboard capture (existing). Candidate code fix: remove line breaks inside the match window before applying the pattern.
nodes.manual_fix: Run `claude setup-token` in any terminal, copy the whole token and paste it into the panel.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code renaming setup-token, changing the token prefix or the flow (for example a device code), or moving the native binary.

nodes.title: Claude subscription token accepted on the laptop and the grid
nodes.assumption: The sk-ant-oat token counts as valid when GET /v1/models with Bearer, 'anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20' and anthropic-version returns 200. NOT KNOWN: no 200 has been recorded for a real setup-token, and the access review asked for one. The laptop refuses the token on 401 or 403. The grid passes it only on 200, and `access requirements` blocks on anything else. So if this endpoint answers valid subscription tokens with 403 or 400, every student is refused at the last step and the laptop rejects good tokens. The grid copy is ~/.ashley/accounts/default/token (mode 600). The token lasts one year, and revocation has been reported to take 3 to 4 days.
nodes.check: On the laptop, validateToken(claudeOauth) succeeds. On the grid, `ashley verify-tokens | grep ^CLAUDE_TOKEN` prints 'CLAUDE_TOKEN ok (subscription token accepted)' (diag id grid.token-claude). Independent ground truth: a trivial worker request returns status ok without 'Failed to authenticate'. Record all three results. If the validator says no and the worker run says yes, the validator is wrong.
failure_signatures: CLAUDE_TOKEN rejected (invalid, expired or revoked: run claude setup-token again)
CLAUDE_TOKEN present (the check answered HTTP <code>)
the Claude token could not be confirmed right now (...); try again in a minute
OAuth access token is invalid
Failed to authenticate
the service rejected it (HTTP 403)
nodes.auto_repair: Nothing for an invalid token. When the validator and the worker disagree, trust the worker run and flag services.ts:66 and grid/ashley:807 for an update.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the Claude step again (Authorize in the browser), then Install on the grid to push the new token.
nodes.future_risk: High: the beta header retired, /v1/models restricted for OAuth tokens, and the yearly expiry (the token must be renewed every year).

nodes.title: Optional Anthropic API key (overflow)
nodes.assumption: An optional sk-ant-api key. Since wizard v2 it is no longer a wizard step; it is set through Manage tokens. GET /v1/models with X-Api-Key returns 200. On the grid it is stored at ~/.ashley/accounts/apikey/apikey (mode 600). It is never injected into laptop terminals, and the grid's verify-tokens does not check it.
nodes.check: Skip when not set. On the laptop, validateToken(anthropicApiKey) succeeds. On the grid, `stat -c %a ~/.ashley/accounts/apikey/apikey` prints 600, and `ashley status --json` lists 'apikey' among the accounts.
failure_signatures: the service rejected it (HTTP 401)
invalid x-api-key
credit balance is too low
nodes.manual_fix: Create a key with a spending limit in the Anthropic Console, or leave it unset.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to the Console URL (console.anthropic.com may redirect) or to billing policy.

nodes.title: Tokens and grid variables in local terminals
nodes.assumption: The persistent environmentVariableCollection puts WSU_ACCESS_ID, ASHLEY_GRID and ASHLEY_GRID_HOME into new integrated terminals, plus GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and HF_TOKEN while ashley.injectTokensIntoTerminals is true. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are never injected, because the local Claude Code would then bill the key. VS Code caches a persistent collection in its own storage. Whether the token values sit there in clear text was not checked, so the statement 'tokens live only in the keychain' may not be exact.
nodes.check: In a new VS Code terminal (PowerShell): `[bool]$env:GITHUB_TOKEN; [bool]$env:HF_TOKEN; [bool]$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` prints True, True, False. Never print the values.
failure_signatures: git or huggingface-cli unauthenticated in a terminal
the local Claude Code reports API billing (an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set elsewhere)
a terminal banner asking to relaunch for environment changes
nodes.auto_repair: Run store.hydrateEnvironment() (idempotent), then relaunch the terminals.
nodes.manual_fix: Open a new terminal.
nodes.future_risk: Changes to how EnvironmentVariableCollection persists or is scoped.

nodes.title: Tokens copied to the grid (names match)
nodes.assumption: pushTokens() writes ~/.ashley/secrets.env (GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, HF_TOKEN; the whole file is overwritten each time), ~/.ashley/accounts/default/token and accounts/apikey/apikey. It sends them over ssh stdin with umask 077, never on the command line. `ashley status --json` lists the NAMES of the secrets and accounts, so the laptop can compare.
nodes.check: On the laptop: in the output of `ssh wsu-grid "~/.ashley/bin/ashley status --json"`, .secrets contains GITHUB_TOKEN and HF_TOKEN whenever the laptop has those tokens, and .accounts contains 'default' (oauth-token). On the login node: `stat -c %a ~/.ashley/secrets.env ~/.ashley/accounts/default/token` prints 600 600.
failure_signatures: grid is missing: GitHub token, Hugging Face token, Claude token
writing secrets.env: ...
writing the Claude token: ...
; the grid copy was not updated (...)
secrets.env missing (GitHub / Hugging Face tokens for the worker)
nodes.auto_repair: Run pushTokens() again. It is idempotent and uses stdin only, so it is safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Run Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid.
nodes.future_risk: Because the whole file is overwritten, any other variable a student or lead adds to secrets.env (for example an NCBI key) is lost. A full home quota makes the write fail.

nodes.title: Login node HTTPS egress and CA trust
nodes.assumption: The login node reaches api.github.com, huggingface.co, api.anthropic.com and github.com over HTTPS, and CentOS 7's curl (7.29, built on NSS) trusts their current certificate chains through its ca-certificates bundle. CentOS 7 is past end of life, so that trust store only gets older.
nodes.check: On the login node: `curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.github.com/zen https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models` prints 200, 401, 401, never 000. Log `curl --version | head -1` and `rpm -q ca-certificates`. The corresponding diag id is grid.internet.
failure_signatures: Peer's Certificate issuer is not recognized.
SSL connect error
Could not resolve host
HF_TOKEN rejected or unreachable while the laptop verifies the same token
CLAUDE_TOKEN present (the check answered HTTP 000)
nodes.auto_repair: Verify through an independent path instead: run the same curl inside the worker container, which has Debian 12's CA store, with `srun --jobid <worker> --overlap -n1`. This is cheap, runs on the compute node and is safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Tell hpc@wayne.edu that the ca-certificates or egress need attention. Meanwhile rely on the laptop's verification.
nodes.future_risk: High. A CA root rotation by any of the three vendors breaks an unpatched CentOS 7 trust store. C&IT could also close egress from the login node. An OS migration would fix both.

nodes.title: curl reads secret headers from stdin (-K -)
nodes.assumption: `curl -K -` reads 'header = "..."' and 'url = "..."' lines from stdin, so tokens never appear in the login node's process list; three verify runs were sampled and none was visible. The -w '%{http_code}' and -m options work.
nodes.check: On the login node: `printf 'header = "X-Ashley-Diag: 1"\n' | curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -K - https://api.github.com/zen` prints 200. While verify-tokens runs, `ps -u $USER -o args | grep -c Bearer` counts 0.
failure_signatures: 000 or an empty status code
a curl warning about the config read from stdin
a token visible in ps output
nodes.auto_repair: None. Never fall back to passing the token on the command line.
nodes.manual_fix: Escalate; token verification on the grid has to wait.
nodes.future_risk: curl replaced by a wrapper, or by a module version that parses config files differently.

nodes.title: Grid-side token verification and its parser
nodes.assumption: `ashley verify-tokens` prints one line per token in a fixed vocabulary. HF_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN: 'ok (<name>)', 'rejected or unreachable' or 'missing'. CLAUDE_TOKEN: 'ok', 'rejected', 'present (HTTP <code>)' or 'missing'. `access requirements` and `ashley diag` grep these lines. For HF and GitHub, 'rejected' and 'unreachable' are one message, so a 429 or a network failure reads as a bad token.
nodes.check: On the login node: `~/.ashley/bin/ashley verify-tokens` prints three lines starting with HF_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN and CLAUDE_TOKEN. Compare each with the laptop's validateToken() for the same token, which is an independent path. A disagreement points to the parser, egress or a rate limit, not to the token.
failure_signatures: no secrets.env
HF_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
GITHUB_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
Hugging Face token missing or rejected
GitHub token missing or rejected
nodes.auto_repair: When the laptop says the token is fine, retry once after 60 s (rate limit or a passing egress problem). Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Renew only a token that the laptop also rejects.
nodes.future_risk: Vendors changing their JSON formatting breaks the grep parsing. 401 and network errors remain indistinguishable.

nodes.title: Lab-access request as a held Slurm job the admin can see
nodes.assumption: A request is `sbatch --parsable --hold -J ashley_access -p reqp -q requeue -t 1 -n 1 --mem=16M -o /dev/null --comment 'ashley-access v1 note=...'`. The admin's `squeue -h -n ashley_access -t PD -o '%i|%u|%k|%V'` must see every user's pending jobs and their comments, so PrivateData must not include jobs. The site must not purge held jobs before the admin reads them.
nodes.check: On the login node: `scontrol show config | grep -i PrivateData` shows no 'jobs' in the value. The grid diag grid.slurm-visibility tests for '= none', which also flags harmless values such as 'usage'. After a student files a request, `squeue -h -u $USER -n ashley_access -t PD -o %i` returns an id, and the admin sees the same job with its comment in the unfiltered query.
failure_signatures: could not file the request: sbatch: error: ...
Invalid qos specification
Invalid partition name specified
the admin's list stays empty while the student sees 'filed'
the state returns to 'none' (the held job was purged)
nodes.auto_repair: On the student's side, file again only when the state is 'none' and no request job exists (one per user). Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: The admin approves directly with 'Grant a user directly', and asks C&IT about PrivateData and purges of held jobs.
nodes.future_risk: A Slurm upgrade enabling PrivateData=jobs; the reqp partition or the requeue QoS being renamed; comments trimmed; held jobs reaped automatically.

nodes.title: Lab access granted (shared folder readable)
nodes.assumption: Approval means named-user POSIX ACLs on /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared, set by its owner, the lab admin. The request is refused until every wizard step is done and the Claude, GitHub and Hugging Face tokens verify on the grid. The unix group oschome lives in the university directory and changes only when C&IT acts on the admin's e-mail.
nodes.check: On the laptop, `ssh wsu-grid "~/.ashley/bin/ashley access whoami --json"` shows admin true, or state 'approved' with granted true (diag id grid.lab-access). On the login node, `test -r /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/library.json && echo ok` prints ok. Log `getent group oschome`.
failure_signatures: Waiting for lab access
denied: <message>; ask your lead to reset your request to ask again
approved, but the lab folder is not readable: the admin should run ashley access admin resync
not yet: <missing items>
finish the setup first; requests are for working environments
nodes.auto_repair: When access is granted but the container has not been adopted, run `ashley install`, which adopts the lab container in a second. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: The lead approves the request in Ashley: Lab access. For group membership, the admin page drafts the e-mail to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: A change in who owns shared/ (the admin is detected with `stat -c %U`); changes in how CephFS handles ACLs; self-service groups at C&IT.

nodes.title: A Node runtime for the MCP server
nodes.assumption: The MCP server runs under the system node if `node --version` matches /^v(2[0-9]|[3-9][0-9])\./ (version 20 or newer), otherwise under VS Code's own executable (process.execPath) with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, which needs Electron's RunAsNode fuse on. Confirmed: Code.exe works as a Node 24 runtime. The absolute path of Code.exe is written into the registration.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `node --version` shows 20 or newer, or PowerShell `$env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1; & '<Code.exe>' -e 'console.log(process.versions.node)'` prints a version of 20 or newer. Remove the variable afterwards.
failure_signatures: Claude Code shows the server 'ashley' as failed to connect
Code.exe opens a window instead of running the script (RunAsNode disabled)
the registered command path no longer exists after a VS Code update
nodes.auto_repair: Register again with the other runtime (system node instead of Electron, or the reverse): `claude mcp remove --scope user ashley`, then add-json. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Install Node 22 LTS, then run Ashley: Connect the Claude Code extension to the grid.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code disabling the RunAsNode fuse, or moving Code.exe into versioned folders, which strands the stored absolute path.

nodes.title: MCP bridge registered with Claude Code
nodes.assumption: `claude mcp add-json --scope user ashley '<json>'` stores {type stdio, command, args [<extensionPath>/dist/mcp-server.js], env {ASHLEY_GRID, ASHLEY_WORKER, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE when needed}}. The fallback writes <workspace>/.mcp.json, which Claude Code asks once to approve. isMcpRegistered() checks only that `claude mcp get ashley` exits 0 and mentions ashley. It does not check that the path exists or that the server connects.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `& <claude.exe> mcp get ashley` exits 0 and reports the server as connected. The args path it prints exists (Test-Path) and lies under the CURRENTLY installed Ashley extension folder, whose version matches package.json.
failure_signatures: add-json refuses on a second registration (a duplicate name; likely), after which the code writes a project .mcp.json instead of replacing the user entry
No MCP server found with name: ashley
Failed to connect, after an extension update deleted the old extension folder: isMcpRegistered() still returns true, so setup never registers again
registration saved with its backslashes mangled (C:UsersgregoAppData...)
a project .mcp.json waiting for approval
nodes.auto_repair: Run `claude mcp remove --scope user ashley`, then add-json with the current extension path and runtime, spawned with an argv array (no shell). Safe and idempotent.
nodes.manual_fix: Run Ashley: Connect the Claude Code extension to the grid, then start a new Claude Code conversation.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code renaming the mcp subcommands or the --scope values, moving its configuration file, or changing MCP transports.

nodes.title: The MCP server starts and reaches the grid
nodes.assumption: dist/mcp-server.js (bundling @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.1 and zod 4.6.5) speaks MCP over stdio in a protocol version that the installed Claude Code accepts. It inherits a PATH on which `ssh` resolves, ASHLEY_GRID names a working alias, and it keeps one GridRelay open for its lifetime.
nodes.check: On the laptop, from Node or Git Bash (LF only): pipe one initialize request into the registered command: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"diag","version":"0"}}}. Pass = a response line whose serverInfo.name is 'ashley'. End to end: Claude Code's ashley_status tool returns JSON containing 'ready'.
failure_signatures: ashley mcp server failed: ...
{"ready":false,"error":"Ashley is not installed on the grid yet"}
relay closed (ssh exit 255) on the server's stderr
an MCP protocol-version error from Claude Code
nodes.auto_repair: Register again (the repair of vscode.mcp-registration).
nodes.manual_fix: Update the Ashley VSIX when Claude Code moves to a newer MCP protocol.
nodes.future_risk: MCP protocol bumps in Claude Code outpacing the bundled SDK; on macOS, processes launched from the GUI may lack /usr/bin on PATH.

nodes.title: Compute nodes reach the internet services Claude needs
nodes.assumption: From inside jobs, nodes reach api.anthropic.com (Claude), registry.npmjs.org (the Claude Code install), registry-1.docker.io (the sandbox build), github.com and huggingface.co. Nothing inbound is needed; the laptop never reaches a node.
nodes.check: On a compute node only, inside a running worker allocation, and slow: `srun --jobid <worker job> --overlap -n1 curl -s -m 8 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' https://api.anthropic.com/ https://registry.npmjs.org/ https://github.com https://huggingface.co`. Pass = no 000. The bootstrap smoke line already records net=<code>, and `ashley diag --node` checks api.anthropic.com as node.probe.
failure_signatures: net=000 in the bootstrap log
STOP: npm install failed
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.anthropic.com
Connection error (in a worker result)
TLS handshake timeout (docker pull)
nodes.auto_repair: If one node fails and others work, resubmit the worker (safe). Otherwise nothing.
nodes.manual_fix: Report to hpc@wayne.edu, naming the node.
nodes.future_risk: Nodes placed behind an HTTP proxy (HTTPS_PROXY would then have to reach the container); Docker Hub limits on anonymous pulls.

nodes.title: Phone access through Claude Remote Control on the worker
nodes.assumption: Remote Control accepts only a full claude.ai login; setup-tokens and API keys are refused. So phone.js keeps a separate login in ~/.ashley/remote/config, obtained by running `claude auth login` in a pty (util-linux `script` inside the container) with the paste-code flow: the laptop opens the link, the student copies the code, and `ashley phone code` delivers it on stdin. `claude remote-control` then runs in a pre-trusted folder with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC unset, using outbound HTTPS only. The login lasts about 30 days.
nodes.check: On the laptop, `ssh wsu-grid "~/.ashley/bin/ashley phone status --worker default --json"` shows job_running true, status.phase 'running' and a session_url. On the compute node, `command -v script` succeeds inside the container (the diag node.probe requires 'script-ok').
failure_signatures: three sign-in attempts did not work; turn phone access off and on to try again
Claude did not accept that code: copy the whole code from the page (it is long) and send it again
the phone sign-in expired; sign in again
Remote Control stopped (exit N); restarting in N s
Phone access did not start: no answer from the worker
nodes.auto_repair: Run `ashley phone off`, then `on`, to restart the flow (safe). The worker already restarts Remote Control with backoff.
nodes.manual_fix: Run Ashley: Phone access again, sign in with the Claude account made with the WSU e-mail, and copy the whole code.
nodes.future_risk: Remote Control's prompts, the trust-dialog key (hasTrustDialogAccepted), URL formats (claude.ai versus claude.com), plan requirements or the paste-code login flow changing; `script` missing from a new container image.

nodes.title: git on the login node can push to github.com over HTTPS
nodes.assumption: The login node's git can clone a bundle made by a modern git, use an in-memory credential helper (`!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo password=$GITHUB_TOKEN; }; f`) and negotiate TLS with github.com. CentOS 7 ships git 1.8.3.1; the version on warrior was not recorded. A bearer token passed through http.extraheader was refused.
nodes.check: On the login node: `git --version`, then `git ls-remote https://github.com/git/git.git HEAD` prints one hash line (anonymous and cheap).
failure_signatures: fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/...': Peer's Certificate issuer is not recognized.
error: RPC failed
SSL connect error
the bundle is refused as unsupported (a bundle version mismatch)
nodes.auto_repair: Run the push inside the worker container, which has Debian 12's git, with `srun --jobid <worker> --overlap` instead of on the login node. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Load a newer git module if C&IT provides one (`module avail git`), or push from the laptop.
nodes.future_risk: GitHub tightening its TLS, ciphers or protocol requirements beyond what an unpatched CentOS 7 git and libcurl can do; changes to the bundle format in modern git.

nodes.title: Pushing the Ashley repository to GitHub through the grid
nodes.assumption: tools/push_via_grid.sh is the only way to push: the laptop checkout has no git remote configured. The script runs `git bundle create --all`, copies the bundle to ~/ashley.bundle with scp, then runs `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'bash -lc ...'`. On the grid it clones the bundle into ~/ashley-repo, checks out main, and pushes main and the tags to https://github.com/GregorySchwing/ashley.git. The token is GITHUB_TOKEN from the LOGIN environment, that is Greg's shell startup files, not ~/.ashley/secrets.env. The remote command ends with `| tail -3; rm -f ~/ashley.bundle` and has no pipefail, so the script exits 0 even when the push fails.
nodes.check: Before: on the laptop, `git rev-parse --verify main`; on the login node, `bash -lc 'test -n "$GITHUB_TOKEN" && echo set'` prints set.
