After, outside the script: on the login node, `git ls-remote https://github.com/GregorySchwing/ashley.git refs/heads/main` (with the same credential helper) must equal the laptop's `git rev-parse main`.
failure_signatures: no GITHUB_TOKEN in the grid login environment
remote: Permission to GregorySchwing/ashley.git denied to <login>.
fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/GregorySchwing/ashley.git/'
error: src refspec main does not match any
remote: Repository not found. (after a move to OpenSpineConsortium)
the script prints three lines of git output and exits 0 although nothing was pushed
nodes.auto_repair: When the login environment lacks GITHUB_TOKEN, source ~/.ashley/secrets.env inside the same remote shell; it is the user's own mode-600 file and is never printed. Always finish with the ls-remote comparison and exit non-zero on a mismatch.
nodes.manual_fix: When the repository moves, pass its URL as $1. Export a repo-scoped token in the grid login environment, or run the GitHub token step. If Windows sockets are flaky, run the script from WSL, which needs its own ssh key and config because the WSL mirror was removed.
nodes.future_risk: Fine-grained token expiry and organisation approval ('pending') once the repository moves to OpenSpineConsortium, where Greg's grid token is not a member; the old git on the login node.

nodes.title: Wayne State help and app links still resolve
nodes.assumption: The URLs the wizard opens still resolve: https://tech.wayne.edu/kb/high-performance-computing (account request), https://services.wayne.edu/TDClient/277/Portal/KB/Article/20242 (Authenticator guide), https://ondemand.grid.wayne.edu/ (campus or VPN only), and the App Store (id388497605) and Play Store (com.google.android.apps.authenticator2) pages for Google Authenticator. The contacts are hpc@wayne.edu and 313-577-4743.
nodes.check: On the laptop, weekly: `curl.exe -s -o NUL -L -m 10 -w "%{http_code}" <url>` returns 200 for each. Check OnDemand only when network.campus-vpn-ondemand passes.
failure_signatures: 404 Not Found
a redirect to a generic knowledge-base landing page
students stuck at 'Grid account and Authenticator'
nodes.manual_fix: Update the constants in wizard.ts:88-92 and publish a new VSIX.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT knowledge-base migrations renumbering TDClient articles; app-store identifiers changing.

nodes.title: Token creation pages and their prefilled fields
nodes.assumption: These pages open with their fields prefilled: https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?description=Ashley%20WSU%20grid&scopes=repo,workflow,read:org,gist, https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens/new?tokenType=write&name=wsu-grid, and https://console.anthropic.com/settings/keys.
nodes.check: On the laptop: `curl.exe -s -o NUL -L -m 10 -w "%{http_code}"` on each returns 200; a login page counts. When a vendor changes its interface, a person confirms the prefill.
failure_signatures: the page opens with empty fields
a redirect to a different console domain
nodes.manual_fix: Update tokenUrl in services.ts and rebuild.
nodes.future_risk: GitHub retiring the classic-token page; Hugging Face ignoring the query parameters; Anthropic changing the Console domain.

nodes.title: Service status of GitHub, Hugging Face and Anthropic
nodes.assumption: A 5xx, a 429 or a network error from a vendor means 'cannot verify now', not 'bad token'. The laptop treats it that way (network:true). The grid's `access requirements`, however, blocks on anything other than 'ok', so an outage blocks lab-access requests.
nodes.check: On the laptop: status.indicator is 'none' in https://www.githubstatus.com/api/v2/status.json and in Anthropic's Statuspage (https://status.anthropic.com/api/v2/status.json), and the Hugging Face status page is reachable. Informational only: report WARN at most.
failure_signatures: HTTP 500, 502 or 503 from validateToken
HTTP 529 overloaded_error
CLAUDE_TOKEN present (the check answered HTTP 5xx)
nodes.auto_repair: Retry with backoff. Safe.
nodes.manual_fix: Wait for the outage to end, and do not renew tokens during it.
nodes.future_risk: The status-page URLs moving.

nodes.title: Grid maintenance or outage
nodes.assumption: When the login node refuses connections or times out from every network, including the VPN, while the rest of the internet works, or when Slurm answers 'Unable to contact slurm controller', the cause is a C&IT maintenance window or an outage, not the student's setup. Queued requests survive, because they are files.
nodes.check: On the laptop: TCP 22 to warrior fails AND https://www.wayne.edu answers AND, on the VPN, OnDemand also fails; together these mean maintenance is likely. When the login node is reachable: `scontrol ping` prints 'Slurmctld(primary) at ... is UP'.
failure_signatures: slurm_load_jobs error: Unable to contact slurm controller (connect failure)
sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Unable to contact slurm controller (connect failure)
ssh: connect to host warrior.grid.wayne.edu port 22: Connection refused
nodes.manual_fix: Wait, and check C&IT's announcements or write to hpc@wayne.edu. Nothing on the laptop needs to change.
nodes.future_risk: Major maintenance windows are when the OS, sshd, host keys, module names and paths change together, so run the full troubleshooter afterwards.

nodes.title: Grid login shell is bash
nodes.assumption: The AccessID's passwd shell is /bin/bash. Every laptop call is `ssh wsu-grid -- '<single-quoted argv>'`, and the remote login shell runs it: it expands the unquoted leading `~/`, and pushTokens and GridApi.sbatch run `bash -c '...'`. Because the shell is Red Hat bash, ~/.bashrc is sourced for these non-interactive commands, which puts ~/.ashley/bin and the VS Code sysroot variables in place.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'getent passwd "$USER" | cut -d: -f7; echo $BASH_VERSION'`. Pass = `/bin/bash` and a version >= 4.2.
failure_signatures: Illegal variable name.
Unmatched '.
bash: -c: line 0: unexpected EOF while looking for matching
Remote-SSH exit code 207 (bashrc block never sourced under tcsh/zsh)
nodes.manual_fix: Ask C&IT (hpc@wayne.edu) to set the login shell to /bin/bash. Ashley supports no other login shell.
nodes.future_risk: Low. An identity-management migration could reset login shells to a site default.

nodes.title: Slurm association allows reqp/requeue, secp/secondary (and gpu)
nodes.assumption: The account has a Slurm association and a default account that allow partition reqp with QoS requeue, and secp with QoS secondary. reqp/requeue is hard-coded in bootstrap.sbatch, as the worker default and on the held access-request job. GPU users also need QoS gpu on gmsap/gvohp/galhp.
nodes.check: login node: `sacctmgr -nP show assoc user=$USER format=account,partition,qos` and `sacctmgr -nP show user $USER format=defaultaccount`. Cheap proof: `sbatch --test-only -p reqp -q requeue -t 1 --mem=16M --wrap true 2>&1` prints 'to start at'. Run the same test for secp/secondary.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Invalid account or account/partition combination specified
sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Invalid qos specification
Job's QOS not permitted to use this partition
ashley: could not file the request: sbatch: error:
ashley: sbatch failed:
nodes.auto_repair: The held access-request job never runs. If reqp/requeue refuses it, resubmit it on secp/secondary. No other repair.
nodes.manual_fix: The student emails hpc@wayne.edu, naming their sponsor, to ask for reqp/requeue and secp/secondary (and gpu if needed).
nodes.future_risk: C&IT renames or consolidates QoS (requeue/secondary/primary/gpu) or partitions, or moves to per-lab accounts instead of per-user defaults. Every hard-coded pair then fails at submit.

nodes.title: oschome unix group (university directory via SSSD)
nodes.assumption: The lab admin and members of the oschome unix group read the shared tree through group bits (2750, g+rX). Students outside the group rely on per-user ACLs. C&IT, not Ashley, maintains group membership (sss, not /etc/group).
nodes.check: login node: `getent group oschome` and `id -nG | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx oschome && echo member`.
failure_signatures: getent group oschome returns nothing
no shared library readable at /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley (ask your lead for the oschome group)
nodes.manual_fix: The admin emails hpc@wayne.edu with the AccessIDs to add (the admin page drafts this email). Until then an ACL approval gives access.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT renames the group or changes the SSSD configuration (enumeration, caching). The group also expires if the CephFS allocation lapses.

nodes.title: Login sshd accepts a public key alone (BatchMode, no OTP)
nodes.assumption: sshd on warrior accepts publickey authentication without a password or Authenticator code. Every Ashley call can then run with BatchMode=yes, ConnectTimeout=20, MACs=+hmac-sha1, AddressFamily=inet and GSSAPIAuthentication=no. The OTP is typed only once, to install the key.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 -o MACs=+hmac-sha1 -o AddressFamily=inet wsu-grid hostname`. Pass = exit 0 and 'warrior' within about 5 s.
failure_signatures: Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive).
no matching MAC found. Their offer: hmac-sha1
Connection timed out during banner exchange
kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer
the grid does not accept the key yet
nodes.auto_repair: On a MAC or IPv6 symptom, rewrite the ssh config block (wizard step sshConfig). On a publickey refusal while the host answers, rerun wizard step installKey (one interactive password+OTP).
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard's 'Install key' step again; check the key line ends with 'ashley' in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.
nodes.future_risk: High. If C&IT sets AuthenticationMethods publickey,keyboard-interactive (2FA on keys), every BatchMode call fails. Recovery would need one interactive login per day held open (Windows OpenSSH has no ControlMaster; the in-panel ssh2 client could hold it). Dropping hmac-sha1 on the server is harmless, since +hmac-sha1 only appends. A laptop OpenSSH that removes hmac-sha1 while the grid offers nothing else breaks every call.

nodes.title: authorized_keys holds the ashley key with StrictModes-safe permissions
nodes.assumption: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys contains the ashley public key, and sshd StrictModes is satisfied: the home directory is not group- or world-writable, ~/.ssh is 700 and authorized_keys is 600, all owned by the user. The installKey command sets umask 077 for new files but never repairs an existing ~/.ssh.
nodes.check: login node (needs one working login): `stat -c '%a %U %n' ~ ~/.ssh ~/.ssh/authorized_keys; grep -c 'ashley$' ~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Pass = home without g+w/o+w, 700, 600, count >= 1. laptop: BatchMode fails with publickey while the password path works = this node.
failure_signatures: Permission denied (publickey...) after the key step
Authentication refused: bad ownership or modes for directory (sshd log only, invisible to the student)
still prompted:
nodes.auto_repair: Over a working BatchMode session: `chmod go-w ~; chmod 700 ~/.ssh; chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Without one: rerun installKey with those chmods added to its remote command.
nodes.manual_fix: In a grid terminal, run the three chmods and confirm the key line is present.
nodes.future_risk: If C&IT moves keys to a central store (AuthorizedKeysCommand or SSSD sshPublicKey), ~/.ssh/authorized_keys is ignored.

nodes.title: Login host key unchanged since first contact
nodes.assumption: Every call runs with StrictHostKeyChecking and BatchMode, so the host key recorded at first contact (accept-new) must stay valid. The wsu-grid alias must resolve to hosts that present one key set.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh-keygen -F warrior.grid.wayne.edu` finds an entry, and `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` prints no host-key warning.
failure_signatures: WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
Host key verification failed.
nodes.manual_fix: Check the new fingerprint against C&IT's published one (or ask hpc@wayne.edu), then `ssh-keygen -R warrior.grid.wayne.edu` and reconnect. Never accept a changed key automatically.
nodes.future_risk: An EL7 to EL8/9 reinstall of the login node, or a second login node behind the same name, changes the host key for every student on the same day.

nodes.title: Script upload by scp (SFTP mode) into ~/.ashley/bin
nodes.assumption: gridInstall uploads with `scp -q ... wsu-grid:~/.ashley/bin/`. Windows OpenSSH 9.x scp speaks SFTP, so warrior must run the sftp subsystem, and the leading '~/' must map to the home directory even though the EL7 server lacks the expand-path extension.
nodes.check: laptop: `echo 'ls .ashley/bin' | sftp -b - -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid` lists the six files, or `scp -q wsu-grid:~/.ashley/bin/VERSION <tmpfile>` succeeds.
failure_signatures: subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed
Received message too long
upload failed:
nodes.auto_repair: Retry with `scp -O` (legacy protocol). If that also fails, stream each file through `ssh wsu-grid 'cat > ~/.ashley/bin/<f>'` on stdin and chmod afterwards.
nodes.manual_fix: Upload with `scp -O` from a terminal, then run `~/.ashley/bin/ashley install`.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT disables the sftp subsystem, or a future OpenSSH client removes legacy `scp -O`.

nodes.title: ~/.bashrc prints nothing for non-interactive ssh
nodes.assumption: Red Hat bash sources ~/.bashrc for every non-interactive ssh command, so ~/.bashrc must write nothing to stdout. Output corrupts sftp/scp. It also lands before READY and JSON lines: parseLastJson and the relay tolerate leading noise, but scp does not.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true | wc -c`. Pass = 0.
failure_signatures: Received message too long 1349281121
protocol error: mtime.sec not present
status did not return JSON
installed scripts did not answer
nodes.auto_repair: The file belongs to the student, so nothing is written automatically. The resolver can show the noisy lines and propose wrapping them in `if [[ $- == *i* ]]; then ... fi`, applied only on confirmation.
nodes.manual_fix: Move echo, module load and conda activate output inside an interactive-only guard.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT adds a banner to /etc/bashrc, or a module system that prints on load.

nodes.title: Ashley block in ~/.bashrc matches bashrc.block
nodes.assumption: ~/.bashrc carries exactly one '# >>> ashley' ... '# <<< ashley' block, identical to ~/.ashley/bin/bashrc.block (the VS Code glibc sysroot variables plus PATH to ~/.ashley/bin). `ashley install` rewrites it idempotently by its markers, `ashley uninstall` removes it, and `access requirements` refuses to pass without it.
nodes.check: login node: `grep -c '^# >>> ashley' ~/.bashrc` = 1, and `diff <(sed -n '/^# >>> ashley/,/^# <<< ashley/p' ~/.bashrc) ~/.ashley/bin/bashrc.block` is empty.
failure_signatures: FAIL  bashrc block missing: run ashley install
bashrc block missing (run the grid step again)
ashley: command not found (in a grid shell)
nodes.auto_repair: `ssh wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley install'` rewrites the block by its markers.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: Once the grid runs EL8+, C&IT may retire the sysroot and the block would point at missing files, so it must be versioned out. If VS Code renames the variables, the block silently stops working.

nodes.title: Block is sourced for non-interactive ssh (no earlier return guard)
nodes.assumption: Red Hat bash (built with SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC) sources ~/.bashrc for non-interactive ssh on the login node and on compute nodes. No return/exit/exec guard may precede the Ashley block, and cmd_install APPENDS the block at the end, so any earlier guard hides it from Remote-SSH's install script.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'echo "$VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER|$PATH"'` shows a non-empty linker and ~/.ashley/bin in PATH. Repeat on the worker node: `ssh <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu 'echo $VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER'` (needs a running job there). Static check on the login node: `awk '/^# >>> ashley/{exit} /^[^#]*(return|exit|exec )/{print NR": "$0}' ~/.bashrc` is empty.
failure_signatures: exit code 207
found GLIBC 2.17
The remote host may not meet VS Code Server's prerequisites for glibc and libstdc++
ashley: command not found
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the block at the TOP of ~/.bashrc, before any guard. This is safe because the block only exports variables.
nodes.manual_fix: Move the block above any `[ -z "$PS1" ] && return` line.
nodes.future_risk: A C&IT /etc/bashrc that exits early for non-interactive shells, a distro whose bash lacks SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC, or Remote-SSH starting a login shell that reads ~/.bash_profile instead.

nodes.title: C&IT VS Code glibc sysroot present and sufficient on compute nodes
nodes.assumption: /wsu/apps/vscode/sysroot/x86_64-linux-gnu/x86_64-linux-gnu/sysroot/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, with its lib and lib64 directories, exists on every compute node VS Code connects to. Its glibc (>= 2.28) and libstdc++ (>= GLIBCXX_3.4.25) must meet the current VS Code server floor. The doctor checks only the login node.
nodes.check: login node: `test -e <linker>` (the doctor line). compute node, via `srun --jobid=$(cat ~/.ashley/workers/default/job.id) --overlap -N1 -n1 -t 1`: `<linker> --version | head -1` reports glibc 2.28 or newer.
failure_signatures: FAIL  missing /wsu/apps/vscode/sysroot/x86_64-linux-gnu/x86_64-linux-gnu/sysroot/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (C&IT moved the sysroot?)
exit code 207
version `GLIBC_2.28' not found
version `GLIBCXX_3.4.25' not found
nodes.auto_repair: Probe for a relocated sysroot (`find /wsu/apps/vscode -maxdepth 6 -name ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`), regenerate bashrc.block with the paths found, then run `ashley install`. If nothing is found, there is no automatic repair.
nodes.manual_fix: Check the C&IT KB article 'How to SSH to the Grid in Visual Studio Code' for new paths, or email hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: High. C&IT may version the sysroot path. VS Code may raise its floor past the sysroot's glibc, or drop the VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_* escape. An EL8/9 upgrade makes the sysroot unnecessary.

nodes.title: patchelf 0.19.1 at the versioned C&IT path
nodes.assumption: /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/0.19.1/bin/patchelf exists and runs on compute nodes. The version number is part of the hard-coded path.
nodes.check: compute node (srun --overlap): `/wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/0.19.1/bin/patchelf --version` prints 'patchelf 0.19.1'.
failure_signatures: FAIL  missing /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/0.19.1/bin/patchelf (C&IT moved the sysroot?)
Remote-SSH server fails right after download
nodes.auto_repair: Take the newest `ls -d /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/*/bin/patchelf | sort -V | tail -1`, regenerate the block and run `ashley install`.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask C&IT for the current patchelf path.
nodes.future_risk: A C&IT patchelf upgrade changes the version in the path.

nodes.title: Grid home is /wsu/home/<2>/<4>/<AccessID>
nodes.assumption: The laptop computes the grid home path without asking the grid. It uses that path as the default folder for Remote-SSH and as ASHLEY_GRID_HOME.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'echo $HOME'` equals gridHome(accessId).
failure_signatures: Remote-SSH: folder does not exist
ASHLEY_GRID_HOME points to a missing path
nodes.auto_repair: Replace the computed path with the $HOME the grid reports, and cache it in settings.
nodes.manual_fix: Type the real home path in the folder prompt.
nodes.future_risk: A home-filesystem migration (for example, Panasas retirement) changes the layout.

nodes.title: Home filesystem has room; quota readable
nodes.assumption: The Panasas home under its soft quota holds ~/.ashley: secrets, account dirs (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and transcripts), inboxes, outboxes, events and logs. `pan_quota` prints used and soft GB on the first numeric line after two header lines. If it fails, the code falls back to df.
nodes.check: login node: `pan_quota | awk 'NR>2 && $1 ~ /^[0-9.]+$/ {print $1,$2; exit}'` prints two numbers with used/soft < 0.9, and `touch ~/.ashley/.probe && rm ~/.ashley/.probe` succeeds.
failure_signatures: Disk quota exceeded
home quota 0/0 GB or ?/? GB in doctor
zero-byte secrets.env, state.json or outbox result
nodes.auto_repair: Never deletes automatically. Can offer to prune ~/.ashley/workers/*/outbox/*.events.jsonl older than 30 days, after confirmation.
nodes.manual_fix: Move large files to /rs/rs_grp_oschome/<id>.
nodes.future_risk: If Panasas is retired, pan_quota disappears. df on the home mount then reports the whole filesystem instead of the user quota, so the doctor shows a wrong number and no error.

nodes.title: ~/.ashley coherent between login and compute nodes
nodes.assumption: A file written under ~/.ashley on the login node becomes visible on the worker's node within the 250 ms poll. rename is atomic for .part->.json, .json->.claimed and outbox writes. state.json mtimes are comparable with the login node clock: status marks a worker alive when mtime is within 90 s, and peerNote uses last_beat.
nodes.check: login node with a live worker: `echo $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/state.json) ))` < 20. Clock check: `srun --jobid=<job> --overlap -N1 -n1 -t 1 date +%s` differs from the login `date +%s` by < 2.
failure_signatures: worker job RUNNING but alive=false
queued <id> on worker <w> (job N RUNNING; k waiting) and never answered
a request processed twice
nodes.auto_repair: The filesystem cannot be repaired from here. When only clock skew is at fault, judge liveness by last_beat inside state.json instead of the file mtime.
nodes.manual_fix: Report skew or stale caching to hpc@wayne.edu with the node name.
nodes.future_risk: Moving home to NFS with attribute caching would delay inbox visibility by seconds and make mtime liveness flap. Four readdirs per second per worker on the home filesystem could draw a C&IT complaint.

nodes.title: ~/.ashley/bin/ashley exists, is executable and answers
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/bin/ashley exists, has LF line endings, is executable (home not mounted noexec) and answers `version` with no environment loaded.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley version'` exits 0 and prints an integer.
failure_signatures: No such file or directory (exit 127, shown as 'Ashley is not installed on the grid yet')
Permission denied (exit 126)
/bin/bash^M: bad interpreter
the grid part is not installed yet
nodes.auto_repair: Rerun wizard step gridInstall: mkdir, scp the six files, then `ashley install`, which strips CR and chmods.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: Home remounted noexec.

nodes.title: All grid scripts present, same release, LF endings
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/bin holds ashley, ashleyd.js, bootstrap.sbatch, worker.sbatch.tpl, bashrc.block and VERSION from one release, all with LF endings. access_request.sbatch is created on demand.
nodes.check: login node: `cd ~/.ashley/bin && ls ashley ashleyd.js bootstrap.sbatch worker.sbatch.tpl bashrc.block VERSION && ! grep -l $'\r' ashley *.sbatch *.tpl *.js *.block`. Stronger: compare `sha256sum` of each file with the extension's dist/grid copies.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Batch script contains DOS line breaks (\r\n)
sed: can't read /wsu/home/.../.ashley/bin/worker.sbatch.tpl: No such file or directory
Error: Cannot find module '.../.ashley/bin/ashleyd.js' in slurm_<job>.out
nodes.auto_repair: Re-upload the bundled files, then run `ashley install`.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: A new release adds a file (for example phone.js, which ashleyd.js already tries to require) that gridScriptFiles does not ship.

nodes.title: Grid scripts version equals the extension's bundled version
nodes.assumption: The grid's VERSION equals extension/dist/grid/VERSION. The gridInstall check reports 'todo' on a mismatch, and the relay's READY line carries the version.
nodes.check: laptop: compare `ssh wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley version'` with the extension's dist/grid/VERSION.
failure_signatures: the grid has Ashley v1; this extension brings v2
ashley: unknown command 'X' (ashley help)
nodes.auto_repair: Rerun wizard step gridInstall. Running workers keep the old ashleyd.js until they restart, so offer `worker stop` then `start`.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code auto-updates the extension ahead of the grid scripts, and long-running workers keep executing the previous daemon.

nodes.title: bash >= 4.2 and GNU coreutils on the login node
nodes.assumption: The CLI needs no python, jq or node on the login node. It needs bash >= 4.2 (associative arrays and `read -t 0.25` in relay), GNU coreutils (`date +%s%3N`, `stat -c`, `sed -i`, `sleep 0.5`, `head -c`, `tail -c +N`, `xargs -r`), GNU grep -o, awk getline, getent, hostname and printf %q.
nodes.check: login node: `bash -c 'declare -A a=([x]=1); read -t 0.01 v </dev/null; date +%s%3N; stat -c %Y ~; sleep 0.01; printf %q "a b"; echo ok'`. Pass = a 13-digit millisecond time and 'ok' at the end.
failure_signatures: declare: -A: invalid option
read: 0.25: invalid timeout specification
date prints a literal 3N
stat: illegal option -- c
nodes.manual_fix: Report the host; Ashley requires a GNU userland.
nodes.future_risk: Low for EL8/9 (bash 4.4/5.1). Only a non-GNU userland would break it.

nodes.title: status/library/access --json emit one parseable JSON line
nodes.assumption: `ashley status --json` prints one JSON object as its last stdout line, within the extension's 90 s timeout. Fields: version, ready, awaiting_access, root, runtime, claude_version, container, source, library, bootstrap_job/state, home_*_gb, workers[], accounts[], secrets[], jobs[]. Worker state.json and library.json are embedded raw, so one malformed file breaks the whole object. The same holds for library, worker list, access whoami/status/requirements and admin list with --json.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley status --json' | tail -1 | node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(0,'utf8'))"` exits 0. Parse on the laptop because python3 and jq may be absent on the EL7 login node.
failure_signatures: status did not return JSON
installed scripts did not answer
Cannot reach the grid
tree stuck on 'Grid installing'
nodes.auto_repair: If a worker's state.json fails JSON.parse, move it aside; the daemon rewrites it every 10 s. If library.json is invalid, flag it for the admin.
nodes.manual_fix: Run `ashley status --json` on the grid and read which embedded file is broken.
nodes.future_risk: A new raw-embedded field, or Slurm names/reasons containing control characters.

nodes.title: config.env complete, sourceable, 600
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/config.env (mode 600) is a bash-sourceable KEY=%q file. It holds ROOT, RUNTIME, SANDBOX, CLAUDE_BIN, BINDS, CONTAINER, SOURCE, BOOTSTRAP_JOB/STATE and, optionally, AWAITING_ACCESS. set_cfg writes it through one shared `$CFG.part` name, so two concurrent writers can race (the tree's `status`, which auto-adopts, and the MCP server). bootstrap.sbatch also writes it.
nodes.check: login node: `bash -n ~/.ashley/config.env && (. ~/.ashley/config.env; for v in ROOT RUNTIME SANDBOX CLAUDE_BIN BINDS; do [ -n "${!v}" ] || echo unset $v; done; [[ $BOOTSTRAP_JOB =~ ^[0-9]*$ ]] || echo bad-job)` prints nothing, and `stat -c %a ~/.ashley/config.env` = 600.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: no config.env
REFUSING: RUNTIME unset in config.env (bootstrap not finished?)
REFUSING: /wsu/home/.../.ashley/config.env missing; run 'ashley install' first
config.env must set ROOT
nodes.auto_repair: If the library is readable, `ashley adopt <default>` rewrites RUNTIME, SANDBOX, CLAUDE_BIN and BINDS. Otherwise `ashley install` restores ROOT. Lab admin only: `ashley bootstrap --resubmit`.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard's grid step again.
nodes.future_risk: A later version adds keys that older adopt paths do not write.

nodes.title: READY: container and Claude Code resolvable from the login node
nodes.assumption: ready means READY is non-empty, CLAUDE_BIN is executable and $SANDBOX/usr/local/bin/node is executable, all seen from the login node (CephFS is mounted there). `status` and `worker start` auto-adopt the library default once it becomes readable.
nodes.check: login node: `ashley status --json` shows "ready":true. Or directly: `test -s ~/.ashley/READY && . ~/.ashley/config.env && test -x "$CLAUDE_BIN" && test -x "$SANDBOX/usr/local/bin/node"`.
failure_signatures: grid not ready yet (bootstrap job N: FAILED); try again when 'ashley status' says ready=true
no container yet: it comes with lab access (the last setup step; your lead approves it)
FAIL  not ready (bootstrap job none: )
nodes.auto_repair: If the library is readable, run `ashley adopt`. If the user is the lab admin, run `ashley bootstrap --resubmit --partition secp --qos secondary`. A student without access has no repair; they wait for access.
nodes.manual_fix: Finish the lab-access step; the lead approves it.
nodes.future_risk: The recorded absolute paths go stale (see grid-node.runtime-path).

nodes.title: Storage ROOT exists and is writable
nodes.assumption: ROOT exists and is writable; workspaces live there. The default is /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER/ashley when that directory exists and is writable, else ~/ashley.
nodes.check: login node: `. ~/.ashley/config.env; test -d "$ROOT" -a -w "$ROOT"`.
failure_signatures: ashley: cannot create ROOT=...
FAIL  ROOT not writable (unset)
REFUSING: cannot write <ROOT>
nodes.auto_repair: `ashley install` without --root falls back to default_root, sets it and runs mkdir.
nodes.manual_fix: Set ashley.gridRoot to a writable path and rerun the grid step.
nodes.future_risk: The CephFS path is renamed at a storage migration, or the group allocation expires.

nodes.title: secrets.env present, 600, with the laptop's token names
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/secrets.env (mode 600) holds GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and HF_TOKEN as KEY=value lines. The laptop writes it over ssh stdin under umask 077, never as an argument. It is bash-sourceable, and the daemon reads it into every run's environment.
nodes.check: login node: `stat -c %a ~/.ashley/secrets.env` = 600, and the secrets[] names in `ashley status --json` include every token the laptop holds.
failure_signatures: FAIL  secrets.env missing (GitHub / Hugging Face tokens for the worker)
grid is missing: GitHub token
no secrets.env
nodes.auto_repair: pushTokens from the laptop's SecretStorage (part of wizard step gridInstall).
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: A token format with characters that bash `source` interprets.

nodes.title: An enabled Claude credential under ~/.ashley/accounts
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/accounts/default/token (600) holds a `claude setup-token` subscription token, or accounts/apikey/apikey holds an API key. The account is not disabled, and any state.json cooldown_until is in the past.
nodes.check: login node: `ashley accounts list` shows at least one entry with "enabled":true and cooldown_until null or past.
failure_signatures: FAIL  no Claude account (setup wizard step 'Claude token', or ashley accounts add-token default)
no enabled Claude account
status: rate_limited
nodes.auto_repair: Re-push the token from the laptop. Run `ashley accounts enable <name>` only when cooldown_until has passed; that clears the stale state.json.
nodes.manual_fix: Run 'Ashley: Store or replace my Claude token for the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: The token expires one year after `claude setup-token`.

nodes.title: Login node reaches HF, GitHub and Anthropic APIs on 443
nodes.assumption: verify-tokens and access requirements run curl from the login node straight to huggingface.co, api.github.com and api.anthropic.com, with no proxy and a 15 s limit.
nodes.check: login node: `for u in https://huggingface.co https://api.github.com https://api.anthropic.com; do curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} $u\n" $u; done`. Pass = no 000.
failure_signatures: HF_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
GITHUB_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
CLAUDE_TOKEN present (the check answered HTTP 000)
the Claude token could not be confirmed right now
nodes.auto_repair: Run the same verification inside a worker allocation (compute nodes have internet), for example with `srun --overlap` using the container's curl.
nodes.manual_fix: Report the egress block to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT restricts login-node egress, a common hardening step. The HF and GitHub checks do not tell 'unreachable' from 'rejected', so a blocked network looks like a bad token.

nodes.title: EL7 curl: -K - config on stdin, TLS 1.2, CA bundle still trusted
nodes.assumption: CentOS 7 curl 7.29 (NSS) reads `-K -` config from stdin with `header = "..."` lines, which keeps tokens out of ps, and supports `-w '%{http_code}'`. It must still negotiate TLS 1.2 with these APIs. Its CA bundle has been frozen since CentOS 7 went EOL (June 2024) and must still trust their roots.
nodes.check: login node: `printf 'header = "X-Probe: 1"\n' | curl -s -m 10 -K - -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.github.com/` = 200, and `curl -sS -m 10 -o /dev/null https://api.anthropic.com/; echo $?` is not 35 or 60.
failure_signatures: curl: (60) Peer's Certificate issuer is not recognized.
curl: (35) SSL connect error
NSS error -12286
HTTP code 000
nodes.auto_repair: Retry with `--cacert "$SANDBOX/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"` (the Debian 12 bundle on CephFS is readable from the login node).
nodes.manual_fix: Ask C&IT to update ca-certificates, or run verification inside a worker.
nodes.future_risk: High. Root CA rotations or TLS 1.3-only endpoints break an unpatched EL7 curl. A login-node OS upgrade fixes this.

nodes.title: HF_TOKEN verified by whoami-v2
nodes.assumption: GET https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 with Authorization: Bearer returns JSON with a "name". The first "name" match is taken as the user, but it could be an organisation's name.
nodes.check: login node: `ashley verify-tokens | grep '^HF_TOKEN'` prints 'HF_TOKEN ok (<name>)'.
failure_signatures: HF_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
HF_TOKEN missing
Hugging Face token missing or rejected
nodes.auto_repair: If the laptop's stored copy verifies from the laptop, re-push it (pushTokens).
nodes.manual_fix: Create a new read token at huggingface.co/settings/tokens and store it with the wizard.
nodes.future_risk: whoami-v2 renamed or versioned, or the JSON shape changes.

nodes.title: GITHUB_TOKEN verified by /user
nodes.assumption: GET https://api.github.com/user with Bearer returns a "login".
nodes.check: login node: `ashley verify-tokens | grep '^GITHUB_TOKEN'` prints 'GITHUB_TOKEN ok (<login>)'.
failure_signatures: GITHUB_TOKEN rejected or unreachable
GITHUB_TOKEN missing
GitHub token missing or rejected
nodes.auto_repair: Re-push from the laptop if the laptop's copy verifies. Otherwise re-run VS Code's GitHub sign-in (wizard step github).
nodes.manual_fix: Sign in to GitHub again in the wizard.
nodes.future_risk: Fine-grained PAT expiry (at most one year, shorter under org policy), or GitHub API version-header deprecation.

nodes.title: Claude subscription token accepted by GET /v1/models
nodes.assumption: GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models with Bearer <oauth token>, `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` and `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` answers 200 for a valid subscription token and 401 for an invalid one. `access requirements` passes only on 'ok'. Any other code blocks the lab-access request.
nodes.check: login node: `ashley verify-tokens | grep '^CLAUDE_TOKEN'` prints 'CLAUDE_TOKEN ok (subscription token accepted)'.
failure_signatures: CLAUDE_TOKEN rejected (invalid, expired or revoked: run claude setup-token again)
CLAUDE_TOKEN present (the check answered HTTP 403)
CLAUDE_TOKEN present (the check answered HTTP 000)
the Claude token on the grid was rejected (expired or revoked)
CLAUDE_TOKEN missing
nodes.auto_repair: On 000/429/5xx, retry after 60 s. As a fallback proof, run a one-turn `claude -p 'reply ok' --max-turns 1` inside a worker. There is no repair for a 401.
nodes.manual_fix: Run `claude setup-token` on the laptop and store the new token.
nodes.future_risk: High. The OAuth beta header is undocumented for this use. If Anthropic retires `oauth-2025-04-20` or refuses OAuth tokens on /v1/models, every valid token fails this check and every lab-access request is blocked. Tokens also expire after one year.

nodes.title: Long-lived `ashley relay` tolerated on the login node
nodes.assumption: Each laptop process (extension, MCP server, CLI) keeps one `ashley relay` bash loop on the login node, sleeping in 250 ms reads, for hours. C&IT's login-node process policy must tolerate it. The relay prints `READY <ms> <version>` first and answers PING with PONG.
nodes.check: laptop: `printf 'PING\nQUIT\n' | ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid '~/.ashley/bin/ashley relay'` prints 'READY <13 digits> <n>' and then 'PONG <13 digits>' within 5 s.
failure_signatures: relay send failed (...); using a fresh ssh
relay ask failed (...); using a fresh ssh
Connection to warrior.grid.wayne.edu closed by remote host.
Killed
ERROR unknown command
nodes.auto_repair: Built in: GridRelay reconnects, and every call falls back to a fresh ssh at about 2 s.
nodes.manual_fix: None needed unless the fallback also fails.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT deploys a login-node reaper (Arbiter-style cgroup limits or a maximum session age) that kills idle long sessions. The fallback path keeps working, only slower.

nodes.title: sshd tolerates Ashley's burst of parallel connections
nodes.assumption: sshd MaxStartups/MaxSessions, and any C&IT rate limiting, tolerate the extension's bursts of parallel BatchMode connections. A tree refresh alone opens status, library, access whoami and access list; doctor and relay reconnects add more. Whether fail2ban or similar is deployed is unknown.
nodes.check: laptop: start 6 `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` in parallel. Pass = all exit 0 within 30 s.
failure_signatures: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer
ssh_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
ssh: connect to host warrior.grid.wayne.edu port 22: Connection timed out (after repeated failures)
nodes.auto_repair: Serialise grid calls and back off exponentially (capped at 60 s). Stop retrying after a publickey failure so that a bad key cannot trigger a ban.
nodes.manual_fix: Wait 10 to 15 minutes. If the laptop's IP was banned, contact hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT tightens MaxStartups or adds fail2ban.

nodes.title: ashley uninstall leaves a fresh account
nodes.assumption: `ashley uninstall [--purge-root]` cancels worker jobs, removes the bashrc block and deletes ~/.ashley. It does NOT cancel a held ashley_access job and does not touch the admin-side status file or ACLs, so a reinstalled account can reappear as filed, pending or approved.
nodes.check: login node, after uninstall: `test ! -e ~/.ashley && ! grep -q '# >>> ashley' ~/.bashrc && [ -z "$(squeue -h -u $USER -n ashley_access -o %i)" ]`.
failure_signatures: reinstalled account shows 'filed' or 'pending' from before
ashley_* jobs left in squeue
nodes.auto_repair: `scancel` any of the user's jobs named ashley_* left after uninstall.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lead for `ashley access admin reset <id>` if a clean request is wanted.

nodes.title: Slurm client commands on PATH for non-interactive ssh
nodes.assumption: sbatch, squeue, sacct, scancel and scontrol are on PATH in a non-interactive ssh session on the login node, with no `module load`.
nodes.check: login node: `command -v sbatch squeue sacct scancel scontrol` prints five paths; `sbatch --version` prints 'slurm X.Y.Z'.
failure_signatures: sbatch: command not found
ashley: sbatch failed: ...: command not found
status shows no jobs and bootstrap_state empty (job_state silently returns empty)
nodes.auto_repair: If a slurm module exists, source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh and `module load slurm`, then re-run.
nodes.manual_fix: Report the host to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: An OS upgrade moves Slurm into a module or /opt. A major Slurm upgrade changes option syntax.

nodes.title: slurmctld answers; errors are not read as 'job gone'
nodes.assumption: slurmctld answers within a few seconds. job_state() discards stderr, so an unreachable controller and a finished job both return an empty string. During an outage, status therefore reports no jobs, and `worker start` or `bootstrap` may submit duplicates.
nodes.check: login node: `scontrol ping` prints 'Slurmctld(primary) at ... is UP', and `timeout 15 squeue -h -u $USER -o %i >/dev/null; echo $?` = 0.
failure_signatures: slurm_load_jobs error: Socket timed out on send/recv operation
slurm_load_jobs error: Unable to contact slurm controller (connect failure)
ashley status exceeds the extension's 90 s timeout
nodes.auto_repair: Retry with backoff. The resolver must NOT treat an empty job_state as 'gone', and must block resubmission, while `scontrol ping` fails.
nodes.manual_fix: Wait; check C&IT maintenance announcements.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm upgrade windows and controller failover.

nodes.title: sacct returns final states of finished jobs
nodes.assumption: slurmdbd is up, and sacct returns the final state of jobs that have left squeue after MinJobAge. job_state keeps the first word, so 'CANCELLED by 123' becomes CANCELLED.
nodes.check: login node: `sacct -n -X -P -o State -S now-1days | head -1; echo $?` = 0. For the bootstrap: `sacct -j $BOOTSTRAP_JOB -n -X -P -o State,ExitCode`.
failure_signatures: sacct: error: Problem talking to the database: Connection refused
sacct: error: Slurm accounting storage is disabled
bootstrap job N: (empty state) in status and doctor
nodes.auto_repair: Read the job's own log instead: in ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_<id>.out, 'READY written' means success and 'STOP:' or 'REFUSING' means failure.
nodes.manual_fix: Report to hpc@wayne.edu if it persists.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm versions change sacct formats or state names.

nodes.title: squeue format codes and filters behave as parsed
nodes.assumption: squeue accepts -h, -u, -n, -t PD and -j, and the format codes %i %j %T %N %M %l %P %R (8 '|'-separated fields) plus %u, %k (comment) and %V (submit time). %N is a short node name. The laptop's GridApi.squeue() passes '$USER' through shq, so it is single-quoted and never expanded. This was found by reading gridApi.ts:56 with shell.ts:86-107 and has not been run. Consequence: the 'connect to another running job' picker and the MCP 'My Slurm jobs' resource always see an empty list.
nodes.check: login node: `squeue -h -u $USER -o '%i|%j|%T|%N|%M|%l|%P|%R' | awk -F'|' 'NF<8{b=1} END{exit b}'` and `squeue -h -n ashley_access -o '%i|%u|%k|%V'` both exit 0. laptop: `ssh wsu-grid "'squeue' '-u' '\$USER' '-h'"` reproduces the quoting bug.
failure_signatures: squeue: error: Invalid user: $USER
No Claude worker is running. Connect to another running job? never offered
fields shifted when a reason contains '|'
nodes.auto_repair: This is a code fix, not a runtime repair: GridApi.squeue should use `ashley status --json` jobs[], or `bash -c 'squeue -u "$USER" ...'`.
nodes.manual_fix: Use `ashley status` on the grid to see jobs.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm moves to --json output and deprecates text formats, or changes comment-field semantics (AccountingStoreFlags).
nodes.source: grid/ashley:195-201, 459, 531; extension/src/core/gridApi.ts:55-58; extension/src/core/shell.ts:86-108; extension/src/core/slurm.ts:16-38; extension/src/extension.ts:248, 400; extension/src/mcp/server.ts:155-156

nodes.title: sbatch --parsable output captured as a clean job id
nodes.assumption: `sbatch --parsable` prints only `<jobid>[;cluster]`. All four submit sites capture `2>&1`: library publish, bootstrap, worker start and access request. Any stderr line from sbatch or a site job_submit plugin (a warning, 'info: defaulting ...') therefore becomes part of the stored id (BOOTSTRAP_JOB in config.env, workers/<w>/job.id).
nodes.check: login node: every workers/*/job.id and BOOTSTRAP_JOB matches ^[0-9]+$. One-time probe: `sbatch --parsable --hold -J ashley_probe -p secp -q secondary -t 1 --mem=16M -o /dev/null --wrap true 2>&1` is a bare integer; scancel it afterwards.
failure_signatures: job.id or BOOTSTRAP_JOB containing 'sbatch: warning:' text
worker job_state 'none' right after a successful start
a second worker for the same name PENDING (Dependency)
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite job.id or BOOTSTRAP_JOB with the last line matching ^[0-9]+, or look the job up by name: `squeue -h -u $USER -n ashley_<w> -o %i`.
nodes.manual_fix: Run `ashley worker stop --name <w>` and start again.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT adds a job_submit.lua that prints notices on stderr.

nodes.title: reqp/requeue accepts and starts Ashley jobs
nodes.assumption: reqp/requeue is the default for bootstrap.sbatch (4 CPU, 16G, 2 h), for workers (4 CPU, 16G, 24 h) and for the held request job, and it starts jobs in reasonable time. On 2026-09-28 it pended 30+ minutes on Priority while secp/secondary started at once.
nodes.check: login node: `sbatch --test-only -p reqp -q requeue -c 4 --mem=16G -t 1-00:00:00 --wrap true 2>&1` prints 'to be started at <time>'. Pass = within an hour; later = warn.
failure_signatures: squeue reason (Priority) or (Resources) for hours
Requested time limit is invalid (missing or exceeds some limit)
Invalid qos specification
nodes.auto_repair: If a worker or bootstrap has pended more than 15 minutes on Priority/Resources and `--test-only` predicts an earlier start on secp/secondary, scancel it and resubmit there (`worker start --partition secp --qos secondary`, or `bootstrap --resubmit --partition secp --qos secondary`).
nodes.manual_fix: Set ashley.worker.partition=secp and ashley.worker.qos=secondary.
nodes.future_risk: reqp is renamed or retired, or the requeue QoS policy changes.

nodes.title: secp/secondary usable as fallback and publish default
nodes.assumption: Students may use secp/secondary, and its MaxWall (90 days per sacctmgr on 2026-09-28) covers requests. Library publish defaults to it. Unknown: whether secondary is preemptible. Workers get --requeue only when qos=requeue, so a preempted secondary worker would be cancelled rather than requeued.
nodes.check: login node: `sbatch --test-only -p secp -q secondary -c 4 --mem=16G -t 1-00:00:00 --wrap true 2>&1`, then `sacctmgr -nP show qos secondary format=name,maxwall,preemptmode` and `scontrol show partition secp | grep -E 'PreemptMode|AllowQos|MaxTime'`.
failure_signatures: Invalid qos specification
Job's QOS not permitted to use this partition
worker state PREEMPTED or CANCELLED with no restart
nodes.auto_repair: If secondary preempts, add --requeue for it as well (a code change), or restart the worker when sacct shows PREEMPTED.
nodes.manual_fix: Start the worker again.
nodes.future_risk: secp is an owned-node scavenger partition and can change with hardware ownership.

nodes.title: GPU workers: gmsap,gvohp,galhp + QoS gpu + gres gpu
nodes.assumption: GPU workers are submitted with `--partition gmsap,gvohp,galhp --qos gpu --gres=gpu:N`. The account must be allowed QoS gpu on those partitions, and the gres name 'gpu' must exist. The partition list is hard-coded in the extension.
nodes.check: login node: `sinfo -h -p gmsap,gvohp,galhp -o '%P %a %G'` lists all three as up with gpu gres, and `sbatch --test-only -p gmsap,gvohp,galhp -q gpu --gres=gpu:1 -c 4 --mem=16G -t 04:00:00 --wrap true 2>&1` prints 'to be started'.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Invalid generic resource (gres) specification
Job's QOS not permitted to use this partition
sbatch: error: invalid partition specified: galhp
nodes.auto_repair: Remove from the list any partition that sinfo does not list or reports inactive, then retry.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu which GPU partitions the account may use.
nodes.future_risk: High. Lab-owned GPU partitions are renamed or retired as hardware ages.

nodes.title: Offered (partition, QoS) pairs valid; hours within MaxWall
nodes.assumption: Every (partition, QoS) pair the UI offers is valid. The MCP tool accepts qos 'primary' with partition reqp, which is probably not a permitted pair (unverified). QoS MaxWall and MaxSubmitJobsPerUser must allow the requested --hours and one held request job alongside the workers.
nodes.check: login node: `sacctmgr -nP show qos requeue,secondary,primary,gpu format=name,maxwall,maxsubmitpu,maxjobspu,preemptmode` and `scontrol show partition reqp secp | grep -E 'AllowQos|MaxTime'`.
failure_signatures: Invalid qos specification
Job violates accounting/QOS policy (job submit limit, user's size and/or time limits)
QOSMaxSubmitJobPerUserLimit
pending reason QOSMaxWallDurationPerJobLimit
nodes.auto_repair: Clamp --hours to the QoS MaxWall. Refuse, or remap, a pair that sacctmgr/scontrol say is not allowed before submitting.
nodes.manual_fix: Pick reqp/requeue or secp/secondary.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT QoS policy changes.

nodes.title: requeue QoS preempts with REQUEUE; workers resume, bootstrap does not
nodes.assumption: QoS requeue is preemptible with PreemptMode REQUEUE. Workers on it carry --requeue and --open-mode=append and resume (the daemon is re-entrant and recovers .claimed files). bootstrap.sbatch on the same QoS carries --no-requeue, so a preempted bootstrap ends PREEMPTED or CANCELLED and must be resubmitted.
nodes.check: login node: `scontrol show config | grep -E '^(PreemptMode|PreemptType|JobRequeue)'` and `sacctmgr -nP show qos requeue format=name,preemptmode`. After an event: `sacct -j <id> -o State,Restarts`.
failure_signatures: bootstrap job N: PREEMPTED (no READY written)
repeated 'ashleyd start' lines in ashleyd.log (requeued)
requests retried with attempt > 1
nodes.auto_repair: If the bootstrap state is PREEMPTED, NODE_FAIL or TIMEOUT, run `ashley bootstrap --resubmit` (on secp/secondary if reqp pends). If a worker was not requeued, run `ashley worker start`.
nodes.manual_fix: Start the worker again; queued requests wait in the inbox.
nodes.future_risk: A PreemptMode change to CANCEL makes requeue workers die at the first preemption.

nodes.title: --dependency=singleton keeps one job per worker name
nodes.assumption: --dependency=singleton, keyed on job name ashley_<name> per user, keeps one worker per name. A stale PENDING or RUNNING twin makes a new submission wait with reason Dependency.
nodes.check: login node: `squeue -h -u $USER -o '%j %i %T %R' | awk '$1 ~ /^ashley_/{c[$1]++} END{for(k in c) if(c[k]>1) print k}'` is empty (the held ashley_access job excepted).
failure_signatures: worker PENDING (Dependency) indefinitely
worker <w> already has job N (PENDING)
nodes.auto_repair: Keep the job whose id is in job.id and scancel the other jobs of the same name.
nodes.manual_fix: `ashley worker stop --name <w>`, then start it again.

nodes.title: --signal=B:TERM@120 reaches the daemon before the wall limit
nodes.assumption: --signal=B:TERM@120 delivers TERM to the batch shell about 2 minutes (up to 3) before the wall limit. The script `exec`s apptainer, so the batch shell's PID becomes apptainer, which should forward the signal to node ashleyd.js, whose SIGTERM handler calls beginStop. Not tested on this grid.
nodes.check: compute node test job (secp/secondary, -t 00:04:00): render the worker template with a fake claude. Pass = ashleyd.log contains 'SIGTERM' and state.json shows stopping before the job ends in TIMEOUT.
failure_signatures: job ends TIMEOUT with no 'SIGTERM' in ashleyd.log
in-flight request without a result in outbox
<id>.json.claimed left in inbox (recovered at next start)
nodes.auto_repair: Restart the worker; the daemon re-queues .claimed files at start.
nodes.manual_fix: Resend the lost request.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm changes signal timing, or apptainer changes signal forwarding.

nodes.title: --output paths resolve against the submit directory
nodes.assumption: #SBATCH --output resolves against the submit directory. ashley cds into ~/.ashley/log (bootstrap, request) or the worker directory (log/slurm_%j.out) before calling sbatch. The worker's log/ must exist beforehand, or the job has nowhere to write.
nodes.check: login node, after submit: `ls ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_<id>.out` exists; once RUNNING, `ls ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log/slurm_<id>.out` exists.
failure_signatures: worker log shows nothing under '--- slurm'
job FAILED at once with no output file
nodes.auto_repair: `mkdir -p` the log directories and resubmit.
nodes.manual_fix: Run `ashley worker start --name <w>` again (it creates log/).

nodes.title: --export semantics: ALL carries PATH; commas split values
nodes.assumption: sbatch's default --export=ALL carries the ssh session's environment into jobs: PATH with ~/.ashley/bin from the bashrc block, HOME, USER. `--export=ALL,K=V,...` splits on commas, so a value containing a comma is cut. `library publish --purpose 'general: Claude Code, Node 22, git, python3'`, exactly as INSTALL.md shows, stores 'general: Claude Code'. Found by reading, not run.
nodes.check: login node, after a publish: `grep -o '"purpose": *"[^"]*"' /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/library.json` equals the requested text.
failure_signatures: library.json purpose truncated at the first comma
stray variables such as ' Node 22' in the publish job environment
nodes.auto_repair: Pass PURPOSE through a file, or base64-encode it, instead of --export (a code fix).
nodes.manual_fix: Use a purpose without commas.

nodes.title: Lab-access request = held zero-work Slurm job
nodes.assumption: A request is `sbatch --hold -J ashley_access -p reqp -q requeue -t 1 -n 1 --mem=16M -o /dev/null --comment 'ashley-access v1 note=...'` of a two-line script. It stays PENDING (JobHeldUser), uses no storage, and is cancelled by tidy_request_job after the decision. Slurm authenticates the submitter, which stops forgery. Unknown: whether C&IT purges long-held jobs, or counts them against a per-user submit limit.
nodes.check: login node (student): `squeue -h -u $USER -n ashley_access -o '%i|%T|%r|%k'` prints one line: PENDING|JobHeldUser|ashley-access v1 note=....
failure_signatures: ashley: could not file the request: sbatch: error:
state flips from 'filed' back to 'none' (held job vanished before ingest)
your request is already with your lead (filed), indefinitely
nodes.auto_repair: If the state is none, no status file exists and the requirements pass, refile with the stored note. If reqp/requeue refuses, file on secp/secondary (the job never runs).
nodes.manual_fix: Run the wizard's last step again, or tell the lead directly.
nodes.future_risk: A purge policy for held jobs, a job_submit plugin that rejects --mem=16M or -t 1, or Slurm hiding --comment from squeue.

nodes.title: squeue shows every user's jobs (PrivateData lacks jobs)
nodes.assumption: squeue shows every user's jobs, so the admin's ingest `squeue -h -n ashley_access -t PD -o '%i|%u|%k|%V'` sees students' held requests. The code comments state this, but it has not been exercised with a second account.
nodes.check: login node (admin): `scontrol show config | grep -i '^PrivateData'` shows none, or a list without 'jobs'; `squeue -h -t PD -o %u | sort -u | wc -l` > 1.
failure_signatures: admin queue empty while the student's `access status` says filed
tree shows 0 pending
nodes.manual_fix: If C&IT enables PrivateData=jobs, ask for an exception or move requests to a drop-box design.
nodes.future_risk: High. PrivateData=jobs is a common hardening step and would silently stop every access request.

nodes.title: srun --jobid --overlap can probe inside a worker allocation
nodes.assumption: `srun --jobid=<id> --overlap` (Slurm >= 20.11) starts a step inside a running worker allocation. The resolver uses it to run compute-node checks without submitting a job; the 2026-09-28 peer test used it too.
nodes.check: login node: `srun --jobid=$(cat ~/.ashley/workers/default/job.id) --overlap -N1 -n1 -t 1 hostname` prints the worker node within 30 s.
failure_signatures: srun: error: Unable to create step for job N: Requested nodes are busy
srun: unrecognized option '--overlap'
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to a tiny probe job: `sbatch --wait -p secp -q secondary -t 2 --mem=100M --wrap '<check>'`.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm changes step-sharing defaults.

nodes.title: worker.sbatch.tpl rendered with no leftover tokens
nodes.assumption: `ashley worker start` renders worker.sbatch.tpl with sed using '|' as the delimiter. The values (partition, QoS, mem, sandbox and claude paths, library root) must contain no '|', '&' or newline ('&' in a sed replacement inserts the match), and no @TOKEN@ may remain.
nodes.check: login node: `grep -c '@[A-Z_]*@' ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/job.sbatch` = 0 and `bash -n ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/job.sbatch` passes.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: invalid partition specified: @PARTITION@
sed: -e expression #1, char N: unknown option to `s'
a sandbox path mangled where '&' was replaced by the match
nodes.auto_repair: Validate the inputs, then re-render with `ashley worker start`.
nodes.manual_fix: Use a container name and path without '|' or '&'.

nodes.title: Worker job RUNNING with a fresh heartbeat
nodes.assumption: A worker is healthy when its job is RUNNING, workers/<w>/node has been written and state.json is younger than 90 s. The job script refuses early, with REFUSING lines, when config, sandbox, claude or runtime is missing on the node.
nodes.check: laptop or login node: `ashley worker list --json` shows job_state RUNNING and alive true. Otherwise run `ashley worker log --name <w>` and grep slurm_<job>.out for REFUSING.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: no config.env
REFUSING: RUNTIME unset in config.env (bootstrap not finished?)
REFUSING: sandbox <path> incomplete
REFUSING: <claude> missing
REFUSING: runtime <path> missing on <host>
REFUSING: no /dev/shm scratch
job_state RUNNING with alive false
nodes.auto_repair: Stop and start the worker once. If a REFUSING line names config or sandbox, run `ashley adopt` first.
nodes.manual_fix: Send the output of 'Ashley: Show worker log' to the lead.

nodes.title: Slurm and the ashley CLI reachable from inside a worker
nodes.assumption: peerNote tells the worker Claude that '~/.ashley/bin/ashley is on PATH' and that it can run `ashley worker start`. Inside the apptainer container, PATH is the container's own plus only the claude directory, so ~/.ashley/bin is probably absent. sbatch, squeue, the munge socket and the Slurm libraries are not bound. So `ashley send`/`result` by full path should work (they only touch files), but `ashley worker start` and job_state from inside a worker should fail. Found by reading; the 2026-09-28 peer test ran on the host through `srun --overlap`, not inside the container.
nodes.check: compute node: `srun --jobid=<job> --overlap -N1 -n1 -t 1 $RUNTIME exec $BINDS $SANDBOX bash -c 'command -v ashley sbatch squeue; ls ~/.ashley/bin/ashley'`. Pass = sbatch and squeue resolve.
failure_signatures: bash: ashley: command not found
ashley: sbatch failed: ... sbatch: command not found
queued <id> on worker <w> (job none not running) from inside a worker
nodes.manual_fix: Code fix: prepend ~/.ashley/bin via APPTAINERENV_PREPEND_PATH, and either bind the Slurm clients, munge socket and slurm.conf, or tell the worker Claude that it cannot submit jobs.

nodes.title: Bootstrap job builds container and writes READY (admin only)
nodes.assumption: This runs for the admin only; students adopt the lab container. bootstrap.sbatch (reqp/requeue, 4 CPU, 16G, 2 h) finds a runtime, builds the sandbox, installs Claude Code pinned at 2.1.283 and writes READY. Exit codes: 1 REFUSING (config or ROOT), 2 no runtime, 3 no runtime could exec, 4 npm failed.
nodes.check: login node: `sacct -j $BOOTSTRAP_JOB -n -X -P -o State,ExitCode` and `grep -E '^(STOP|REFUSING)|READY written' ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_$BOOTSTRAP_JOB.out`.
failure_signatures: STOP: no container runtime found on <host>
STOP: sandbox built but no runtime could exec it
STOP: npm install failed
REFUSING: cannot write <ROOT>
REFUSING: <cfg> missing; run 'ashley install' first
State TIMEOUT after 2 h
nodes.auto_repair: `ashley bootstrap --resubmit` (on secp/secondary if reqp pends). Use `--update` to reinstall Claude Code. Exit 2 or 3: re-resolve the runtime (see grid-node.runtime-path).
nodes.manual_fix: Send ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_<job>.out to the lead.
nodes.future_risk: The pinned Claude Code version is yanked, or the node:22-bookworm tag moves.

nodes.title: Recorded absolute apptainer path exists on every compute node
nodes.assumption: The RUNTIME path recorded at build time (for example /wsu/el7/gnu7/apptainer/1.2.2/bin/apptainer, stored in library.json and config.env) exists and executes on every compute node a worker lands on. The worker never runs `module load`: it checks -x on that path and execs it.
nodes.check: compute node (srun --overlap, or a 1-minute secp/secondary job): `. ~/.ashley/config.env; test -x "$RUNTIME" && "$RUNTIME" --version` prints 'apptainer version 1.2.2'.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: runtime /wsu/el7/gnu7/apptainer/1.2.2/bin/apptainer missing on <host>
FAIL  runtime missing on this host (fine on the login node if the compute nodes have it)
nodes.auto_repair: In a tiny job: `source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh; module load apptainer` (any version), test exec of the sandbox, then set_cfg RUNTIME (student). The admin re-publishes or patches the runtime field in library.json.
nodes.manual_fix: The lead re-publishes the library entry after a grid OS upgrade.
nodes.future_risk: High. An EL7 to EL8/9 upgrade retires the /wsu/el7 tree, and an apptainer module bump (1.2.2 to 1.3/1.4) removes the versioned path.

nodes.title: /dev/shm writable scratch on compute nodes
nodes.assumption: /dev/shm on compute nodes is writable and large enough to serve as the worker's /tmp (bound with -B $SCR:/tmp) and as bootstrap scratch. Node /tmp is swept by a cleaner, so it is not used. Files in /dev/shm count against the job's memory cgroup.
nodes.check: compute node: `d=/dev/shm/${USER}_probe; mkdir -p $d && df -h /dev/shm && rmdir $d`. Pass = writable with more than 1 GB free.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: no /dev/shm scratch
No space left on device (writes to /tmp inside Claude runs)
job OUT_OF_MEMORY after large /tmp use
nodes.auto_repair: Restart the worker with `--exclude <node>` (a template option to add).
nodes.manual_fix: Report the node to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT caps /dev/shm per job.

nodes.title: Worker node name matches the laptop's *.nas.grid.wayne.edu block
nodes.assumption: `hostname -f` on compute nodes returns <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu, which the laptop's `Host *.nas.grid.wayne.edu` ProxyJump block matches. squeue %N gives the short name, which nodeHost() completes with nodeDomain.
nodes.check: login node: `cat ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/node` ends with '.nas.grid.wayne.edu'.
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname asx1.localdomain
Remote-SSH connects without ProxyJump and times out
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the stored node as its short name plus nodeDomain.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT renames the DNS domain.

nodes.title: ssh to a compute node only while holding a job there
nodes.assumption: pam_slurm_adopt on compute nodes admits the user only while they hold a job on that node, and adopts the session into the newest job's cgroup. Remote-SSH to the worker node therefore works while the worker runs, and its VS Code server shares the worker's --mem and --cpus. The node's sshd took about 23 s before running a command (measured).
nodes.check: laptop, with a worker RUNNING on <node>: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu true` exits 0 within 60 s. From the login node without a job: `ssh <node> true` fails with the pam_slurm_adopt message.
failure_signatures: Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node
Connecting with SSH timed out
oom-kill in slurm_<job>.out, or state OUT_OF_MEMORY, after the VS Code server joins the cgroup
nodes.auto_repair: Start a worker before connecting. Keep remote.SSH.connectTimeout at 300 (the extension sets it).
nodes.manual_fix: Start a worker, then 'Open my grid files'.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT disables ssh to compute nodes in favour of OnDemand, or a slower PAM stack pushes sessions past the timeout.

nodes.title: Compute nodes enforce CephFS POSIX ACLs like the login node
nodes.assumption: Every compute node mounts CephFS with POSIX ACL enforcement identical to the login node's. An approved student outside the group, holding only named-user ACLs, can then traverse /rs/rs_grp_oschome and read and execute the shared sandbox inside a job. Not yet tested with a non-owner account.
nodes.check: compute node, run as an approved non-member: `test -r /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/library.json && test -x <sandbox>/usr/local/bin/node && <runtime> exec <sandbox> true`.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: sandbox <path> incomplete
FATAL: container creation failed: mount /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared: permission denied
access state approved_unreadable
nodes.auto_repair: If the ACL is missing, the admin runs `ashley access admin resync`. Otherwise there is no automatic repair.
nodes.manual_fix: Ticket to hpc@wayne.edu naming the node.
nodes.future_risk: CephFS client changes (kernel vs fuse, the acl mount option) at an OS upgrade.

nodes.title: Compute nodes reach Anthropic, npm, Docker Hub, HF, GitHub
nodes.assumption: Compute nodes have direct outbound HTTPS. Claude runs, npm install, Docker Hub pulls in bootstrap, and hf/git inside workers all depend on it. The container shares the host network namespace.
nodes.check: compute node: `curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.anthropic.com/` is non-000. Also check the bootstrap smoke line `net=` in bootstrap_<id>.out.
failure_signatures: smoke: ... net=000
npm ERR! network
FATAL: While making image from oci registry: ... timeout
API Error: Connection error
nodes.manual_fix: Report to hpc@wayne.edu with the node name.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT introduces an egress proxy or allowlist on compute nodes.

nodes.title: CephFS lab volume mounted with free quota
nodes.assumption: /rs/rs_grp_oschome (CephFS, 20 TB, group oschome) is mounted on the login node and on the compute nodes, and has space left under its quota.
nodes.check: login node: `stat -f -c %T /rs/rs_grp_oschome` prints ceph, and `df-ceph oschome` shows usage < 90%. Optionally `getfattr -n ceph.quota.max_bytes /rs/rs_grp_oschome`.
failure_signatures: No such file or directory: /rs/rs_grp_oschome
Disk quota exceeded (EDQUOT) during npm install or publish
Transport endpoint is not connected
nodes.manual_fix: The lead frees space or asks C&IT for more.
nodes.future_risk: The allocation expires or needs renewal, or the path changes at a storage migration.

nodes.title: Lab admin = owner of /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared
nodes.assumption: The lab admin is whoever owns /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared (`stat %U`, currently go2432). ASHLEY_ADMIN is consulted only when stat fails.
nodes.check: login node: `stat -c %U /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared` prints go2432, and `ashley access whoami --json` shows lab_admin go2432.
failure_signatures: only the owner of /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared can run access init
only the lab admin (<x>) can manage requests
only the lab admin publishes containers
nodes.manual_fix: Ask C&IT to restore ownership of shared/ to the lab admin.
nodes.future_risk: A storage migration that chowns the tree to root or a service account leaves the lab with no admin.

nodes.title: setfacl present; CephFS honours POSIX ACLs
nodes.assumption: setfacl and getfacl exist on the login node, and CephFS honours POSIX ACLs (confirmed 2026-09-28 for the admin). Panasas homes do not, which is why access state lives on the volume.
nodes.check: login node (admin): `f=$(mktemp -p /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/access/requests); setfacl -m u:$USER:r-- $f && getfacl -p $f | grep -q user:$USER:r--; rm -f $f`.
failure_signatures: setfacl: <path>: Operation not supported
setfacl: command not found
<id> approved, but N part(s) of the lab folder could not be opened (not owned by you?)
nodes.manual_fix: Ticket to hpc@wayne.edu: the CephFS mount has lost ACL support.
nodes.future_risk: CephFS remounted without ACLs, or a migration to a filesystem with NFSv4-only ACLs.

nodes.title: Volume/shared/access modes as `access init` sets them
nodes.assumption: After `ashley access init`: the volume root is o-rwx with default ACL o::---. shared/ is 2750 with a default ACL of u::rwx,g::r-x,o::---. Everything under shared/ is group read-only. access/ and access/status are 2710, access/requests is 2700, and each status/<id>.json is 600 plus u:<id>:r--. The old world-writable inbox is gone, and `library publish` keeps shared/ashley at 2750. ARCHITECTURE.md lags the code: it still describes the 1733 drop-box and 2775.
nodes.check: login node: `stat -c '%a %n' /rs/rs_grp_oschome /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/access /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/access/status /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/access/requests`. Pass = root other bits 0, shared 2750, ashley 2750, access 2710, status 2710, requests 2700. Also `test ! -e /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/access/inbox`.
failure_signatures: approved students cannot traverse (state approved_unreadable)
grid users outside the lab can read shared/ (silent)
access/inbox still present
nodes.auto_repair: Admin: `ashley access init`. It is idempotent and re-applies approved users.
nodes.manual_fix: The lead runs `ashley access init`.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT resets modes on the volume, or a member creates a world-readable directory at the root.

nodes.title: Each member's /rs/rs_grp_oschome/<id> closed to others
nodes.assumption: The volume root is traversable by approved users, so /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER (the member's own tree, bound into workers) must be o-rwx. cmd_adopt closes it; cmd_install does not.
nodes.check: login node: `stat -c %a /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER` ends in 0, and `getfacl -p /rs/rs_grp_oschome | grep -q '^default:other::---'`.
failure_signatures: other grid users can list /rs/rs_grp_oschome/<id>/ashley/workspaces (silent)
nodes.auto_repair: `[ -O /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER ] && chmod o-rwx /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER`. This is safe because only the owner acts on their own directory.
nodes.manual_fix: `chmod o-rwx /rs/rs_grp_oschome/<id>`.

nodes.title: Approved users hold read ACLs on the whole lab folder
nodes.assumption: Approve sets --x on the volume root, r-x plus a default r-X on shared/, and a recursive r-X plus default ACLs on every child except access/ and symlinks. It fails on files the admin does not own. It walks every inode, which can outlast the extension's 120 s ssh timeout, and the ssh is then killed mid-walk, possibly leaving partial grants. Content added later is covered by the default ACLs only when created in place; cp -a and mv keep the old ACLs.
nodes.check: login node (admin), per approved user: `getfacl -p /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/library.json | grep -q 'user:<id>:r'`, and `find /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared -path '*/access' -prune -o ! -user $USER -print | head` is empty.
failure_signatures: <id> approved, but N part(s) of the lab folder could not be opened (not owned by you?)
cannot read the shared container <sandbox> (ask your lead for the oschome group)
extension access action times out at 120 s
nodes.auto_repair: Admin: `ashley access admin resync`, run as a Slurm job rather than over a 120 s ssh call.
nodes.manual_fix: The lead runs resync. Files owned by other members must be chowned or re-created by the admin.
nodes.future_risk: As shared/ grows (datasets), the walk time grows with it.

nodes.title: Per-applicant status file readable only by that applicant
nodes.assumption: Each applicant has status/<id>.json (600 plus u:<id>:r--) and --x path ACLs on the volume root, shared/, access/ and status/, so student_state can read its own decision. Ingest writes a status file only for users that `getent passwd` resolves through SSSD; others are skipped silently.
nodes.check: login node (student): `test -r /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/access/status/$USER.json`, and the state in `ashley access status --json` agrees with it.
failure_signatures: state stuck at filed after the admin decided
approved_unreadable
an applicant never appears in the admin list (getent failed)
nodes.auto_repair: Admin: run `ashley access admin list` (it ingests) or `ashley access init` (it re-applies path_traverse).
nodes.manual_fix: The lead re-runs the admin list.
nodes.future_risk: An SSSD outage or identity-source change on the login node.

nodes.title: Grid-side eligibility: tokens verify and bashrc block present
nodes.assumption: `ashley access requirements --json` passes only when CLAUDE_TOKEN, HF_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN are ok and the bashrc block is present. The wizard also requires every earlier step done and the Claude Code and Remote-SSH extensions installed.
nodes.check: login node: `ashley access requirements --json` prints {"ok":true,"missing":[]}.
failure_signatures: not eligible yet:
finish the setup first; requests are for working environments

nodes.title: Lab access progresses none > filed > pending > approved
nodes.assumption: Lab access moves none -> filed (held job) -> pending (admin ingest opened a status file) -> approved, denied or removed. Approved means library.json is readable, and reset lets the student ask again. In lab mode (ASHLEY_LAB=1, the default) students never build their own container and wait at this node.
nodes.check: student: `ashley access whoami --json` state. Admin: `ashley access admin list --json`. Consistency rules: approved implies library.json is readable; filed implies a held ashley_access job exists.
failure_signatures: Waiting for lab access (for days)
your request was already decided (denied); ask your lead to reset it if you need to ask again

approved_unreadable
nodes.auto_repair: approved_unreadable: the admin runs resync. filed with no held job: refile.
nodes.manual_fix: Remind the lead. The admin page drafts the oschome-group email to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: This step depends on a human: approvals wait on the lead's response time, and the flow stalls if the admin leaves the lab.

nodes.title: library.json parseable by the python-free grep parser
nodes.assumption: library.json is written by json.dump(indent=1), with one flat object per entry and string fields. The grid CLI parses it with grep and sed (the login node has no python), and that parse breaks on nested objects, escaped quotes or a '}' inside a string.
nodes.check: login node: `ashley library` lists a default, and `ashley library --json | tail -1` parses on the laptop.
failure_signatures: no shared library readable at /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley (ask your lead for the oschome group)
no library entry 'X' (ashley library)
adopt dies with an empty sandbox field
nodes.manual_fix: The admin re-publishes the entry and never hand-edits library.json with nested values.
nodes.future_risk: A future schema field with a nested object breaks lib_field.

nodes.title: Default library entry's sandbox and claude readable by the user
nodes.assumption: For this user, through group bits or ACLs, the default entry's sandbox/usr/local/bin/node is executable and its claude_bin is readable.
nodes.check: login node: `s=$(grep -o '"sandbox": *"[^"]*"' /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/library.json | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4); test -x $s/usr/local/bin/node`, then run `ashley adopt`.
failure_signatures: cannot read the shared container <sandbox> (ask your lead for the oschome group)
cannot read <claude_bin>
nodes.auto_repair: After the admin's resync, run `ashley adopt <default>`.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lead to approve or resync.

nodes.title: Publishing an image requires Node 22 and python3 inside it
nodes.assumption: An image can be published only if it provides /usr/local/bin/node (Node 22), npm and python3; the library.json merge runs the container's python3. docker://nvidia/cuda:*-runtime images provide neither node nor python3, so the INSTALL.md CUDA example stops at the build check. Found by reading, not run.
nodes.check: login node, after the job: `grep -E 'library entry written|published' ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_<id>.out`, and the entry is present in library.json.
failure_signatures: build with <rt> failed:
STOP: sandbox built but no runtime could exec it
python3: not found
only the lab admin publishes containers
ENOENT at npm install on the shared path (seen once, fixed by binding a shared ROOT)
nodes.manual_fix: Publish from a base with Node 22 (for example a node:22-bookworm image with CUDA libraries added), not from bare nvidia/cuda.
nodes.future_risk: Node 22 reaches end of life in April 2027 and the node:22-bookworm tag freezes. Debian bookworm reaches end of life after that.

nodes.title: Cheap way to run a check ON a compute node (srun --overlap into the worker, or a 1-CPU probe job)
nodes.assumption: Every compute-node check in this graph runs as a Slurm step, never as work on the login node. With a worker running: srun --jobid=$JID --overlap -N1 -n1 --quiet -t 1 <cmd> (Slurm >= 20.11 semantics of --overlap; used successfully in docs/research/library_peer_test.sh). With no worker: a probe job 'sbatch --parsable -p secp -q secondary -t 5 -c 1 --mem=1G -D ~/.ashley/log -o probe_%j.out --wrap <cmd>' starts within minutes. Throughout this graph PROBE(cmd) means one of these two, and CEXEC(cmd) means PROBE('source ~/.ashley/config.env; mkdir -p /dev/shm/${USER}_probe; $RUNTIME exec $BINDS -B /dev/shm/${USER}_probe:/tmp $SANDBOX <cmd>; rm -rf /dev/shm/${USER}_probe').
nodes.check: Login node (only waits): JID=$(cat ~/.ashley/workers/default/job.id); srun --jobid=$JID --overlap -N1 -n1 --quiet -t 1 hostname -f -> prints the same host as ~/.ashley/workers/default/node within ~10 s. No worker running: sbatch --parsable -p secp -q secondary -t 5 -c 1 --mem=1G -D ~/.ashley/log -o probe_%j.out --wrap 'hostname -f'; pass = probe_<id>.out contains a *.nas.grid.wayne.edu name and sacct State=COMPLETED.
failure_signatures: srun: unrecognized option '--overlap'
srun: error: Unable to create step for job <id>: Requested node configuration is not available
srun: Job <id> step creation temporarily disabled, retrying
srun: error: Invalid job id specified
probe job PENDING (Priority) for more than 10 minutes
nodes.auto_repair: If srun --overlap is refused, fall back to the sbatch --wrap probe; if the secp/secondary probe pends > 10 min, resubmit the same probe on reqp/requeue.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu whether --overlap steps are allowed inside running jobs; meanwhile run node checks as tiny sbatch jobs and read ~/.ashley/log/probe_<id>.out.
nodes.future_risk: A Slurm upgrade can change step-overlap defaults or disallow extra steps (OverlapStep policy); partition/QoS names used by the fallback probe are site-specific and may be renamed.

nodes.title: Partitions and QoS the jobs name exist and the account may use them
nodes.assumption: Partition reqp with QoS requeue (bootstrap and worker default), secp with QoS secondary (the documented fallback, and the default for library publish), and GPU partitions gmsap,gvohp,galhp with QoS gpu exist, are up, and the user's Slurm association permits each pairing. galhp and the 'gpu' QoS name are not verified anywhere in the repository.
