nodes.check: Login node (read-only, instant): sinfo -h -o '%P %a' -p reqp,secp,gmsap,gvohp,galhp -> each listed and 'up'; for each pair: sbatch --test-only -p reqp -q requeue -t 1 -c 1 --wrap true (and secp/secondary, gmsap/gpu --gres=gpu:1) -> stderr 'sbatch: Job <n> to start at ...' (nothing is submitted). Optional: sacctmgr -n -P show assoc user=$USER format=partition,qos.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Invalid partition name specified
sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Invalid qos specification
sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Invalid account or account/partition combination specified
Job's QOS not permitted to use this partition
ashley: sbatch failed: <message>
nodes.auto_repair: Pick the first pairing that --test-only accepts (reqp/requeue, then secp/secondary) and write it to ashley.worker.partition / ashley.worker.qos; for GPU, drop partitions that --test-only rejects from the comma list.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lab admin or hpc@wayne.edu which partition/QoS the AccessID may use and set ashley.worker.partition and ashley.worker.qos accordingly.
nodes.future_risk: reqp/secp/gmsap/gvohp are WSU-specific names; C&IT renames or retires partitions when hardware (H200/L40S) arrives or at the el7 -> el8/el9 migration; QoS names requeue/secondary/gpu may be consolidated.
nodes.source: grid/bootstrap.sbatch:8-10; grid/worker.sbatch.tpl:7-8; grid/ashley:75,247,268-269; extension/src/core/slurm.ts:59-75; extension/package.json (ashley.worker.partition, ashley.worker.qos)

nodes.title: Requested wall time fits the QoS MaxWall
nodes.assumption: The worker's --time (hours from the extension, 1..720, rendered as D-HH:00:00) and the bootstrap's 02:00:00 are within the chosen QoS MaxWall (measured: primary 30 d, secondary 90 d; requeue and gpu unknown).
nodes.check: Login node: sacctmgr -n -P show qos requeue,secondary,primary,gpu format=name,maxwall; then sbatch --test-only -p <part> -q <qos> -t <rendered time> --wrap true -> accepted.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Batch job submission failed: Requested time limit is invalid (missing or exceeds some limit)
squeue reason QOSMaxWallDurationPerJobLimit
job PENDING forever with a limit reason
nodes.auto_repair: Clamp hours to the QoS MaxWall reported by sacctmgr and resubmit.
nodes.manual_fix: Choose fewer hours or a QoS with a longer MaxWall (primary).
nodes.future_risk: C&IT changes QoS limits without notice; the extension's 720 h ceiling is hard-coded.

nodes.title: Worker and bootstrap jobs start within minutes
nodes.assumption: A submitted worker or bootstrap job leaves PENDING quickly. Measured: reqp/requeue sat PENDING (Priority) 30+ minutes while secp/secondary started at once.
nodes.check: Login node: squeue -j $JID -h -o '%T|%r|%V' -> RUNNING, or PENDING younger than 10 minutes.
failure_signatures: PENDING (Priority)
PENDING (Resources)
PENDING (QOSMaxJobsPerUserLimit)
PENDING (AssocGrpCpuLimit)
Ashley view shows the worker as PENDING for long
nodes.auto_repair: For the user's own pending ashley_* job: scontrol update JobId=$JID Partition=secp QOS=secondary; if refused, scancel and resubmit with --partition secp --qos secondary (queued requests stay in the inbox, nothing is lost).
nodes.manual_fix: Set ashley.worker.partition=secp and ashley.worker.qos=secondary, or wait.
nodes.future_risk: Fair-share weights and partition policies change each semester; secondary may become preemptible (see grid-slurm.requeue-reentrancy).

nodes.title: Grid scripts on disk have LF line endings
nodes.assumption: bootstrap.sbatch, worker.sbatch.tpl (and the rendered job.sbatch), ashley and ashleyd.js have no CR characters; files scp'd from a Windows checkout are stripped by 'ashley install' (sed 's/\r$//').
nodes.check: Login node: file ~/.ashley/bin/* ~/.ashley/workers/*/job.sbatch | grep -c CRLF -> 0.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Batch script contains DOS line breaks (\r\n)
/bin/bash^M: bad interpreter: No such file or directory
$'\r': command not found
nodes.auto_repair: sed -i 's/\r$//' on the affected files (what ashley install does), then re-render job.sbatch with ashley worker start.
nodes.manual_fix: Rerun 'Ashley: Install or update Ashley on the grid'.
nodes.future_risk: A new upload path that bypasses 'ashley install', or a git core.autocrlf setting on a student's machine overriding .gitattributes.

nodes.title: #SBATCH --output resolves against the submit directory and that directory exists
nodes.assumption: --output is relative to the submit directory: the worker is submitted with 'cd ~/.ashley/workers/<w> && sbatch job.sbatch' and writes log/slurm_%j.out (open-mode append); the bootstrap is submitted from ~/.ashley/log and writes bootstrap_%j.out. If the log directory is missing, Slurm cannot open stdout and the job fails with no log at all.
nodes.check: Login node: test -d ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log -a -w ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log && test -d ~/.ashley/log; after a job: sacct -j $JID -X -n -o State,ExitCode and ls ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log/slurm_$JID.out exists.
failure_signatures: sacct State FAILED with no slurm_<id>.out or bootstrap_<id>.out file
ashley worker log shows '--- slurm' with nothing under it
nodes.auto_repair: mkdir -p ~/.ashley/log ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/{inbox,outbox,log} and resubmit.
nodes.manual_fix: Do not delete log/ folders under ~/.ashley; rerun ashley worker start.
nodes.future_risk: If submission is ever done with sbatch -D elsewhere, relative outputs move (CLAUDE.md: --output resolves against the submit dir).

nodes.title: worker.sbatch.tpl renders to a complete job.sbatch
nodes.assumption: 'ashley worker start' substitutes @NAME@ @PARTITION@ @QOS@ @CPUS@ @MEM@ @TIME@ @GRES@ @REQUEUE@ @GPUS@ @CONC@ @SANDBOX@ @CLAUDE_BIN@ @LIBRARY@ with sed using '|' as delimiter; values must not contain '|' or '&' and no placeholder may survive.
nodes.check: Login node: grep -c '@[A-Z_]*@' ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/job.sbatch -> 0; grep -E '^#SBATCH --(partition|qos|time|mem|cpus-per-task)=' job.sbatch shows concrete values.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: invalid partition specified: @PARTITION@
sed: -e expression #N, char M: unknown option to `s'
REFUSING: sandbox @SANDBOX@ incomplete
nodes.auto_repair: Re-render with ashley worker start --name <w> using validated values (hours integer, mem like 16G).
nodes.manual_fix: Avoid special characters in worker settings; reinstall grid scripts if the template itself is damaged.
nodes.future_risk: New placeholders added to the template in a later Ashley version without the matching sed expression in an older grid/ashley.

nodes.title: --dependency=singleton job names do not collide
nodes.assumption: Each worker job is named ashley_<worker> with --dependency=singleton, so only one runs per name per user. Ashley also uses the names ashley_access (a held request job that never runs) and ashley_bootstrap. A worker named 'access' would wait forever behind the held request (and the admin ingest, which reads 'squeue -n ashley_access -t PD', would take the pending worker for an access request); a worker named 'bootstrap' waits behind a bootstrap job. Worker-name validation (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$) allows both.
nodes.check: Login node: squeue -u $USER -h -o '%j %T %r' | sort | uniq -c -> no ashley_<name> appears twice; ls ~/.ashley/workers contains neither 'access' nor 'bootstrap'.
failure_signatures: worker PENDING (Dependency) indefinitely
DependencyNeverSatisfied
an admin queue entry whose note is empty and whose job is a worker
nodes.auto_repair: If a same-name job is PENDING and is an older ashley_<w> of this user, scancel it; refuse worker names access and bootstrap (reserved).
nodes.manual_fix: Rename the worker (ashley worker stop --name access; start it under another name).
nodes.future_risk: Any new ashley_* job name (probe jobs, publish jobs) enlarges the collision set.

nodes.title: squeue/sacct answer for the user's own jobs
nodes.assumption: job_state() asks squeue first and sacct second; an empty answer is read as 'job gone'. sacct needs slurmdbd and keeps records only for the retention period.
nodes.check: Login node: squeue -u $USER -h -o %i exits 0 within 10 s; sacct -n -X -j $BOOTSTRAP_JOB -o State returns a state for a job finished today.
failure_signatures: slurm_load_jobs error: Socket timed out on send/recv operation
sacct: error: Problem talking to the database: Connection refused
status shows bootstrap_state empty for a job that ran
worker_json job_state 'none' while the job runs
nodes.auto_repair: Retry after 30 s before acting on an empty state; never start a second worker while squeue errors (singleton is the backstop).
nodes.manual_fix: Wait for slurmctld/slurmdbd; report persistent errors to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm upgrades change output formats; accounting retention purges old BOOTSTRAP_JOB ids so a stale id reads as gone (see the access review's stale BOOTSTRAP_JOB finding).

nodes.title: Wall-time and cancel signals reach ashleyd.js through apptainer
nodes.assumption: #SBATCH --signal=B:TERM@120 signals only the batch shell; because the template ends with 'exec $RUNTIME exec ...', the batch shell IS the apptainer process, which must forward SIGTERM to 'node ashleyd.js'. The daemon then stops claiming and kills running claude children after 90 s, inside the 120 s budget (Slurm may deliver the signal up to 60 s off). A plain scancel sends SIGTERM to every process and SIGKILL after KillWait, so the 90 s grace is not honoured there.
nodes.check: Login node, after a worker ended: grep -E 'stopping \(SIGTERM\)|^.* exit$' ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log/ashleyd.log | tail -2 -> 'stopping (SIGTERM)' followed by 'exit'; scontrol show config | grep -E '^KillWait' (>= 30 s).
failure_signatures: ashleyd.log ends without 'stopping (SIGTERM)'
result status 'cancelled' with error 'claude exited null by SIGKILL without a result'
slurmstepd: error: *** JOB <id> ON <node> CANCELLED AT <time> DUE TO TIME LIMIT ***
state.json frozen at 'busy' after the job ended
nodes.auto_repair: None at runtime; the next daemon start recovers .claimed requests.
nodes.manual_fix: Run apptainer in the background and 'wait' with a bash trap that forwards TERM (also makes the /dev/shm cleanup trap fire); raise the signal lead time.
nodes.future_risk: Apptainer releases change signal forwarding in the starter; Slurm changes --signal timing; a switch to cgroup v2 changes how steps are killed.

nodes.title: A requeued or preempted worker resumes without harm
nodes.assumption: On QoS requeue the job carries --requeue and --open-mode=append; a requeued script restarts from the top on possibly another node, and recoverClaimed() moves *.json.claimed back to the inbox, so a request that was half done runs again from scratch (tool side effects repeat; events.jsonl is appended twice). On any other QoS the job is --no-requeue, so preemption (if secondary is preemptible) simply kills the worker.
nodes.check: Login node: scontrol show job $JID | grep -o 'Restarts=[0-9]*' -> Restarts=0 expected; grep -c 'recovered .*\.claimed' ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log/ashleyd.log counts re-run requests; sacctmgr -n -P show qos requeue,secondary format=name,preempt,preemptmode.
failure_signatures: recovered <id>.json.claimed
slurmstepd: error: *** JOB <id> ON <node> CANCELLED AT <time> DUE TO PREEMPTION ***
two 'start <id>' lines for one id in ashleyd.log
node file changes mid-session (Remote-SSH window loses its host)
nodes.auto_repair: If the job ended by preemption without requeue: ashley worker start --name <w> (inbox survives).
nodes.manual_fix: Keep requests idempotent; use primary QoS for long, side-effecting runs.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT can change PreemptMode or JobRequeue globally; making secondary preemptible would silently kill secp workers.

nodes.title: bootstrap.sbatch completes (own container or library publish)
nodes.assumption: One job (5-15 min, 4 CPU, 16G, 2 h limit, --no-requeue) finds a runtime, builds or reuses the sandbox, installs the pinned Claude Code, smoke-tests, and writes READY + config.env (own) or merges library.json (LIBRARY=1, admin). Exit codes: 1 config/ROOT refused, 2 no runtime, 3 no runtime could exec, 4 npm install failed. It is idempotent: finished pieces are skipped.
nodes.check: Login node: sacct -j $BOOTSTRAP_JOB -X -n -o State,ExitCode -> COMPLETED 0:0; tail -3 ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_$BOOTSTRAP_JOB.out contains 'READY written' (own) or 'published <name>' (library).
failure_signatures: REFUSING: ~/.ashley/config.env missing; run 'ashley install' first
REFUSING: cannot write <ROOT>
STOP: no container runtime found on <host>
STOP: sandbox built but no runtime could exec it
STOP: npm install failed
STOP: <npm>/bin/claude missing after install
LIBRARY=1 needs ROOT_OVERRIDE
nodes.auto_repair: ashley bootstrap --resubmit --partition secp --qos secondary (admin/own build only; students adopt the library instead).
nodes.manual_fix: Read ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_<job>.out; the STOP line names the failed step (runtime, build, npm).
nodes.future_risk: Every vendor update in the chain (module, Docker Hub, npm, Claude Code) surfaces here first; the 2 h limit assumes Docker Hub and npm are fast.

nodes.title: GPU workers get a GPU and apptainer --nv sees it
nodes.assumption: With gpus>0 the job gets '#SBATCH --gres=gpu:N' on gmsap,gvohp,galhp (QoS gpu) and the daemon runs under 'apptainer exec --nv', which binds the host NVIDIA driver libraries into the container.
nodes.check: Login node: sinfo -h -p gmsap,gvohp,galhp -o '%P %G' shows gpu gres. Compute node: CEXEC with --nv inside a GPU worker allocation: nvidia-smi -L -> at least one 'GPU 0:' line.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Invalid generic resource (gres) specification
WARNING: Could not find any nv files on this host!
nvidia-smi: command not found
CUDA error: no CUDA-capable device is detected
nodes.manual_fix: Start a CPU worker, or ask C&IT which GPU partition/gres name applies to the account.
nodes.future_risk: Driver upgrades, new gres type names (gpu:h200), GPU partitions renamed; library GPU images must still carry Node 22 at /usr/local/bin/node (see container.image-contents).

nodes.title: Environment modules work in a batch shell and apptainer/1.2.2 is available
nodes.assumption: Compute nodes have /etc/profile.d/modules.sh defining 'module' in a non-interactive batch shell, and 'module load apptainer/1.2.2' yields /wsu/el7/gnu7/apptainer/1.2.2/bin/apptainer. Other candidates tried in order: conda singularity under ~/mambaforge or ~/miniforge3, module singularity/3.5.2, /usr/bin/apptainer, /usr/bin/singularity; ~/.local/bin/singularity is deliberately skipped (partial install).
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(bash -c 'source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh && module -t avail apptainer 2>&1') -> lists apptainer/1.2.2.
failure_signatures: module: command not found
ERROR: Unable to locate a modulefile for 'apptainer/1.2.2'
ModuleCmd_Load.c(213):ERROR:105: Unable to locate a modulefile for 'apptainer/1.2.2'
runtime candidates: (empty)
STOP: no container runtime found on <host>
nodes.auto_repair: Pick the newest apptainer/* module that 'module -t avail' lists (sort -V | tail -1), pass it to the bootstrap and resubmit.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu which apptainer module replaced 1.2.2.
nodes.future_risk: The el7 -> el8/el9 migration renames module trees (/wsu/el9/...), Lmod may replace Tcl modules, and 1.2.2 will be retired; the version is hard-coded.

nodes.title: The recorded RUNTIME path runs on every compute node without 'module load'
nodes.assumption: RUNTIME is stored as an absolute path (config.env, and library.json 'runtime' for shared containers) and the worker executes it directly, without loading the module's environment; the path must exist and work on whichever node Slurm picks.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(bash -c 'source ~/.ashley/config.env; test -x "$RUNTIME" && "$RUNTIME" --version') -> 'apptainer version 1.2.2'.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: runtime <path> missing on <host>
exit 127
apptainer: error while loading shared libraries
nodes.auto_repair: Own container: ashley bootstrap --resubmit (the sandbox exists, so only discovery and the config rewrite run). Shared container: admin republishes the entry (or patches library.json 'runtime'), then ashley adopt <entry> for each student.
nodes.manual_fix: Tell the lab admin the runtime path in library.json no longer exists.
nodes.future_risk: The path embeds the OS and compiler (/wsu/el7/gnu7/...), so an OS upgrade breaks every stored RUNTIME at once.

nodes.title: Unprivileged user namespaces are enabled on compute nodes
nodes.assumption: The apptainer module runs non-setuid, so both 'build --sandbox' and 'exec' need /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces > 0 on the node. Never use --fakeroot: uid 0 inside makes Claude Code refuse --dangerously-skip-permissions.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(cat /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces) -> a number > 0, and CEXEC(id -u) -> the user's uid (not 0).
failure_signatures: Failed to create user namespace
user namespace not supported
--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons
nodes.auto_repair: Resubmit the job with --exclude=<node> if only some nodes have it disabled.
nodes.manual_fix: Report the node to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: Security hardening after a user-namespace CVE (as some distributions did) would disable unprivileged Apptainer grid-wide.

nodes.title: ROOT (container, npm prefix, caches, workspaces) is writable with room
nodes.assumption: ROOT defaults to /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER/ashley when that directory exists and is writable, else $HOME/ashley. It holds containers/ (1.1 GB sandbox), npm/, npm-cache/, cache/ (APPTAINER_CACHEDIR), tmp/ (APPTAINER_TMPDIR, TMPDIR during the build) and workspaces/. It must be writable from compute nodes and under quota.
nodes.check: Login node: source ~/.ashley/config.env; test -w "$ROOT"; df-ceph oschome (usage < 90 %). Compute node: PROBE(bash -c 'source ~/.ashley/config.env; touch $ROOT/tmp/.p && rm $ROOT/tmp/.p').
failure_signatures: REFUSING: cannot write <ROOT>
FAIL  ROOT not writable (<path>)
EDQUOT: disk quota exceeded
No space left on device
nodes.auto_repair: Clear $ROOT/cache and $ROOT/tmp (safe, regenerated) in a job; recreate missing subdirectories with mkdir -p.
nodes.manual_fix: Free space on the lab volume or set ashley.gridRoot to a location with room.
nodes.future_risk: The CephFS allocation (from 2026-09-21) can be resized, moved or renamed; students without /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER fall back to the nearly full Panasas home.

nodes.title: Compute nodes reach the internet directly
nodes.assumption: Compute nodes have outbound HTTPS without a proxy (verified to zenodo.org and api.anthropic.com), so Docker Hub, npm, Anthropic, GitHub, Hugging Face and the VS Code download CDN are reachable from jobs. Containers share the host network namespace.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(curl -s -m 8 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.anthropic.com/) -> any code other than 000.
failure_signatures: net=000 in the bootstrap smoke line
curl: (7) Failed to connect
curl: (28) Connection timed out
nodes.manual_fix: Report egress loss to hpc@wayne.edu; if C&IT introduces a proxy, set HTTPS_PROXY for jobs.
nodes.future_risk: A campus egress firewall, a mandatory proxy, IPv6-only changes or TLS inspection would break every external dependency at once.

nodes.title: Docker Hub serves docker://node:22-bookworm to the grid
nodes.assumption: registry-1.docker.io, auth.docker.io and its CDN are reachable, the tag exists, and the anonymous pull quota for the grid's shared egress IP is not exhausted. Only builds (admin publishes, --build-own) pull; students adopt.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(curl -s -m 8 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/) -> 401 (reachable, auth required). Rate headroom: fetch an anonymous token from auth.docker.io for repository:ratelimitpreview/test:pull and HEAD its manifest; read the ratelimit-remaining header (> 0).
failure_signatures: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit
dial tcp: lookup registry-1.docker.io: no such host
manifest unknown
FATAL:   While making image from oci registry: error fetching image to cache
nodes.auto_repair: Retry after the rate window, or rebuild from the same official image through a mirror: IMAGE=docker://public.ecr.aws/docker/library/node:22-bookworm.
nodes.manual_fix: Authenticate pulls (APPTAINER_DOCKER_USERNAME/PASSWORD) or wait.
nodes.future_risk: Docker Hub has tightened anonymous limits before; all grid nodes likely share few egress IPs, so one heavy user exhausts the quota for everyone.

nodes.title: The base image tag is stable enough, and Node 22 is supported
nodes.assumption: docker://node:22-bookworm is a moving tag: a rebuild months later gives newer Node 22.x and Debian packages than the entry recorded. Node 22 reaches end of life on 2027-04-30; bookworm's glibc 2.36 stays above Claude Code's floor.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'node -v; ldd --version | head -1') -> v22.x and glibc 2.36; login node: the library.json entry's 'image' and 'built' fields.
failure_signatures: a republished entry behaves differently from the old one
npm WARN EBADENGINE
nodes.manual_fix: Pin by digest when publishing (docker://node:22-bookworm@sha256:<digest>) and record the digest; before April 2027 publish a node:24 entry and make it the default.
nodes.future_risk: Node 22 EOL; Debian bookworm moving to LTS; Claude Code raising its Node or glibc floor.

nodes.title: apptainer build --sandbox works unprivileged on a compute node
nodes.assumption: A sandbox directory (not a SIF: SIF-to-sandbox conversion failed on this grid and some nodes lack unsquashfs) is built into $SANDBOX.part with APPTAINER_CACHEDIR/TMPDIR on ROOT, checked for /usr/local/bin/node, then moved into place. Measured: 6-7 min, 1.1 GB.
nodes.check: Login node: source ~/.ashley/config.env; test -x "$SANDBOX/usr/local/bin/node" && test ! -e "$SANDBOX.part"; the bootstrap log contains 'built <size>' or 'sandbox exists'.
failure_signatures: build with <runtime> failed:
FATAL:   While performing build:
INFO:    Converting SIF file to temporary sandbox...
no space left on device
nodes.auto_repair: rm -rf "$SANDBOX.part"; clear $ROOT/cache in a job; resubmit the bootstrap.
nodes.manual_fix: Admin only; students use the lab container.
nodes.future_risk: Apptainer releases change unprivileged build behaviour; CephFS quota; many small files on CephFS.

nodes.title: The image carries Node at /usr/local/bin/node, npm, bash, git, curl and python3
nodes.assumption: /usr/local/bin/node is the readiness marker everywhere (build, exec test, worker preflight, adopt); npm installs Claude Code; python3 merges library.json for LIBRARY=1; git/curl are in the smoke test; ashleyd.js needs Node >= 16.7 (crypto.randomUUID, fs.rmSync). Images without Node at that path (INSTALL.md's nvidia/cuda example) fail the marker, every runtime candidate rebuilds, and the job ends 'no runtime could exec'. A python3-less image skips the library merge unchecked yet still prints 'published'.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'for b in node npm bash git curl python3; do command -v $b >/dev/null || echo MISSING $b; done; test -x /usr/local/bin/node || echo MISSING marker') -> no output.
failure_signatures: build with <runtime> failed:
STOP: sandbox built but no runtime could exec it
python3: not found
'published <name>' in the log without 'library entry written: <name>'
nodes.manual_fix: Base GPU and R entries on an image that installs Node 22 at /usr/local/bin (or add it in a definition file) and has python3.
nodes.future_risk: The official node image changing its layout or dropping python3/git in slimmer variants.

nodes.title: library.json is readable and its default entry points at real files
nodes.assumption: /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/library.json is readable by the student, parses with the grep-based parser (one-level objects, no '}' inside strings), names a default, and the entry's sandbox, claude_bin and runtime exist and are readable/executable.
nodes.check: Login node: ashley library --json -> available true; for the default: test -x <sandbox>/usr/local/bin/node && test -r <claude_bin> && test -x <runtime>.
failure_signatures: no shared library readable at /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley (ask your lead for the oschome group)
no library entry '<name>' (ashley library)
cannot read the shared container <path> (ask your lead for the oschome group)
cannot read <claude_bin>
nodes.auto_repair: ashley adopt <default> once the entry is valid.
nodes.manual_fix: Lab admin: republish the entry or run ashley access admin resync.
nodes.future_risk: A library.json schema change or a 'purpose' text containing '}' breaks lib_field; entries pinned to an old runtime path break at OS upgrade.

nodes.title: Named-user ACLs on the lab folder are enforced for a non-owner on compute nodes
nodes.assumption: Approval grants read through setfacl u:<id>:r-X; the only test was as the owner (whose access never consults the named entry), and compute nodes may mount CephFS with different ACL options than the login node. Not known yet.
nodes.check: Compute node, as a student: PROBE(test -x /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/containers/<entry>/usr/local/bin/node && echo READABLE).
failure_signatures: REFUSING: sandbox <path> incomplete (on the node while the login node reads it)
Permission denied
nodes.auto_repair: Admin: ashley access admin resync.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the non-owner test from the access review (a second account, ls on login and via srun on a node); report mount differences to C&IT.
nodes.future_risk: CephFS client changes (kernel vs fuse, client_acl_type) at OS upgrades.

nodes.title: An admin publish merges the entry and leaves the tree group-readable
nodes.assumption: ashley library publish submits bootstrap.sbatch with LIBRARY=1 ROOT_OVERRIDE LIB_NAME IMAGE GPU PURPOSE; the job merges library.json with the container's python3 (atomic .part rename), runs chmod -R g+rX,g-w,o-rwx and setgid on directories, then ashley access admin resync.
nodes.check: Login node: grep -c '"<name>"' /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley/library.json -> 1; stat -c %a /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley -> 2750; the publish log has 'library entry written: <name>'.
failure_signatures: only the lab admin publishes containers
LIBRARY=1 needs ROOT_OVERRIDE
npm error code ENOENT (shared ROOT not bound; fixed in a38812e)
'published' without 'library entry written'
nodes.auto_repair: Rerun the publish (the merge is idempotent).
nodes.manual_fix: Admin reads ~/.ashley/log/bootstrap_<job>.out.
nodes.future_risk: Mode changes in a later version reopening the library (access review findings on 2775).

nodes.title: READY and config.env describe a usable container
nodes.assumption: Satisfied by EITHER path (follow the one config.env SOURCE names): own build (bootstrap writes RUNTIME, SANDBOX, CLAUDE_BIN, BINDS, BOOTSTRAP_STATE=done and READY) or adoption (ashley adopt writes the same keys from library.json, SOURCE=shared). is_ready requires READY non-empty, CLAUDE_BIN executable and $SANDBOX/usr/local/bin/node executable.
nodes.check: Login node: ashley status --json -> ready true; grep -cE '^(ROOT|RUNTIME|SANDBOX|CLAUDE_BIN|BINDS)=' ~/.ashley/config.env -> 5.
failure_signatures: FAIL  not ready (bootstrap job <id>: <state>)
grid not ready yet (bootstrap job ...)
no container yet: it comes with lab access
REFUSING: <VAR> unset in config.env (bootstrap not finished?)
nodes.auto_repair: If the library is readable: ashley adopt <default>; admin with no library: ashley bootstrap --resubmit.
nodes.manual_fix: Students: wait for lab access (the wizard's last step). Admin: read the bootstrap log.
nodes.future_risk: A stale BOOTSTRAP_JOB can block the awaiting-access path (access review finding).

nodes.title: The container sees home, the CephFS tree, ROOT and the lab folder
nodes.assumption: BINDS holds -B $HOME, -B /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER (if it exists), -B $ROOT when outside those, and -B /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared for adopted or library sandboxes (added again by the template when the sandbox lives there). Binding the parent '-B /rs' does NOT expose the tree (/rs is a symlink into /.rs/volumes); each path is bound explicitly. BINDS is word-split, so paths must not contain spaces.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'for p in "$HOME" "$ROOT" /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared "$(dirname $CLAUDE_BIN)"; do test -r "$p" || echo MISSING $p; done') -> no output; login node: grep ^BINDS= ~/.ashley/config.env.
failure_signatures: npm error code ENOENT (on the shared path)
No such file or directory (for a file that exists on the host)
cannot open file
nodes.auto_repair: Rerun ashley adopt <entry> (recomputes BINDS including the lab folder) or append the missing -B to BINDS in config.env; restart the worker.
nodes.manual_fix: Tell the lab admin which host path is missing inside the worker.
nodes.future_risk: New lab storage (another volume, datasets elsewhere) needs a bind that nothing adds automatically; an OS upgrade moving /rs.

nodes.title: /dev/shm scratch exists, has room, and is cleaned up
nodes.assumption: /tmp on nodes is swept by a cleaner, so each job uses /dev/shm/${USER}_ashley_<name>_<job> bound to /tmp inside the container (TMPDIR=/tmp; Claude's temp tree and tool output land there). tmpfs pages count against the job's memory limit. The worker template sets 'trap rm -rf $SCR EXIT' and then 'exec's apptainer, which replaces the shell, so the trap never runs and every worker job leaves its directory behind on the node.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(bash -c 'df -h /dev/shm | tail -1; ls -d /dev/shm/${USER}_ashley_* 2>/dev/null') -> free space > 2 GB and every listed suffix is a job id in 'squeue -u $USER -h -o %i'.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: no /dev/shm scratch
ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
slurmstepd: error: Detected 1 oom-kill event(s) in StepId=<id>.batch
nodes.auto_repair: PROBE on that node: remove /dev/shm/${USER}_ashley_*_<jobid> and ${USER}_ashley_boot_<jobid> whose job id is not in the user's squeue list.
nodes.manual_fix: Change the template to run apptainer in the background and 'wait', so the trap fires.
nodes.future_risk: A job_container/tmpfs plugin or an epilog that cleans /dev/shm (helpful) or a smaller /dev/shm on new nodes.
nodes.source: grid/worker.sbatch.tpl:39-41,45; grid/bootstrap.sbatch:42; CLAUDE.md (Grid: /tmp is node-local and swept)

nodes.title: apptainer exec runs Node inside the sandbox as the user
nodes.assumption: $RUNTIME exec $BINDS -B <shm>:/tmp $SANDBOX node ... prints 'node v22...' on a compute node, without SIF conversion; uid inside equals the user's (non-root) and apptainer's adapted /etc/passwd has the user (os.userInfo() in the daemon's peer note throws otherwise, leaving the request stuck as .claimed).
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'node -v; id -u; getent passwd $(id -u) | cut -d: -f1') -> v22.x, a non-zero uid, the AccessID.
failure_signatures: runtime <rt> cannot exec: <output>
FATAL:   while executing starter: /usr/libexec/singularity/bin/starter not found
INFO:    Converting SIF file to temporary sandbox...
exit 127
uv_os_get_passwd returned ENOENT
nodes.auto_repair: ashley bootstrap --resubmit (rediscovers a runtime that can exec) or ashley adopt for shared containers.
nodes.manual_fix: Report the runtime/node to the lab admin.
nodes.future_risk: Apptainer config changes (config passwd = no, mount home = no), a switch from userns to setuid or vice versa.

nodes.title: Only intended environment reaches Claude inside the container
nodes.assumption: sbatch exports the submitting ssh session's environment (which sourced ~/.bashrc) and apptainer passes host variables into the container (PATH is reset). The daemon deletes CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC, DISABLE_TELEMETRY; other routing variables (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX, HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_OPTIONS, APPTAINERENV_*) are not removed and would change where requests go or how Node runs.
nodes.check: Compute node, inside the worker allocation: PROBE(bash -c 'env | cut -d= -f1 | grep -E "^(ANTHROPIC_|CLAUDE_CODE_USE_|NODE_OPTIONS|HTTPS?_PROXY|APPTAINERENV_|SINGULARITYENV_)"') -> empty (names only; values are never printed).
failure_signatures: API Error: 401 against a non-Anthropic base URL
Could not load credentials from any providers
usage billed to an unexpected provider
nodes.manual_fix: Remove those exports from ~/.bashrc (or guard them), then restart the worker; long term the daemon should delete them too.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code adds new env knobs that override auth or endpoints.

nodes.title: DNS and TLS work inside the container
nodes.assumption: The container uses apptainer's adapted /etc/resolv.conf and Debian bookworm's CA bundle; no TLS interception and no proxy are needed for api.anthropic.com, registry.npmjs.org, github.com and huggingface.co.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'for u in api.anthropic.com registry.npmjs.org github.com huggingface.co; do printf "%s " $u; curl -s -m 8 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://$u/; done') -> no 000.
failure_signatures: curl: (6) Could not resolve host
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY
smoke: ... net=000
nodes.manual_fix: If C&IT adds TLS inspection, set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and SSL_CERT_FILE for the worker; if a proxy appears, HTTPS_PROXY.
nodes.future_risk: CA rotations make an old, never-rebuilt sandbox's bundle stale; campus network policy changes.

nodes.title: npm can fetch the pinned @anthropic-ai/claude-code from the registry
nodes.assumption: registry.npmjs.org is reachable from the container, version 2.1.283 is still published with its linux-x64 native binary, and the user's ~/.npmrc (visible because $HOME is bound) does not set another registry, ignore-scripts=true or omit=optional, any of which can leave a broken install. npm_config_cache points at $ROOT/npm-cache.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.283 version; npm config get registry; npm config get ignore-scripts') -> 2.1.283, https://registry.npmjs.org/, false.
failure_signatures: npm error code ETARGET
npm error code E404
npm error code ENOTFOUND
npm error network request to https://registry.npmjs.org/... failed
npm error code EINTEGRITY
STOP: npm install failed
nodes.auto_repair: Remove $ROOT/npm-cache (or npm cache verify) and rerun the bootstrap with UPDATE=1; set npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ explicitly in the install command.
nodes.manual_fix: Fix ~/.npmrc; if the version was deprecated, choose a newer pin and republish.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic could steer distribution away from npm toward the native installer; npm policy changes; registry outages.

nodes.title: The pinned Claude Code binary is installed and executable
nodes.assumption: $NPM_PREFIX/bin/claude exists, is executable by the user (group/ACL X for shared entries), and 'claude --version' prints '2.1.283 (Claude Code)'. The bootstrap's idempotency compares the first field with CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION; if the output format changes it reinstalls every run.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'source ~/.ashley/config.env; $CLAUDE_BIN --version') -> '2.1.283 (Claude Code)'; login node: claude_version in ~/.ashley/READY and in each worker's state.json agree.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: <path>/bin/claude missing
STOP: <path>/bin/claude missing after install
Permission denied
claude_version differs between READY and state.json
nodes.auto_repair: Own container: ashley bootstrap --update (UPDATE=1 reinstalls at the pin). Shared: admin publishes a new entry; students ashley adopt.
nodes.manual_fix: Admin republishes.
nodes.future_risk: Each Claude Code release; npm packaging changes (native binary delivery).

nodes.title: The container's glibc satisfies Claude Code's Bun binary
nodes.assumption: Claude Code is a Bun native ELF; since about 2.1.243 it needs GLIBC_2.26+ and it has crashed on CentOS 7.9's glibc 2.17, so it runs only inside the container (bookworm, glibc 2.36), never on the host.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'ldd --version | head -1; objdump -T $(readlink -f $CLAUDE_BIN) 2>/dev/null | grep -o "GLIBC_[0-9.]*" | sort -uV | tail -1') -> 2.36 and a required symbol version <= 2.36.
failure_signatures: version `GLIBC_2.xx' not found
Illegal instruction (core dumped)
nodes.manual_fix: Publish an entry from a newer base image (Debian trixie / Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 22+).
nodes.future_risk: A future Claude Code build requiring glibc newer than bookworm's 2.36.

nodes.title: The node's kernel and CPU run the Claude Code binary
nodes.assumption: The host kernel (reported 5.15) and each node's CPU instruction set can run the Bun ELF; a SIGILL was reported on a CentOS 7.9 host (cause, kernel or glibc, not settled). Old nodes may lack instructions a new build selects.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(bash -c 'uname -r; grep -m1 -o -w avx2 /proc/cpuinfo') and CEXEC($CLAUDE_BIN --version; echo rc=$?) -> rc=0 (not 132/135).
failure_signatures: Illegal instruction (core dumped)
exit 132
panic(main thread): Illegal instruction
Bus error (exit 135)
nodes.auto_repair: Record the failing node and restart the worker with --exclude=<node>.
nodes.manual_fix: Pin the last Claude Code version that ran, or use a constraint for newer CPUs.
nodes.future_risk: New Claude/Bun builds raising the ISA baseline; an OS upgrade to a RHEL 8 kernel (4.18).

nodes.title: Claude Code does not update itself or write into the shared prefix
nodes.assumption: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 keep the pinned version (so every student runs the same bits) and avoid writes into the read-only shared npm prefix.
nodes.check: Login node: claude_version in state.json of every worker equals the entry's claude_version in library.json/READY across restarts.
failure_signatures: claude_version drifts between workers
EACCES: permission denied (writing under the npm prefix)
nodes.auto_repair: ashley bootstrap --update for own containers.
nodes.manual_fix: Admin republishes the entry.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code renaming these variables (DISABLE_UPDATES was added alongside).

nodes.title: The pinned claude accepts every flag the daemon passes
nodes.assumption: argv = -p <prompt> --output-format stream-json --verbose (--dangerously-skip-permissions | --permission-mode <mode>) --max-turns N [--model M] [--allowedTools a,b] --append-system-prompt <note> (--resume <uuid> | --session-id <uuid>). stream-json with --print requires --verbose (verified on 2.1.283). --bare must never be added (it ignores CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN). --dangerously-skip-permissions is refused as root.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC($CLAUDE_BIN --help) contains --output-format, --verbose, --permission-mode, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --model, --allowedTools, --append-system-prompt, --resume, --session-id; hidden flags (--max-turns) are proven by the zero-cost canary in container.claude-stream-json-contract not printing 'unknown option'.
failure_signatures: error: unknown option '--max-turns'
Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose
--dangerously-skip-permissions cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons
Error: Invalid session ID
nodes.auto_repair: Reinstall the last pin that passed (bootstrap UPDATE=1 CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=<previous>).
nodes.manual_fix: Update ashleyd.js argv to the renamed flags and republish.
nodes.future_risk: Flag renames or removals in Claude Code; --bare becoming the -p default (the docs call it the recommended script mode) would silently stop subscription auth.

nodes.title: claude -p emits NDJSON ending in a result event the daemon parses
nodes.assumption: Each stdout line is JSON; the turn's last is {type:'result', is_error, subtype, result, session_id, total_cost_usd, duration_ms, num_turns, usage}. A result arrives even on auth failure (is_error true). The error arm carries errors[] and may lack 'result'; the daemon reports only 'subtype', so the cause is lost.
nodes.check: Compute node, zero cost (no valid token used): CEXEC(bash -c 'CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=sk-ant-oat01-invalid $CLAUDE_BIN -p ping --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 1 | tail -1') -> JSON with "type":"result" and "is_error":true. Laptop: npm run test:unit passes (daemon.test.ts with fake-claude.js).
failure_signatures: claude exited <code> without a result: <stderr>
status error with empty result on every request
result error 'error_during_execution' with no further detail
nodes.auto_repair: Reinstall the last pin that passed the canary.
nodes.manual_fix: Adapt ashleyd.js parsing; include result.errors in the error text.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic changes stream-json event names or fields (cost, usage) in any release.

nodes.title: api.anthropic.com answers from compute nodes
nodes.assumption: The worker's claude reaches api.anthropic.com; the token check (GET /v1/models with anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20 and anthropic-version: 2023-06-01) returns 200 for a valid setup-token token and 401 for an invalid one. The grid's verify treats any other code (000, 403, 429, 5xx) as 'present', which is not verification.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(curl -s -m 15 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models) -> 401 unauthenticated (reachable). Login node: ashley verify-tokens -> 'CLAUDE_TOKEN ok'.
failure_signatures: CLAUDE_TOKEN present (the check answered HTTP 000)
overloaded_error
API Error: 529
net=000
nodes.auto_repair: Retry with backoff; report 000 as unverified rather than passing.
nodes.manual_fix: Check status.anthropic.com; report persistent 000 from nodes to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: The oauth beta header or API version is retired; the endpoint's behaviour for OAuth tokens changes (the code a valid token receives was not yet recorded with a real token).

nodes.title: At least one enabled Claude credential directory exists
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/accounts/<name>/ holds 'token' (setup-token, sk-ant-oat...), or 'apikey', or '.credentials.json'; files 600, directory 700; not 'disabled'; subscriptions sort before API keys, 'default' first. Token files are re-read on every request.
nodes.check: Login node: ashley accounts list -> non-empty with enabled true; stat -c %a ~/.ashley/accounts/default/token -> 600; head -c 10 ~/.ashley/accounts/default/token -> sk-ant-oat (prefix only, never the value).
failure_signatures: no enabled Claude account in ~/.ashley/accounts (run the Ashley setup wizard or `ashley accounts add-token`)
every enabled Claude account is on cooldown until <time>
worker status 'blocked'
nodes.auto_repair: If the laptop's SecretStorage holds a Claude token and the grid has none, push it (pushTokens: ssh stdin, umask 077); clear a cooldown only when cooldown_until is already past (ashley accounts enable <name>).
nodes.manual_fix: Ashley: Store or replace my Claude token for the grid (runs claude setup-token).
nodes.future_risk: Token format changes (the pattern expects sk-ant-oat).

nodes.title: The grid's Claude credential authenticates
nodes.assumption: Token accounts reach Claude Code as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (one-year token from claude setup-token, Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise only, not refreshed after a 401); API-key accounts as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; '.credentials.json' copies die with their refresh token (seen after eight idle days).
nodes.check: Login node: ashley verify-tokens -> 'CLAUDE_TOKEN ok (subscription token accepted)' (one tiny GET, token fed to curl on stdin).
failure_signatures: Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed
OAuth access token is invalid
CLAUDE_TOKEN rejected (invalid, expired or revoked: run claude setup-token again)
authentication_failed
nodes.auto_repair: If the laptop holds a newer token than the grid copy, push it; otherwise prompt Renew (claude setup-token on the laptop).
nodes.manual_fix: Run Ashley: Store or replace my Claude token for the grid and press Authorize on claude.ai.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic changes token lifetime, format, the beta header, or how -p usage is charged to subscriptions.

nodes.title: The subscription window is not exhausted
nodes.assumption: Pro/Max five-hour and weekly windows have room; rotation happens only among the student's own credentials (subscription first, own API key as overflow), never across people.
nodes.check: Login node: grep -h cooldown_until ~/.ashley/accounts/*/state.json; ashley worker list --json -> state.status not 'blocked'.
failure_signatures: You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm
You've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am
status rate_limited with retry_after
credits_required
nodes.auto_repair: None beyond the daemon's own rotation; wait for retry_after.
nodes.manual_fix: Wait for the reset, or add an API key with a spending cap.
nodes.future_risk: Plan limits and wording change.

nodes.title: Limit messages are recognised and the reset time parsed
nodes.assumption: Seven regexes (hit your limit, usage limit reached, rate limit, too many requests, 429, out of usage, overloaded_error) detect exhaustion; parseResetTime handles 'try again in N' and 'resets 3:45pm' in the container's local time zone (apptainer binds /etc/localtime); 'resets Mon 12:00am' does not match and falls back to 60 minutes; stream-json's rate_limit_event (resetsAt) is ignored. The patterns exist twice (protocol.ts and ashleyd.js) and must agree.
nodes.check: Laptop: npm run test:unit (protocol.test.ts, daemon.test.ts); diff the pattern lists in protocol.ts:111-119 and ashleyd.js:57. Compute node: CEXEC(date +%Z) -> EDT/EST, not UTC.
failure_signatures: status error (not rate_limited) whose result text contains 'hit your'
hourly retries during a weekly limit
cooldown_until off by 4-5 hours
nodes.manual_fix: Parse rate_limit_event.resetsAt; keep one pattern list.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic rewords limit messages or adds weekday/timezone formats; overloaded_error (a server-side 529) is counted as the student's limit and puts the account on cooldown for an hour.

nodes.title: A named session resumes under the account and directory that hold its transcript
nodes.assumption: sessions/<name>.json maps to a session id whose transcript is <account dir>/projects/<encoded cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl, and the cwd still exists. resolveSession ignores the stored account, so after a rate-limit rotation or a forced account the next --resume runs under a different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and should not find the transcript. Transcripts older than cleanupPeriodDays (30) are deleted by Claude Code.
nodes.check: Login node: for each ~/.ashley/sessions/*.json, ls ~/.ashley/accounts/<account>/projects/*/<session_id>.jsonl exists and test -d <cwd>.
failure_signatures: No conversation found with session ID: <uuid> (expected wording; capture the exact text on first occurrence)
second turn of a session fails right after 'requeued <id> for account <other>'
nodes.auto_repair: If the transcript sits under another account, resend with that account; if it is gone, rewrite the session entry so the next turn starts a new session id instead of resuming.
nodes.manual_fix: Start a new session name.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code changing its session storage layout or retention.

nodes.title: Concurrent claude processes share one CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR safely
nodes.assumption: Each account directory is the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for every run of every worker of that account (concurrency 2 per worker, several workers possible), on the shared Panasas home. Whether Claude Code tolerates concurrent writers to .claude.json/history.jsonl on a network filesystem is not documented either way (the research claim that Anthropic advises against it was refuted).
nodes.check: Login node: running workers x concurrency per account; ls ~/.ashley/accounts/*/ | grep -E 'corrupt|backup' -> none.
failure_signatures: a .claude.json.corrupted.* or backup file appears
Claude reports its configuration file is corrupted
history entries missing
nodes.manual_fix: Use concurrency 1, or give each worker its own config directory per account.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code storing more state (plugins, memory) in the config dir.

nodes.title: Claude's Bash tool can start a login shell inside the container
nodes.assumption: Claude's Bash tool snapshots a login shell that sources ~/.bashrc inside the container. The student's bashrc (module calls, conda hooks, /etc/profile.d/modules.sh, which the container lacks) must not error or hang; a public issue (#42952) saw every Bash command fail under HPC cgroups, Apptainer and Lmod. The ashley block adds ~/.ashley/bin to PATH, which the peer note relies on.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(env -i HOME=$HOME TERM=dumb bash -lc 'echo SNAPSHOT_OK; command -v ashley') -> SNAPSHOT_OK and ~/.ashley/bin/ashley within 5 s, nothing on stderr.
failure_signatures: bash: module: command not found
/etc/profile.d/modules.sh: No such file or directory
Bash tool calls failing or timing out on every command
nodes.manual_fix: Guard HPC-only lines in ~/.bashrc with '[ -z "$APPTAINER_CONTAINER" ]' or '[ -f /etc/profile.d/modules.sh ]'; set CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL=/bin/bash.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code changing its snapshot mechanism; WSU changing the default bashrc skeleton.

nodes.title: Slurm commands inside the worker container (currently not provided)
nodes.assumption: LIMITS.md says the worker Claude can submit and poll jobs, and the peer note tells it to 'ashley worker start'. Nothing binds sbatch/squeue/scancel, /etc/slurm or the munge socket into the container, so from Claude's shell they should be missing. 'ashley send' still works because job_state swallows the missing squeue. Not tested from inside a worker.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'command -v sbatch squeue scancel || echo MISSING') -> today expected MISSING; pass once bound.
failure_signatures: bash: sbatch: command not found
ashley: sbatch failed: ... command not found
queued <id> on worker <w> (job ... not running)
nodes.manual_fix: Bind the site's Slurm client binaries, libraries, /etc/slurm and /var/run/munge into the container (site-specific paths), or route job submission through a login-node request; until then, correct LIMITS.md and the peer note.
nodes.future_risk: A Slurm upgrade moving client library/plugin paths breaks any bind added for this.

nodes.title: The worker job passes its REFUSING checks
nodes.assumption: Before exec, the job sources config.env and refuses unless RUNTIME, SANDBOX, CLAUDE_BIN and ROOT are set, $SANDBOX/usr/local/bin/node and CLAUDE_BIN are executable and RUNTIME exists on this node; it then writes 'node' (hostname -f) and 'job.id'.
nodes.check: Login node: grep REFUSING $(ls -t ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log/slurm_*.out | head -1) -> nothing; test -s ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/node.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: no config.env
REFUSING: <VAR> unset in config.env (bootstrap not finished?)
REFUSING: sandbox <path> incomplete
REFUSING: <path> missing
REFUSING: runtime <path> missing on <host>
REFUSING: no /dev/shm scratch
nodes.auto_repair: Follow the named node: missing sandbox/claude -> ashley adopt (shared) or bootstrap --resubmit (own); runtime missing on host -> container.runtime-path repair; then ashley worker start.
nodes.manual_fix: Read the REFUSING line; it names the broken piece.
nodes.future_risk: New required config keys added by a later Ashley version while an old config.env remains.

nodes.title: ashleyd.js is running and heartbeating
nodes.assumption: While the worker job is RUNNING, the daemon rewrites state.json every 10 s (alive = mtime younger than 90 s on the login node's clock) and polls the inbox every 250 ms; an exception inside tick is logged and polling continues.
nodes.check: Login node: ashley worker list --json -> job_state RUNNING and alive true; tail -3 ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log/ashleyd.log shows no 'uncaughtException'.
failure_signatures: alive false while job_state RUNNING
uncaughtException
tick error
ashleyd: --worker-dir is required
the job COMPLETED seconds after starting
nodes.auto_repair: ashley worker stop --name <w>; ashley worker start --name <w> (inbox and .claimed requests survive).
nodes.manual_fix: Send ashley worker log --name <w> to the lab admin.
nodes.future_risk: Node.js API changes in a newer container Node; an Ashley upgrade left half-applied.

nodes.title: The job's CPU, memory and pid limits hold the daemon, claude runs and VS Code
nodes.assumption: 4 CPU / 16G (defaults) cover the daemon, up to CONCURRENCY claude processes and their tools, the /dev/shm scratch (counted as memory), and the Remote-SSH VS Code server that pam_slurm_adopt places into the same job.
nodes.check: Login node: sstat -j $JID.batch -n -o MaxRSS; sacct -j $JID -o MaxRSS,State; grep -c oom-kill ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log/slurm_$JID.out -> 0.
failure_signatures: slurmstepd: error: Detected 1 oom-kill event(s) in StepId=<id>.batch
claude exited 137
fork: retry: Resource temporarily unavailable
nodes.auto_repair: After an OOM, restart the worker with --mem doubled (up to 64G) when the queue allows.
nodes.manual_fix: Lower ashley.worker.concurrency or raise ashley.worker.memory.
nodes.future_risk: A cgroup v2 migration changes accounting and enforces pids.max.

nodes.title: The home directory has room for ~/.ashley and ~/.vscode-server
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley (inbox, outbox events, account dirs holding Claude transcripts, sessions, state) and ~/.vscode-server live on the Panasas home (soft quota about 4.3 TB, measured 93 % full). Every state/result write is an atomic .part+rename that fails on EDQUOT, and a failed result write loses that request's answer.
nodes.check: Login node: pan_quota (used < 95 % of soft); du -sh ~/.ashley ~/.vscode-server.
failure_signatures: EDQUOT: disk quota exceeded
ENOSPC: no space left on device
tick error Error: EDQUOT
FAIL  home quota ...
nodes.auto_repair: Delete outbox/*.events.jsonl and outbox/*.json older than 30 days; prune old VS Code server builds (grid-node.vscode-server-install). Never delete transcripts automatically.
nodes.manual_fix: Move large data to the lab volume.
nodes.future_risk: Quota policy changes; transcripts growing under the account dirs.

nodes.title: Login and compute nodes see one consistent ~/.ashley
nodes.assumption: The relay on the login node writes inbox files (.part then rename) and the daemon on a compute node sees them in readdir within one 250 ms poll; rename-to-.claimed is atomic across clients; events.jsonl appends made on the node are visible to stat/tail on the login node. Measured receipt 0.19 s median.
nodes.check: Login node: node-ashley-cli latency 5 (from the laptop) -> receipt under 1 s; or write ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/probe.$$ on login and PROBE(ls) it from the node within 1 s.
failure_signatures: 'queued <id>' but no events for minutes while the worker is idle
receipt latency far above 1 s
the same id claimed twice
nodes.manual_fix: Report to the lab admin; lengthen the poll.
nodes.future_risk: A home migration off Panasas to an NFS-style store with attribute caching would break the 250 ms assumption.

nodes.title: Node, login node and file server clocks agree
nodes.assumption: Liveness compares state.json's mtime with the login node's clock (90 s), the peer note compares last_beat with the node's clock, and cooldowns are ISO times; a skew of more than a few seconds misreports liveness.
nodes.check: Login node: date +%s versus PROBE(date +%s) -> difference < 5 s.
failure_signatures: worker RUNNING but shown as 'starting' forever
live peers missing from the peer note
nodes.manual_fix: Report the skewed node to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: NTP/chrony configuration changes at an OS upgrade.

nodes.title: Running workers execute the installed ashleyd.js
nodes.assumption: A worker keeps the daemon code it started with; the wizard uploads new scripts (VERSION 2) without restarting workers, and state.json carries no daemon version, only claude_version.
nodes.check: Login node: stat -c %Y ~/.ashley/bin/ashleyd.js is older than the worker's state.json 'started' time; cat ~/.ashley/bin/VERSION equals the extension's dist/grid/VERSION.
failure_signatures: the grid has Ashley v<old>; this extension brings v<new>
behaviour predates the docs (1 s poll, no peer note)
nodes.auto_repair: When the worker is idle (running [] and queued 0): ashley worker stop then start.
nodes.manual_fix: Restart the worker after updating.
nodes.future_risk: Every Ashley release.

nodes.title: The worker has the current GitHub and Hugging Face tokens
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/secrets.env is read once when the daemon starts and merged into every claude environment; renewing a token rewrites the file, but a running worker keeps the old value until it restarts (Claude account token files, by contrast, are re-read per request).
nodes.check: Login node: stat -c %Y ~/.ashley/secrets.env is older than the worker's 'started' time.
failure_signatures: remote: Invalid username or token
401 Client Error ... Invalid user token (hf)
Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/...'
nodes.auto_repair: Restart idle workers after pushTokens.
nodes.manual_fix: ashley worker stop and start after changing tokens.
nodes.future_risk: Token rotations becoming more frequent (fine-grained PAT expiry).

nodes.title: Session working directories exist and are visible inside the container
nodes.assumption: The daemon gets ASHLEY_ROOT=$ROOT; a new session defaults to $ROOT/workspaces/<session>; a request cwd (e.g. ~/Student_Projects/...) must lie under a bound path, since mkdirSync happens inside the container.
nodes.check: Compute node: CEXEC(bash -c 'test -w "$ROOT/workspaces" && echo ok') and test -d for each session cwd in ~/.ashley/sessions/*.json.
failure_signatures: tick error Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir '<path>'
EACCES: permission denied, mkdir
nodes.auto_repair: If the path exists on the host but not in the container, add its top directory to BINDS and restart the worker.
nodes.manual_fix: Use a cwd under home or the lab volume.
nodes.future_risk: New storage locations outside the bound set.

nodes.title: Prompts fit in one argv element
nodes.assumption: The prompt and the appended system prompt are passed as command-line arguments; Linux limits one argument to 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN). A larger prompt fails at spawn.
nodes.check: Login node: wc -c ~/.ashley/workers/*/inbox/*.json -> each under 100 KiB (laptop side: refuse or spill larger prompts to a file).
failure_signatures: spawn E2BIG
request left as <id>.json.claimed with no outbox result
nodes.manual_fix: Put long material in a file on the grid and reference it in the prompt.
nodes.future_risk: Pasting whole documents into prompts as usage grows.

nodes.title: A claude run ends by itself instead of waiting on a permission prompt
nodes.assumption: In -p mode with --permission-mode acceptEdits, an action needing approval is expected to be denied rather than waited on; --permission-prompts none (2.1.259+, documented to prevent hangs) is not passed. A hung run holds a concurrency slot until the 6 h hard cap.
nodes.check: Login node: for ids in state.json 'running', the matching outbox/<id>.events.jsonl was modified within the last 30 minutes.
failure_signatures: hard cap reached for <id>; killing
status cancelled after about 6 h
running ids whose events file stopped growing
nodes.manual_fix: Restart the worker to free the slot; add --permission-prompts none to the daemon's argv.
nodes.future_risk: Permission behaviour of -p changing between versions.

nodes.title: The node name the worker records matches the laptop's ProxyJump pattern
nodes.assumption: The job writes 'hostname -f' (e.g. asx1.nas.grid.wayne.edu) to ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/node; the laptop uses it verbatim when it contains a dot, and only 'Host *.nas.grid.wayne.edu' carries ProxyJump. Another suffix means a direct, unreachable connection.
nodes.check: Login node: cat ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/node ends with .nas.grid.wayne.edu. Laptop: ssh -G <node> | grep -i proxyjump -> proxyjump wsu-grid.
failure_signatures: worker <w> has no node yet
ssh: Could not resolve hostname <node>
Connecting with SSH timed out (no jump host in the path)
nodes.auto_repair: Rewrite the node file as $(hostname -s).nas.grid.wayne.edu via PROBE, or set ashley.nodeDomain to the observed suffix and rewrite the ssh block.
nodes.manual_fix: Tell the lab admin the node domain changed.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT renaming the node domain or making hostname -f return an internal/InfiniBand name.

nodes.title: The node's sshd admits the user while a job runs there
nodes.assumption: Compute-node sshd accepts the same public key (shared home authorized_keys) through the login-node jump and, via pam_slurm_adopt, only while the user has a running job on that node; the session is adopted into the newest job (its cgroup limits and lifetime).
nodes.check: Login node: squeue -u $USER -h -t R -o %N includes the node. Laptop: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=150 <node> true -> exit 0 (slow, see vscode.node-connect-timeout).
failure_signatures: Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node
Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535
Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic)
nodes.auto_repair: If no job runs on the node, start a worker and connect to its node.
nodes.manual_fix: Start a worker (Ashley connects only to nodes where the user holds a job).
nodes.future_risk: C&IT could require 2FA on nodes, change pam_slurm_adopt's action_no_jobs, or disable direct ssh to nodes.

nodes.title: Compute-node host keys match the laptop's known_hosts
nodes.assumption: The node block uses StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new: new nodes are learned silently, but a reinstalled node with new keys hard-fails.
nodes.check: Laptop: ssh -o BatchMode=yes <node> true does not print 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED'; compare with ssh wsu-grid ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 <node>.
failure_signatures: WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
Host key verification failed.
nodes.auto_repair: Only when the key the login node sees for that node equals the new key: ssh-keygen -R <node> on the laptop, then reconnect.
nodes.manual_fix: Confirm the reinstall with C&IT before removing the old key.
nodes.future_risk: The el7 -> el9 reinstall regenerates every node's host keys at once.

nodes.title: Remote-SSH waits long enough for the node's slow sshd
nodes.assumption: The node's sshd takes about 23 s (observed 27 to 101 s) before running anything, and the first connection also installs the server; remote.SSH.connectTimeout must be at least 300 (Ashley sets it when it opens a node).
nodes.check: Laptop: VS Code user setting remote.SSH.connectTimeout >= 300; optionally time ssh -o BatchMode=yes <node> true < 300 s.
failure_signatures: Connecting with SSH timed out
Could not establish connection to "<node>"
nodes.auto_repair: Set remote.SSH.connectTimeout to 300 (Global), as commandConnect does.
nodes.manual_fix: Settings > remote.SSH.connectTimeout = 300, then connect again.
nodes.future_risk: Node sshd/PAM changes; Remote-SSH changing the setting's meaning.

nodes.title: Remote-SSH knows each node is Linux
nodes.assumption: remote.SSH.remotePlatform['<node fqdn>'] = 'linux' so Remote-SSH does not ask for (or mis-detect) the platform on each new node.
nodes.check: Laptop: VS Code user settings remote.SSH.remotePlatform has the node's FQDN mapped to linux.
failure_signatures: Select the platform of the remote host
nodes.auto_repair: Write the entry (commandConnect does).
nodes.manual_fix: Pick Linux when asked.
nodes.future_risk: Remote-SSH dropping per-host platform settings or adding wildcard support.

nodes.title: C&IT's glibc sysroot and patchelf exist on compute nodes
nodes.assumption: VS Code Server 1.99+ needs glibc >= 2.28 and libstdc++ >= 3.4.25 (host has 2.17); C&IT provides /wsu/apps/vscode/sysroot/x86_64-linux-gnu/x86_64-linux-gnu/sysroot/{lib,lib64} (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2) and /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/0.19.1/bin/patchelf (>= 0.18 required). 'ashley doctor' checks these on the login node only.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(bash -c 'S=/wsu/apps/vscode/sysroot/x86_64-linux-gnu/x86_64-linux-gnu/sysroot; test -e $S/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 && $S/lib/libc.so.6 | head -1; /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/0.19.1/bin/patchelf --version') -> a glibc version >= 2.28 and 'patchelf 0.19.1'.
failure_signatures: FAIL  missing <path> (C&IT moved the sysroot?)
exit code 207
The remote host may not meet VS Code Server's prerequisites for glibc and libstdc++
found GLIBC 2.17
nodes.auto_repair: If the paths moved, find the newest /wsu/apps/vscode/patchelf/* and sysroot and rewrite the bashrc block via ashley install; if the host glibc is >= 2.28 after an OS upgrade, remove the variables.
nodes.manual_fix: Follow C&IT's KB article 'How to SSH to the Grid in Visual Studio Code' for the current paths.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT moving or versioning the sysroot; VS Code raising its floor beyond it; after an OS upgrade the stale exports pointing at deleted files would break the server.

nodes.title: The sysroot variables are exported when Remote-SSH starts the server
nodes.assumption: Remote-SSH's non-interactive ssh sources ~/.bashrc (Red Hat bash with SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC) and the ashley block sits before any interactive-only 'return' guard, so VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER/PATH and VSCODE_SERVER_PATCHELF_PATH are set.
nodes.check: Laptop: ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid 'echo ${VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER:-UNSET}' -> the sysroot path (same home and bash as the nodes); login node: the line number of '# >>> ashley' in ~/.bashrc is below the first top-level 'return'.
failure_signatures: UNSET
exit code 207
glibc
You are connecting to an OS version that is unsupported by Visual Studio Code (followed by failure)
nodes.auto_repair: ashley install rewrites the block; if a return guard precedes it, move the block above the guard (keep a backup of ~/.bashrc).
nodes.manual_fix: Move the '# >>> ashley' block above '[ -z "$PS1" ] && return'.
nodes.future_risk: WSU changing /etc/bashrc or the skeleton; VS Code changing which shell it launches.

nodes.title: The VS Code server installs and runs from ~/.vscode-server
nodes.assumption: With no remote.SSH.serverInstallPath, the server goes to ~/.vscode-server on the nearly full home; the node downloads the build matching the laptop's VS Code commit from Microsoft's CDN; each VS Code release adds another build.
nodes.check: Compute node: PROBE(curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://update.code.visualstudio.com/api/latest/server-linux-x64/stable) -> 302; login node: ls ~/.vscode-server/cli/servers; du -sh ~/.vscode-server; the newest log.txt shows 'Extension host agent started'.
failure_signatures: Failed to download VS Code Server
EDQUOT: disk quota exceeded
tar: ... Cannot write
nodes.auto_repair: Delete ~/.vscode-server/cli/servers/Stable-<commit> for all but the two newest commits, only when no running job node has a process from that commit.
nodes.manual_fix: Remote-SSH: Kill VS Code Server on Host, then reconnect.
nodes.future_risk: Microsoft changing download hosts or layout; home quota.

nodes.title: No stale VS Code server blocks a new connection
nodes.assumption: A server process left from an earlier window coincided with two 302 s timeouts on asx1 (not diagnosed).
nodes.check: Compute node, in the worker allocation: PROBE(pgrep -u $USER -fc '.vscode-server/cli/servers') compared with the number of open Remote windows for that node.
failure_signatures: two consecutive 'Connecting with SSH timed out' at about 302 s while the server log shows the previous connection
nodes.auto_repair: PROBE(pkill -u $USER -f '.vscode-server/cli/servers') on that node, then reconnect.
nodes.manual_fix: Command Palette: Remote-SSH: Kill VS Code Server on Host.
nodes.future_risk: Remote-SSH exec-server behaviour changes.

nodes.title: VS Code server sockets survive the node's /tmp cleaner (unverified)
nodes.assumption: Under pam_slurm_adopt, pam_systemd is disabled and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset, so the server's IPC and terminal sockets probably live in the node's /tmp, which a cleaner sweeps while jobs run (it deleted multiprocessing sockets of other jobs). Not observed yet for VS Code.
nodes.check: Laptop: ssh <node> 'echo ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-UNSET}; ls /tmp | grep -c vscode'.
failure_signatures: The terminal process failed to launch
ENOENT ... vscode-ipc-*.sock
extension host reconnect loops after hours
nodes.manual_fix: Reload the window.
nodes.future_risk: Cleaner policy changes.

nodes.title: The Claude Code VS Code extension stays on the laptop
nodes.assumption: The Claude Code extension bundles a native binary that would meet host glibc 2.17 if VS Code installed it on the node's server; it must run on the UI side. Ashley itself declares extensionKind ['ui'].
nodes.check: Login node: ls ~/.vscode-server/extensions | grep -ci anthropic.claude-code -> 0; laptop: remote.extensionKind['anthropic.claude-code'] = ['ui'] if set.
failure_signatures: version `GLIBC_2.xx' not found in the remote extension host log
Claude panel fails only in the node window
nodes.auto_repair: Add remote.extensionKind {'anthropic.claude-code': ['ui']} to user settings.
nodes.manual_fix: Uninstall the Claude Code extension from the SSH host in the Extensions view.
nodes.future_risk: Claude extension manifest changes; VS Code remote extension sync.

nodes.title: ssh client still offers hmac-sha1
nodes.assumption: The laptop's OpenSSH can still negotiate hmac-sha1, the only MAC the grid's OpenSSH 7.4 sshd offers modern clients. 'MACs +hmac-sha1' only appends to the list; it cannot bring back a MAC the build removed.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -Q mac` includes a line `hmac-sha1`. Pass = present.
failure_signatures: no matching MAC found. Their offer: hmac-sha1
Bad SSH2 Mac spec 'hmac-sha1'
nodes.manual_fix: Install an OpenSSH build that still has hmac-sha1, or ask hpc@wayne.edu to enable hmac-sha2-256/512 on warrior's sshd.
nodes.future_risk: An OpenSSH release (Windows OpenSSH follows upstream) that compiles out SHA-1 MACs. Then every grid ssh fails at once until C&IT upgrades sshd.

nodes.title: One ssh binary for Node, terminals and Remote-SSH
nodes.assumption: Several things resolve ssh separately: run('ssh') and run('scp') resolve through the extension host's PATH, while terminals use System32\OpenSSH and Remote-SSH uses remote.SSH.path. All of them must reach the same OpenSSH, reading the same %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config. A Git-for-Windows/MSYS ssh or a PuTTY plink found first on PATH reads a different config and known_hosts.
nodes.check: laptop: compare `where ssh` (Windows) or `command -v ssh` with resolveExecutable('ssh') and remote.SSH.path. `ssh -G wsu-grid` must print `macs ...hmac-sha1` and `addressfamily inet`. Pass = one binary, and the block is applied.
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname wsu-grid
no matching MAC found (from a different ssh than the one diagnosed)
nodes.auto_repair: Set remote.SSH.path to the resolved System32 OpenSSH. Spawn ssh/scp by the absolute path from resolveExecutable.
nodes.manual_fix: Remove the other ssh from PATH, or point remote.SSH.path at C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe.
nodes.future_risk: Git for Windows or another installer moving its ssh ahead of System32 on PATH.

nodes.title: scp upload to ~/.ashley/bin works
nodes.assumption: scp from OpenSSH 9+ uses the SFTP protocol by default. Against the grid's OpenSSH 7.4 sftp-server, which has no expand-path extension, the remote path '~/.ashley/bin/' must still resolve, and the sftp subsystem must be enabled.
nodes.check: laptop: scp a 1-byte temp file to wsu-grid:~/.ashley/.scp-probe with BatchMode, then `ssh wsu-grid rm ~/.ashley/.scp-probe`. Pass = exit 0.
failure_signatures: scp: realpath ~/.ashley/bin/: No such file
subsystem request failed on channel 0
Received message too long
scp: Connection closed
nodes.auto_repair: Retry the upload with `scp -O` (legacy protocol), or stream a tar over ssh stdin (`tar -C dist/grid -cf - . | ssh wsu-grid 'tar -C ~/.ashley/bin -xf -'`).
nodes.manual_fix: Run the grid install step again after the fallback. If sftp is disabled on warrior, contact hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: OpenSSH removing the legacy scp protocol (-O). C&IT disabling the sftp subsystem.

nodes.title: Grid key loads without a passphrase
nodes.assumption: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu has no passphrase. BatchMode=yes ssh, the relay, and Remote-SSH background connections cannot answer a passphrase prompt. stepSshKey keeps an existing key at that path without inspecting it.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh-keygen -y -P "" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu` exits 0.
failure_signatures: Load key ... incorrect passphrase supplied to decrypt private key
Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive) with an agent-less BatchMode
nodes.manual_fix: Remove the passphrase (`ssh-keygen -p -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_wsu -N ""`), or delete the key and rerun the SSH key and login steps.
nodes.future_risk: A student reusing a passphrase-protected key, or a security policy requiring passphrases.

nodes.title: Private key file permissions
nodes.assumption: The private key is readable only by the student. POSIX mode 600; on Windows, an ACL without inherited Users or Everyone entries. ssh refuses a key that others can read. The wizard only runs chmod on non-Windows systems.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh-keygen -y -P "" -f key` does not print 'UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE'. On Windows, `icacls key` lists only the user, SYSTEM and Administrators.
failure_signatures: WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE!
Permissions for '...id_ed25519_wsu' are too open
bad permissions: ignore key
nodes.auto_repair: POSIX: chmod 600 key. Windows: icacls key /inheritance:r /grant:r "%USERNAME%:F".
nodes.manual_fix: Fix the key's permissions as above, or regenerate the key.
nodes.future_risk: Profile migration, backup restore or OneDrive/roaming sync resetting ACLs.

nodes.title: Login node host key known and unchanged
nodes.assumption: known_hosts holds warrior's current host key. The login Host block sets no StrictHostKeyChecking, so a BatchMode connection to an unknown host fails. The in-panel ssh2 key install never writes known_hosts, so right after it testConnection can fail and fall back to the terminal.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh-keygen -F warrior.grid.wayne.edu` finds an entry, and `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` stderr does not contain 'Host key verification failed' or 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED'.
failure_signatures: Host key verification failed.
WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
No ED25519 host key is known for warrior.grid.wayne.edu
nodes.auto_repair: Missing entry only: one `ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` (trust on first use). Never auto-replace a changed key.
nodes.manual_fix: Changed key: confirm the new fingerprint with hpc@wayne.edu, then `ssh-keygen -R warrior.grid.wayne.edu` and reconnect.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT reinstalling or upgrading the login node (el7 to el8/9 regenerates host keys), or adding login nodes behind the same name.

nodes.title: Compute node host keys
nodes.assumption: Node keys are accepted on first use (accept-new) and stay stable. A reimaged node presents a changed key, and Remote-SSH then fails with no prompt.
nodes.check: laptop: after a Remote-SSH failure, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu true` stderr does not contain 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED'.
failure_signatures: WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
Host key for asx1.nas.grid.wayne.edu has changed
nodes.manual_fix: Confirm the node was reimaged (hpc@wayne.edu), then `ssh-keygen -R <node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu`.
nodes.future_risk: Node OS reimages during a Wayne State upgrade.

nodes.title: In-panel ssh2 client negotiates with the grid
nodes.assumption: The bundled ssh2@1.17.0 (pure JS; cpu-features left external) supports the grid's kex, host key type and hmac-sha1. The password-and-code login in the panel depends on it.
nodes.check: laptop: `node dist/ashley-cli.js ssh2-probe` (probeWithKey) returns 'ssh2 reached'. Pass = exit 0.
failure_signatures: Handshake failed: no matching key exchange
Handshake failed: no matching host key format
Timed out while waiting for handshake
nodes.manual_fix: The wizard falls back to a terminal login. Rebuild with a newer ssh2.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT restricting sshd to post-quantum or other KEX that ssh2 lacks. An ssh2 major version dropping hmac-sha1.

nodes.title: In-panel login verifies warrior's host key
nodes.assumption: The ssh2 connect sets no hostVerifier, so it sends the grid password and the OTP to whatever host answers on port 22. This is safe only on an untampered network path.
nodes.check: code review / laptop: ConnectConfig.hostVerifier compares against the known_hosts entry for warrior. Pass = present.
failure_signatures: (silent) credentials sent to an intercepting host
nodes.manual_fix: Add a hostVerifier that pins the known_hosts key or a fingerprint published by C&IT. Until then, do the first login only from campus or the VPN.
nodes.future_risk: Hostile public Wi-Fi. A host key rotation after an upgrade would make a pinned verifier fail, which is correct behaviour.

nodes.title: No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the laptop
nodes.assumption: Nothing in the environment (system variables, the VS Code process, integrated terminals) sets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. If one is set, the local Claude Code silently bills an API key or is redirected. Ashley never injects them, but the student's OS may.
nodes.check: laptop: process.env of the extension host, plus the environmentVariableCollection, contain none of the three.
failure_signatures: local Claude shows API usage billing
Investigate with Claude charged to an API key
nodes.manual_fix: Remove the variable from the Windows user or system environment (or shell profile), then restart VS Code.
nodes.future_risk: Other tools' installers setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY globally.

nodes.title: Pre-approved AccessID list loads
nodes.assumption: media/allowlist.json in the VSIX parses as {accessIds:[...]}, or ashley.allowlistUrl answers JSON within 10 s. If both fail, allowlist() returns null, which means no restriction; a broken list silently opens the gate.
nodes.check: laptop: read and parse the bundled file. If allowlistUrl is set, fetch it and require HTTP 200 with a JSON accessIds array. Warn when the result would be null.
failure_signatures: allowlist null (gate open)
<id> is not on the lab's pre-approved list (stale bundled list)
nodes.manual_fix: Lead: `python tools/allow.py add <id>` and rebuild the VSIX, or publish the JSON at allowlistUrl.
nodes.future_risk: URL host moving; a VSIX built without media/.

nodes.title: VS Code's Electron runs as Node
nodes.assumption: When no system node >= 20 exists, the MCP server runs as process.execPath with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1. This relies on the Electron RunAsNode fuse staying enabled in VS Code.
nodes.check: laptop: spawn process.execPath with env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and args ['-e','console.log(process.version)']. Pass = prints v20+.
failure_signatures: Code.exe opens a window instead of printing
MCP server ashley: Failed to connect
spawn ... ENOENT after a VS Code update moved Code.exe
nodes.auto_repair: Re-register the MCP server with a system node when one is present.
