nodes.manual_fix: Install Node.js 22 LTS, then run Ashley: Connect the Claude Code extension to the grid.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code disabling the runAsNode fuse (Electron hardening). The macOS helper binary path changing.

nodes.title: MCP registration points at this install
nodes.assumption: The user-scope registration stores absolute paths: the node or Code.exe path, and <extensionPath>/dist/mcp-server.js, whose folder name contains the extension version. It also stores ASHLEY_GRID. All three must still match the installed extension and the current ashley.sshAlias. isMcpRegistered only checks that the name exists.
nodes.check: laptop: `claude mcp get ashley`. Parse the command, args and env. Pass = the files exist, args[0] is under the current extensionPath, and ASHLEY_GRID equals the current sshAlias.
failure_signatures: Cannot find module '...ashley-wsu-1.0.0/dist/mcp-server.js'
ashley: Failed to connect
MCP tools ssh to an old alias
nodes.auto_repair: Run registerMcp() again (claude mcp add-json --scope user overwrites).
nodes.manual_fix: Ashley: Connect the Claude Code extension to the grid.
nodes.future_risk: Every Ashley update (new versioned folder), VS Code moving its install path, the student renaming the alias.

nodes.title: MCP server answers initialize
nodes.assumption: dist/mcp-server.js, built with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.1 and zod 4, starts under the registered runtime and speaks a protocol version the installed Claude Code accepts.
nodes.check: laptop: spawn the registered command, write one JSON-RPC `initialize` line, and expect a result with protocolVersion and serverInfo.name='ashley' within 10 s. Then send tools/list and expect 10 ashley_* tools.
failure_signatures: ashley mcp server failed:
Unsupported protocol version
SyntaxError in mcp-server.js under an old node
nodes.auto_repair: Re-register (a newer runtime).
nodes.manual_fix: Update Ashley (a rebuild with a newer SDK).
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code dropping older MCP protocol revisions. SDK or zod breaking changes.

nodes.title: claude mcp subcommands exist
nodes.assumption: The bundled claude still has `mcp add-json --scope user`, `mcp get <name>` and `mcp remove --scope user`, with the same exit-code meanings.
nodes.check: laptop: `claude mcp --help` lists add-json, get and remove, and `claude mcp add-json --help` mentions --scope.
failure_signatures: error: unknown command 'add-json'
error: unknown option '--scope'
nodes.auto_repair: Fall back to writing .mcp.json in the workspace (already coded).
nodes.manual_fix: Update Ashley. Register by hand with `claude mcp add`.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code CLI renames.

nodes.title: Local Claude Code is signed in
nodes.assumption: The laptop's Claude Code is logged in with a subscription. Investigate with Claude runs `claude -p` locally with WebSearch and WebFetch, the MCP bridge is only useful from a logged-in session, and lab access requires it.
nodes.check: laptop: `claude auth status` JSON has loggedIn=true and authMethod other than apiKey.
failure_signatures: Invalid API key · Please run /login
Claude could not answer (exit 1)
loggedIn": false
nodes.manual_fix: Open the Claude Code panel and sign in with the Pro/Max account made with AccessID@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: `auth status` output format changing, or WebSearch being unavailable on some plans.

nodes.title: claude setup-token prints a capturable token
nodes.assumption: `claude setup-token` needs a TTY, opens the browser, and prints one token that matches /sk-ant-oat[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/ with no ANSI codes or line breaks inside it. It prints nothing without a TTY (measured).
nodes.check: laptop: `claude setup-token --help` exits 0. After a capture, the stored token matches the pattern and /v1/models answers 200 (account.claude).
failure_signatures: Token captured but rejected: 401
no token captured; clipboard fallback
unknown command 'setup-token'
nodes.manual_fix: Copy the token from the terminal and paste it into the panel field.
nodes.future_risk: A new token prefix (e.g. sk-ant-oat02 is fine, a different prefix is not), a token printed across lines, or the command renamed or made interactive differently.

nodes.title: Microsoft (Wayne State) sign-in provider
nodes.assumption: VS Code's built-in 'microsoft' provider can get a session with VSCODE_TENANT:organizations and User.Read in the WSU Entra tenant, and session.account.label is the UPN ending in wayne.edu.
nodes.check: laptop: vscode.authentication.getSession('microsoft', scopes, {silent:true}) returns a session whose label matches /@([a-z0-9-]+\.)*wayne\.edu$/ (skip when never signed in).
failure_signatures: AADSTS65001 consent required
AADSTS53003 blocked by Conditional Access
<name> is not a Wayne State account
nodes.manual_fix: Sign in with AccessID@wayne.edu. If the tenant blocks VS Code, the lead asks C&IT to allow the VS Code app, or types the AccessID by hand.
nodes.future_risk: The WSU tenant disabling user consent or requiring device compliance. MSAL changing account.label to the display name.

nodes.title: GitHub sign-in provider and its OAuth app
nodes.assumption: VS Code's 'github' provider grants repo, workflow, read:org and gist, and returns a gho_ token that GitHub keeps honouring on the grid.
nodes.check: laptop: getSession('github', GITHUB_SCOPES, {silent:true}) returns a token, and GET api.github.com/user answers 200.
failure_signatures: GitHub sign-in did not complete
User did not consent
401 Bad credentials
nodes.manual_fix: Paste a classic PAT with the pre-filled scopes instead (the fallback field).
nodes.future_risk: VS Code switching GitHub auth to fine-grained or expiring tokens. The student revoking the VS Code app.

nodes.title: Default terminal supports shell integration
nodes.assumption: The hidden terminal that runCapturing opens reports shellIntegration within 6 s. That requires a default profile of PowerShell, pwsh, bash, zsh or fish (not cmd.exe), and VS Code >= 1.93 for executeCommand/read().
nodes.check: laptop: read terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.<os> and the matching profile's path. Pass when it is a supported shell. Optionally open a hidden terminal and wait for onDidChangeTerminalShellIntegration.
failure_signatures: This terminal has no shell integration; the token will be picked up from your clipboard instead
nodes.manual_fix: Set Terminal > Integrated > Default Profile to PowerShell (Windows) or bash/zsh.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code shell-integration API changes. Corporate PowerShell execution policy blocking the integration script.

nodes.title: Troubleshooter report folder
nodes.assumption: globalStorageUri/diagnostics is writable. The hourly sweep writes one JSON report per run and nothing prunes them (about 8,760 files a year).
nodes.check: laptop: mkdir, then write and delete a probe file. Warn when there are more than 500 files or more than 50 MB.
failure_signatures: EACCES/ENOSPC writing diagnostics/*.json
check crashed: ENOSPC
nodes.auto_repair: Delete reports older than 30 days, keeping the last 100.
nodes.manual_fix: Free disk space.
nodes.future_risk: Unbounded growth. A VS Code storage path change.

nodes.title: Remote-SSH reads the Ashley ssh config
nodes.assumption: remote.SSH.configFile is empty or ~/.ssh/config, and remote.SSH.path is empty or an OpenSSH that honours the block (ProxyJump to *.nas.grid.wayne.edu, MACs +hmac-sha1).
nodes.check: laptop: read both settings. Pass when configFile is empty or resolves to the file the wizard wrote, and path is empty or passes laptop.ssh-path-consistency.
failure_signatures: Could not establish connection to "voh3.nas.grid.wayne.edu"
no matching MAC found (Remote - SSH log)
nodes.auto_repair: Clear remote.SSH.configFile if it points elsewhere and lacks the block (ask first).
nodes.manual_fix: Settings: clear remote.SSH.configFile / remote.SSH.path, or copy the Ashley block into the file Remote-SSH uses.
nodes.future_risk: Remote-SSH defaults changing (exec server, local server download).

nodes.title: Grid scripts bundled in the extension
nodes.assumption: <extensionPath>/dist/grid holds ashley, ashleyd.js, phone.js, bootstrap.sbatch, worker.sbatch.tpl, bashrc.block and VERSION, with LF line endings. grid.scripts compares against VERSION.
nodes.check: laptop: all 7 files exist and are non-empty, and none contains \r.
failure_signatures: no grid scripts found in <dir>
$'\r': command not found (on the grid)
nodes.manual_fix: Reinstall the Ashley VSIX.
nodes.future_risk: A build run without ../grid present (esbuild copies only if it exists).

nodes.title: TCP 22 to the login node, sshd banner
nodes.assumption: The laptop's network lets outbound TCP 22 reach warrior (hospital/DMC or guest Wi-Fi often blocks it), and sshd announces itself. The banner version is recorded so that an sshd upgrade shows up.
nodes.check: laptop: open TCP to warrior.grid.wayne.edu:22 (IPv4) and read the first line within 10 s. Pass = starts with 'SSH-2.0-'. Warn when it changes from the recorded 'OpenSSH_7.4'.
failure_signatures: connect ETIMEDOUT
ECONNREFUSED
kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
nodes.manual_fix: Change networks (campus Wi-Fi, home, phone hotspot) or connect the WSU VPN.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT restricting SSH to VPN or campus only. An sshd upgrade changing algorithms (re-verify MACs and host keys).

nodes.title: Login host resolves to IPv4
nodes.assumption: warrior.grid.wayne.edu (ashley.loginHost) has an A record. The block forces AddressFamily inet.
nodes.check: laptop: dns.lookup(loginHost, {family:4}). Pass = an address.
failure_signatures: ssh: Could not resolve hostname warrior.grid.wayne.edu
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND
nodes.manual_fix: Check DNS or VPN. If the login host was renamed, set ashley.loginHost and rerun the SSH configuration step.
nodes.future_risk: Login node rename or retirement (for example a new cluster name).

nodes.title: sshd connection limits not tripped
nodes.assumption: Bursts of short ssh connections do not hit warrior's MaxStartups or a fail2ban-style ban: tree refresh, the hourly sweep, the relay, token checks, and every GridApi call without the relay.
nodes.check: laptop: three sequential `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` all succeed, and none prints kex_exchange_identification.
failure_signatures: kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer
ssh_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
Connection timed out during banner exchange
nodes.auto_repair: Back off: pause sweeps for 15 minutes and route calls through the relay.
nodes.manual_fix: Wait. If it persists, ask hpc@wayne.edu whether your IP is blocked.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT tightening MaxStartups or adding IP bans after failed logins.

nodes.title: OnDemand reachable (2FA setup)
nodes.assumption: ondemand.grid.wayne.edu answers only from campus or the WSU VPN, and the wizard uses that as its VPN test. It matters only while 2FA is being set up.
nodes.check: laptop: GET https://ondemand.grid.wayne.edu/ with redirect manual within 8 s. Skip when twoFactorDone.
failure_signatures: fetch failed
ETIMEDOUT
nodes.manual_fix: Join the campus Wi-Fi or connect GlobalProtect VPN.
nodes.future_risk: OnDemand URL change, or OnDemand opened to the internet (then the VPN inference is wrong).

nodes.title: Grid password + OTP prompt shape
nodes.assumption: warrior's keyboard-interactive auth asks for 'Password:' first and then a verification code (Google Authenticator PAM). The panel routes prompts by /pass/i and /verification|code|token/i.
nodes.check: during installKey only: log the prompt texts. Pass = the first matches /pass/i and a later one matches /code|verification/i. Skip once the key works.
failure_signatures: the grid rejected the password or the code (3x)
unexpected prompt text (Duo push, 'Passcode or option')
nodes.manual_fix: Use the terminal fallback and answer the prompts as shown.
nodes.future_risk: WSU moving the grid to Duo or Microsoft MFA (push or number matching), which changes the prompts.

nodes.title: ssh to a compute node through the jump host
nodes.assumption: ProxyJump via warrior needs AllowTcpForwarding on the login sshd. The node lets the student in only while they hold a running job there (pam_slurm_adopt). The node's sshd takes ~25 s, under remote.SSH.connectTimeout.
nodes.check: laptop (slow): `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=120 <worker node>.nas.grid.wayne.edu hostname`. Pass = the node name. Warn when it takes over 120 s.
failure_signatures: channel 0: open failed: administratively prohibited: open failed
Access denied by pam_slurm_adopt: you have no active jobs on this node
Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535
Connecting with SSH timed out
nodes.auto_repair: Start or restart a worker so a job holds the node.
nodes.manual_fix: Start a worker first. If forwarding is prohibited, contact hpc@wayne.edu (Remote-SSH to nodes depends on it).
nodes.future_risk: C&IT disabling TCP forwarding on the login node, changing the node domain, or making node sshd slower.

nodes.title: Grid account active, password not aged out
nodes.assumption: The AccessID and its grid account are active (sponsor renewal current), and the password has not expired. PAM can refuse even key logins with a forced password change, which BatchMode cannot answer.
nodes.check: laptop: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes wsu-grid true` stderr contains none of the expiry strings.
failure_signatures: WARNING: Your password has expired.
You are required to change your password immediately
Password change required but no TTY available.
Your account has expired; please contact your system administrator
nodes.manual_fix: Change the AccessID password at the WSU password portal. For an expired grid account, ask your sponsor or hpc@wayne.edu to renew it.
nodes.future_risk: WSU password-age policy, annual grid account renewal.

nodes.title: GitHub token scopes and expiry
nodes.assumption: GET /user answers 200 even for a token that lacks the scopes the worker needs. Those are repo, plus workflow for Actions files. A fine-grained PAT expires on a date.
nodes.check: laptop or grid: GET api.github.com/user. The X-OAuth-Scopes header includes repo, and the github-authentication-token-expiration header, if present, is more than 14 days away (warn under 14).
failure_signatures: remote: Permission to <org>/<repo>.git denied
refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow
Bad credentials after expiry
nodes.manual_fix: Press Renew next to GitHub (sign-in grants the scopes).
nodes.future_risk: GitHub deprecating classic PATs or adding forced expiry.

nodes.title: Lab GitHub orgs allow the token
nodes.assumption: Organizations the student pushes to (OpenSpineConsortium, the lab's) allow VS Code's GitHub OAuth app or the PAT, and have SSO authorized if they use SAML.
nodes.check: grid: `GET api.github.com/orgs/<lab org>` with the token is not 403, and a `git ls-remote` of a lab repo succeeds.
failure_signatures: Although you appear to have the correct authorization credentials, the organization has enabled OAuth App access restrictions
Resource protected by organization SAML enforcement
nodes.manual_fix: Org owner approves the VS Code app (or the student uses a PAT authorized for the org).
nodes.future_risk: Orgs enabling OAuth app restrictions or SSO.

nodes.title: Hugging Face token can write
nodes.assumption: The HF token has a write role, because the lab uploads datasets. whoami-v2 accepts read tokens too.
nodes.check: laptop or grid: whoami-v2 JSON auth.accessToken.role is 'write' or fineGrained with repo write.
failure_signatures: 403 Forbidden: You don't have the rights to create a model under this namespace
nodes.manual_fix: Create a Write token (the page opens pre-filled) and press Renew.
nodes.future_risk: HF token model changes.

nodes.title: Claude setup-token age
nodes.assumption: A setup-token lasts about one year and carries no expiry of its own. ~/.ashley/accounts/default/minted_at is the only record of its age.
nodes.check: grid: `cat ~/.ashley/accounts/default/minted_at`. Warn from day 330, fail from day 365. Warn when the file is missing.
failure_signatures: CLAUDE_TOKEN rejected (invalid, expired or revoked
Failed to authenticate
nodes.manual_fix: Press Renew next to Claude (runs claude setup-token; the grid copy is updated).
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic changing the setup-token lifetime.

nodes.title: Phone (Remote Control) login valid
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley/remote/config holds a full claude.ai login, not a setup-token, which lasts about 30 days. It is never logged out.
nodes.check: grid, via the worker: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.ashley/remote/config claude auth status reports loggedIn true. Skip when phone access is off.
failure_signatures: the phone sign-in expired; sign in again
You must be logged in to use Remote Control
nodes.manual_fix: Ashley: Phone access (sign in again and paste the code).
nodes.future_risk: Login lifetime changes. Remote Control becoming available to setup-tokens (it could then be simplified).

nodes.title: Grid login shell is bash
nodes.assumption: The remote side of every ssh call is parsed by a POSIX/bash login shell. That covers the single-quoted argv, `~/'...'` tilde expansion, `bash -c`, `$USER` in squeue, and the relay path left unquoted.
nodes.check: grid: `getent passwd $USER | cut -d: -f7` ends in /bash.
failure_signatures: Unmatched '.
~/.ashley/bin/ashley: No such file or directory with a tcsh shell
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu to set the login shell to /bin/bash.
nodes.future_risk: Account provisioning defaults changing.

nodes.title: Non-interactive login prints nothing
nodes.assumption: ~/.bashrc and /etc/bashrc write nothing to stdout for non-interactive ssh. SFTP-mode scp breaks on stray output, and JSON answers are parsed from the last line.
nodes.check: grid: `ssh wsu-grid true` produces 0 bytes on stdout.
failure_signatures: Received message too long 1349281121
scp: Connection closed
status did not return JSON
nodes.manual_fix: Guard echo lines in ~/.bashrc with `[[ $- == *i* ]]`, or redirect them to stderr.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT adding a login banner to /etc/bashrc, or a module load that prints to stdout.

nodes.title: Sysroot variables reach non-interactive ssh
nodes.assumption: RHEL bash sources ~/.bashrc for ssh commands (SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC), and the Ashley block comes before any return guard. The existing node only greps that the block exists.
nodes.check: grid: `ssh wsu-grid printenv VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER` prints the path from the block.
failure_signatures: The remote host may not meet VS Code Server's prerequisites for glibc
exit code 207
printenv prints nothing
nodes.auto_repair: Move the managed block to the top of ~/.bashrc (awk rewrite, idempotent).
nodes.manual_fix: Put the block above `[ -z "$PS1" ] && return` or `case $- in *i*)` in ~/.bashrc.
nodes.future_risk: A new /etc/skel/.bashrc with an early return. An OS whose bash lacks SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC.

nodes.title: bash 4 and GNU tools on the login node
nodes.assumption: The grid CLI is bash and coreutils only. It needs bash >= 4.2 (local -A, read -t 0.25), GNU date %3N, stat -c, sed -i, sort -V, find -perm /mode, timeout, tail -c +N, awk getline, getent and curl -K -.
nodes.check: grid: `bash -c 'declare -A a; read -t 0.01 </dev/null; date +%s%3N; stat -c %Y ~; sort -V </dev/null; timeout 1 true; find ~ -maxdepth 0 -perm /o=w'` exits 0 with 13-digit ms.
failure_signatures: declare: -A: invalid option
read: 0.25: invalid timeout specification
date: invalid format
nodes.manual_fix: Contact hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: A login-node image change (unlikely to drop GNU, but a minimal image might lack getfacl or timeout).

nodes.title: Grid home path matches gridHome()
nodes.assumption: $HOME = /wsu/home/<ab>/<ab12>/<accessid>. The extension builds the Remote-SSH folder and ASHLEY_GRID_HOME from this formula.
nodes.check: grid: `ssh wsu-grid 'echo $HOME'` equals gridHome(accessId).
failure_signatures: Remote-SSH: folder does not exist
ASHLEY_GRID_HOME points to a missing path
nodes.auto_repair: Store the reported $HOME and use it instead of the formula.
nodes.manual_fix: Open the folder that `echo $HOME` prints.
nodes.future_risk: A C&IT home migration (a new storage system or path scheme).

nodes.title: Home quota readable
nodes.assumption: `pan_quota` (Panasas) exists and its output has the used and soft GB in columns 1-2 after line 2. The df fallback reports filesystem totals, not the user's quota.
nodes.check: grid: `command -v pan_quota`, and the awk parse yields two numbers. Warn when home_quota fell back to df.
failure_signatures: home quota ?/? GB
home at 3 % (df on a multi-PB filesystem)
nodes.manual_fix: Update the quota parser for the new tool.
nodes.future_risk: Panasas replaced (VAST, Ceph), pan_quota output changing.

nodes.title: Home coherent across nodes
nodes.assumption: The file queue needs the login node and the compute nodes to see the same $HOME, with an atomic rename(2) and mkdir, and attribute caching short enough that inbox, outbox and state.json changes show up within ~1 s and heartbeats within 90 s.
nodes.check: grid (slow): inside the worker allocation (srun --overlap), write a nonce file with .part+rename. On the login node, time until `cat` sees it. Pass under 5 s. Also mkdir the same lock dir twice (the second must fail with EEXIST).
failure_signatures: worker alive=false although the daemon logs beats
result never appears on the login node
two phone hosts at once
nodes.manual_fix: Report to hpc@wayne.edu (home filesystem caching).
nodes.future_risk: A home filesystem change with longer attribute caching, or non-atomic rename across nodes.

nodes.title: Login and compute node clocks agree
nodes.assumption: Several things compare timestamps from different nodes. Heartbeat age is the file mtime compared with the login node's `date` (90 s). Cooldowns, the phone lease (60 s stale) and relay skew correction depend on the same agreement.
nodes.check: grid: inside the worker `date +%s%3N` vs the login node's, one srun round trip apart. Pass when |skew| < 5 s.
failure_signatures: daemon stopped answering N s ago while the log shows beats
phone lease taken over repeatedly
nodes.manual_fix: Report NTP drift to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: NTP misconfiguration after a node reimage.

nodes.title: Grid secrets private
nodes.assumption: ~/.ashley and accounts/ are 700. secrets.env, accounts/*/token and apikey are 600. No ACL entry or default ACL (for example on Panasas or a group-shared home) grants others read.
nodes.check: grid: `stat -c %a` on each, and `getfacl -p` shows no user: or group: entries with r. Pass = modes as listed.
failure_signatures: secrets.env present (644)
group::r-- on accounts/
nodes.auto_repair: chmod 700 ~/.ashley ~/.ashley/accounts ~/.ashley/remote; chmod 600 ~/.ashley/secrets.env ~/.ashley/accounts/*/{token,apikey}; setfacl -b on them.
nodes.manual_fix: Run the repair, then renew tokens if they were exposed.
nodes.future_risk: A home restore or migration resetting modes.

nodes.title: Ashley ROOT writable
nodes.assumption: ROOT from config.env (/rs/rs_grp_oschome/<id>/ashley or ~/ashley) exists and is writable. Session working directories and workspaces/phone live there. `ashley doctor` checks this, `ashley diag` does not.
nodes.check: grid: `. ~/.ashley/config.env; [ -w "$ROOT/workspaces" ]`.
failure_signatures: cannot create ROOT=
EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '<ROOT>/workspaces/<session>'
nodes.auto_repair: `mkdir -p $ROOT/workspaces`. If the volume is gone, reset ROOT to ~/ashley via set_cfg.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lead about the lab volume, or set ashley.gridRoot.
nodes.future_risk: CephFS allocation moved or expired.

nodes.title: sshd StrictModes satisfied
nodes.assumption: The home directory is not group- or world-writable, ~/.ssh is 700 and authorized_keys is 600. Otherwise sshd ignores the key.
nodes.check: grid: `stat -c %a ~ ~/.ssh ~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Pass = home without g+w/o+w, 700, 600.
failure_signatures: Authentication refused: bad ownership or modes for directory
Permission denied (publickey,keyboard-interactive) after it worked
nodes.auto_repair: chmod go-w ~; chmod 700 ~/.ssh; chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (only while still logged in).
nodes.manual_fix: Log in with the password and code once and run those chmods.
nodes.future_risk: A group-sharing change to the home directory (setfacl or chmod g+w by a tool).

nodes.title: User and group lookups (sssd)
nodes.assumption: getent passwd and getent group answer through sssd. admin_ingest silently drops applicants it cannot resolve, and approve refuses them.
nodes.check: grid: `getent passwd $USER` and `getent group oschome` return lines within 5 s.
failure_signatures: no grid user <id>
requests silently not ingested
nodes.manual_fix: Retry later. Report an sssd outage to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: Directory migration (AD or IPA changes).

nodes.title: Environment modules and the pinned modules
nodes.assumption: /etc/profile.d/modules.sh defines `module` in batch and `bash -lc` shells, and apptainer/1.2.2 (pinned in bootstrap) and singularity/3.5.2 exist. discover_runtime loads the default apptainer.
nodes.check: grid: `bash -lc 'module -t avail apptainer 2>&1'` lists apptainer/1.2.2. Warn when only a different version exists.
failure_signatures: module: command not found
Lmod has detected the following error: The following module(s) are unknown: "apptainer/1.2.2"
STOP: no container runtime found
nodes.auto_repair: Pass the newest listed apptainer version to bootstrap and repair the configured RUNTIME (grid.runtime).
nodes.manual_fix: Lead republishes the container with the current module.
nodes.future_risk: Module version retired or renamed, Lmod migration, el7 to el8 module trees.

nodes.title: Long relay survives on the login node
nodes.assumption: The long-lived `ashley relay` ssh session (read -t 0.25 loop) is not killed by a login-node reaper or an idle timeout.
nodes.check: laptop: count 'relay closed' events in the Ashley log over 24 h. Warn when above 12, or when the relay dies at a regular age.
failure_signatures: relay closed (ssh exit 255)
relay closed (ssh exit 137)
nodes.auto_repair: Already reconnects. Lengthen ServerAliveInterval or reconnect proactively before the observed age.
nodes.manual_fix: Nothing needed (the fresh-ssh fallback works). Tell hpc@wayne.edu if it is killed as abuse.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT deploying Arbiter-style reapers or a TMOUT for non-interactive sessions.

nodes.title: Named sessions still have transcripts
nodes.assumption: Each ~/.ashley/sessions/<name>.json session_id has a transcript under ~/.ashley/projects/*/<id>.jsonl. Claude Code deletes transcripts after cleanupPeriodDays (30). resolveSession still passes --resume, which then fails every time.
nodes.check: grid: for each sessions/*.json, find ~/.ashley/projects -name '<sid>.jsonl'. Pass = all found.
failure_signatures: No conversation found with session ID:
claude exited 1 without a result
nodes.auto_repair: Drop session_id from the stale sessions/<name>.json (keep cwd) so the next turn starts fresh. Set cleanupPeriodDays high in each account's settings.json.
nodes.manual_fix: Start the session again under a new name.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code changing the retention default or the transcript path.

nodes.title: Old VS Code servers pruned
nodes.assumption: Remote-SSH installs one ~200 MB server per VS Code release under ~/.vscode-server on the quota'd Panasas home and never removes the old ones.
nodes.check: grid: `du -sm ~/.vscode-server/cli/servers/*`. Warn when there are more than 3 versions or more than 1 GB.
failure_signatures: Disk quota exceeded during server install
Failed to install the VS Code Server
nodes.auto_repair: Remove server versions other than the newest two that are not in use (no process with that commit).
nodes.manual_fix: Remote-SSH: Uninstall VS Code Server from Host.
nodes.future_risk: Monthly VS Code releases.

nodes.title: Partitions exist and are allowed
nodes.assumption: reqp (worker, bootstrap and access-request default), secp (fallback, publish default), and gmsap, gvohp and galhp (GPU workers) exist and accept this account.
nodes.check:
grid: `sinfo -h -o %P -p reqp,secp,gmsap,gvohp,galhp`, and `sbatch --test-only -p

--wrap true` exits 0 for reqp and secp.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: invalid partition specified: reqp
Batch job submission failed: Invalid account or account/partition combination specified
nodes.auto_repair: Point ashley.worker.partition and QoS at the first partition that accepts the account (secp/secondary).
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu or the lead for the current partition names.
nodes.future_risk: Partitions renamed or retired with hardware (V100 nodes).

nodes.title: GPU QoS and gres
nodes.assumption: GPU workers submit with --qos gpu and --gres=gpu:N on the gmsap,gvohp,galhp partitions.
nodes.check: grid: sacctmgr assoc QoS includes gpu, and `sbatch --test-only -p gmsap,gvohp,galhp -q gpu --gres=gpu:1 --wrap true` exits 0. Skip when no GPU worker is configured.
failure_signatures: Invalid qos specification
Invalid generic resource (gres) specification
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lead for GPU QoS access.
nodes.future_risk: GPU QoS renamed or typed gres (gpu:h200:1) required.

nodes.title: Requested wall time within QoS limits
nodes.assumption: ashley.worker.hours (up to 720) is within the chosen QoS MaxWall (primary 30 d, secondary 90 d, requeue ?). Per-user job and TRES limits allow another worker. Otherwise the job pends forever.
nodes.check: grid: `sacctmgr -n -P show qos <q> format=name,maxwall,maxjobspu,maxtrespu`. Pass when hours <= maxwall. A pending worker's reason does not start with QOSMax.
failure_signatures: Reason=QOSMaxWallDurationPerJobLimit
Reason=QOSMaxJobsPerUserLimit
Reason=AssocGrpCPULimit
nodes.auto_repair: Resubmit with hours clamped to maxwall (worker restart after rewriting --time).
nodes.manual_fix: Lower Hours when starting the worker.
nodes.future_risk: QoS policy changes.

nodes.title: Slurm output formats Ashley parses
nodes.assumption: Ashley parses several outputs. `sbatch --parsable` prints id[;cluster]. `squeue -h -o '%i|%j|%T|%N|%M|%l|%P|%R'` and '%i|%u|%k|%V' (comment, submit time) print as formatted, with -t PD and -n filters. `sacct -j -n -X -o State -P` prints the state. `scontrol show config` prints 'PrivateData = ...'.
nodes.check: grid: run each against a known job (for example the worker's). Pass = the fields split into the expected count, and the job id is numeric.
failure_signatures: jobId not numeric
bootstrap job X: (empty state)
parseSqueue returns []
nodes.manual_fix: Update the parsers in slurm.ts and grid/ashley.
nodes.future_risk: A Slurm major upgrade (for example 23 to 24/25) changing formats or defaults.

nodes.title: Held access-request job accepted and kept
nodes.assumption: `sbatch --hold -J ashley_access -p reqp -q requeue -t 1 -n 1 --mem=16M --comment ...` is accepted: the minimums are allowed, the student has the requeue QoS, and the comment is stored and shown by squeue %k. The held job also stays pending until the admin decides (no purge of held jobs).
nodes.check: grid: `sbatch --test-only --hold -p reqp -q requeue -t 1 -n 1 --mem=16M --comment probe --wrap true` exits 0. For a filed student, own_request_job is non-empty until a decision.
failure_signatures: could not file the request
Requested time limit is invalid
Memory specification can not be satisfied
state flips from filed to none without a decision
nodes.auto_repair: Resubmit the request when state is none but no decision exists (idempotent).
nodes.manual_fix: The lead grants directly (Grant a user directly).
nodes.future_risk: C&IT purging long-held jobs, raising the minimum memory, or restricting the requeue QoS.

nodes.title: Publish passes PURPOSE through --export
nodes.assumption: `sbatch --export=ALL,...,PURPOSE=$purpose` carries a free-text purpose. Commas separate --export entries, so the documented purpose 'general: Claude Code, Node 22, git, python3' would split.
nodes.check: grid: `sbatch --test-only --export='ALL,X=a, b' --wrap true` exits 0, and a published entry's purpose equals the one given.
failure_signatures: sbatch: error: Invalid environment variable name
library entry purpose truncated at the first comma
nodes.manual_fix: Pass the purpose in a file or base64-encode it (a code change). Until then, use purposes without commas.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm --export parsing changes.

nodes.title: srun --overlap into the worker's job
nodes.assumption: `srun --jobid=<running worker> --overlap -N1 -n1` starts a step inside the student's own allocation (Slurm >= 20.11). diag-node, grid_tests.sh and worker-to-worker tests use it.
nodes.check: grid: `timeout 60 srun --jobid=<jid> --overlap -N1 -n1 --quiet hostname` prints the worker's node.
failure_signatures: srun: error: Unable to create step for job
srun: unrecognized option '--overlap'
step creation temporarily disabled, retrying
nodes.manual_fix: Restart the worker. Report to hpc@wayne.edu if steps are refused.
nodes.future_risk: Slurm changes to step and overlap semantics.

nodes.title: Worker job directives honoured
nodes.assumption: The worker job relies on several directives. --dependency=singleton keeps one job per worker name. --signal=B:TERM@120 gives the daemon a grace period. --open-mode=append and --requeue apply on the requeue QoS. --output=log/slurm_%j.out resolves against the submit dir, because ashley cds into the worker dir before sbatch.
nodes.check: grid: `scontrol show job <jid>` shows Dependency=singleton (while pending), Requeue=1 on the requeue QoS, and StdOut under ~/.ashley/workers/<w>/log.
failure_signatures: two jobs for one worker running at once
slurm_*.out missing
daemon killed without 'stopping (SIGTERM)' in ashleyd.log
nodes.manual_fix: Stop the duplicate worker job (ashley worker stop, then start).
nodes.future_risk: Slurm policy disabling requeue or singleton.

nodes.title: Preemption gives grace, requests replay safely
nodes.assumption: On the requeue QoS, preemption sends SIGTERM with enough grace. On restart, recoverClaimed re-runs interrupted requests from the beginning, which is safe only if prompts are idempotent. A prompt that submitted jobs may submit them twice.
nodes.check: grid: `scontrol show config | grep -E 'PreemptMode|GraceTime'` and the requeue QoS GraceTime. Warn when the grace is under 120 s. Count 'recovered' lines in ashleyd.log.
failure_signatures: recovered <id>.json.claimed
duplicate Slurm jobs after a requeue
nodes.manual_fix: Use secp/secondary or primary for long tasks. Write prompts so they check before resubmitting.
nodes.future_risk: Preemption policy changes.

nodes.title: Worker not stuck pending
nodes.assumption: A worker on reqp/requeue starts within a reasonable time. Measured: reqp pended 30+ min on Priority while secp/secondary started at once.
nodes.check: grid: squeue %R for PENDING worker jobs. Warn when pending more than 15 min with reason Priority or Resources.
failure_signatures: Reason=(Priority)
Reason=(Resources)
nodes.auto_repair: Offer (with consent) to resubmit the worker on secp/secondary with the same resources.
nodes.manual_fix: Set ashley.worker.partition=secp and qos=secondary, then start the worker again.
nodes.future_risk: Cluster load. Changes to the fair-share policy.

nodes.title: /dev/shm scratch on the node
nodes.assumption: /dev/shm is writable with room to spare. It is bound as /tmp in the container, and what the job writes there counts against the job's --mem (16G). Scratch left by SIGKILLed jobs, whose trap never ran, stays behind.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker via srun --overlap): `df -k /dev/shm` free > 2 GB. List /dev/shm/${USER}_ashley_* directories whose job id is no longer running.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: no /dev/shm scratch
ENOSPC on /tmp inside the container
oom-kill event in slurm_*.out
nodes.auto_repair: Remove ${USER}_ashley_* and ${USER}_diag_* directories of jobs that squeue no longer lists.
nodes.manual_fix: Raise worker memory, or keep large temp files in ROOT.
nodes.future_risk: Node tmpfs sizing or cgroup accounting changes.

nodes.title: Apptainer exec mode on the node
nodes.assumption: The configured apptainer can exec a sandbox without root. Either it is installed setuid, or unprivileged user namespaces are enabled (user.max_user_namespaces > 0).
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): `cat /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces` > 0, or `ls -l $(dirname $RUNTIME)/../libexec/apptainer/bin/starter-suid` is setuid.
failure_signatures: FATAL: while performing image mount: ... user namespace not supported
starter not found
Operation not permitted
nodes.manual_fix: Report to hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: A kernel CVE response disabling user namespaces, or a change in apptainer install mode.

nodes.title: Bind sources exist on the node
nodes.assumption: Every BINDS source exists on the compute node: $HOME, /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER, the shared lab folder and ROOT. Autofs may mount CephFS only on first access.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): for each -B path in config.env BINDS, `ls -d <path>` succeeds.
failure_signatures: FATAL: container creation failed: mount hook function failure: mount /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared->... error: no such file or directory
REFUSING: sandbox ... incomplete
nodes.auto_repair: Remove bind entries whose source no longer exists from config.env (set_cfg BINDS) and restart the worker.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lead whether the lab volume moved.
nodes.future_risk: CephFS path or mount changes.

nodes.title: Node reaches every service it needs
nodes.assumption: Compute nodes have direct outbound HTTPS, with no proxy, to api.anthropic.com, claude.ai/claude.com and platform.claude.com (OAuth and Remote Control), registry.npmjs.org, registry-1.docker.io, huggingface.co and github.com. If a proxy is introduced, HTTPS_PROXY must pass into the container.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker, inside the container): curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} for each host. Pass = not 000.
failure_signatures: 000 (curl timeout)
getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN
Remote Control stays 'starting'
npm ERR! network
nodes.manual_fix: Report to hpc@wayne.edu. If a proxy is announced, add HTTPS_PROXY to secrets.env.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT adding an egress firewall or proxy to compute nodes.

nodes.title: GPU visible inside the container
nodes.assumption: For GPU workers, `--nv` binds the host NVIDIA driver libraries and the container image's CUDA works with the node's driver.
nodes.check: grid (in a GPU worker): `$RUNTIME exec --nv $SANDBOX nvidia-smi -L` lists one GPU. Skip for CPU workers.
failure_signatures: WARNING: Could not find any nv files on this host!
CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
nodes.manual_fix: Lead publishes an image that matches the node driver.
nodes.future_risk: Driver upgrades on GPU nodes, CUDA image upgrades.

nodes.title: VS Code server runs on the node with the C&IT sysroot
nodes.assumption: The C&IT sysroot's glibc (via VSCODE_SERVER_CUSTOM_GLIBC_LINKER/PATH and patchelf 0.19.1) meets the current VS Code server's glibc floor. VS Code keeps this unsupported escape hatch.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): the sysroot's libc.so.6 version is >= the floor stated for the laptop's VS Code version. The newest ~/.vscode-server/cli/servers/*/log.txt contains 'Extension host agent started' after the last connect.
failure_signatures: exit code 207
GLIBC_2.28 not found
The remote host may not meet VS Code Server's prerequisites
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu for an updated sysroot. Meanwhile pin the previous VS Code version.
nodes.future_risk: VS Code raising the glibc floor or removing the custom-glibc variables. C&IT not updating the sysroot. A grid OS upgrade making it unnecessary.

nodes.title: No stale VS Code server blocking a reconnect
nodes.assumption: A server left over from an earlier window on the node does not block a new connection. It was observed: two 302 s timeouts while pid 25363 still ran.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): `pgrep -u $USER -f vscode-server` older than the last successful connect, and more than one server commit running.
failure_signatures: Connecting with SSH timed out (302 s) while an earlier window's server still runs
nodes.auto_repair: `pkill -u $USER -f 'vscode-server/cli/servers/Stable-<old commit>'` in the worker allocation.
nodes.manual_fix: Remote-SSH: Kill VS Code Server on Host, then reconnect.
nodes.future_risk: Remote-SSH reconnect logic changes.

nodes.title: Account .claude.json intact
nodes.assumption: Account config dirs sit on the network home (Anthropic advises against this). Concurrent claude processes in one CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (concurrency 2, several workers) must not corrupt .claude.json. Its lock is mkdir-based and goes stale after 10 s.
nodes.check: grid: each ~/.ashley/accounts/*/.claude.json and remote/config/.claude.json parses as JSON.
failure_signatures: Configuration file at ... is corrupted
SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
nodes.auto_repair: Restore the newest .claude.json.backup* that parses, or remove the file (it is recreated; the phone config is reseeded by pretrust).
nodes.manual_fix: Lower worker concurrency to 1 if it recurs.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code config-write changes on network filesystems.

nodes.title: Container image provides what Ashley runs
nodes.assumption: Every library image has Node >= 18 (22) at /usr/local/bin/node, which bootstrap, adopt, is_ready and the worker template test for. It also has python3 for the publish merge, git, curl with CA certificates, bash, util-linux `script` for the phone pty, and a glibc above Claude Code's floor. docs/INSTALL.md's nvidia/cuda example has no /usr/local/bin/node, so its publish fails.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): `$RUNTIME exec $SANDBOX sh -c 'test -x /usr/local/bin/node && node -v && python3 -V && git --version && curl -V && command -v script'`.
failure_signatures: build with apptainer failed
REFUSING: sandbox ... incomplete
python3: not found (publish)
spawn script ENOENT
nodes.manual_fix: Lead publishes from an image with Node 22 installed at /usr/local/bin (for example a node:22-bookworm-based CUDA image).
nodes.future_risk: Upstream image layout changes. Node 22 end of life (2027-04-30). Debian bookworm end of life.

nodes.title: Pinned Claude Code still accepted
nodes.assumption: The pinned @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.283 still authenticates and runs against the Anthropic API (no minimum-version refusal), and the version recorded in READY or library.json equals `claude --version`.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): `claude --version` equals the recorded claude_version. A 1-turn `claude -p ok --max-turns 1` with the account's token returns is_error=false.
failure_signatures: Please update Claude Code
This version of Claude Code is no longer supported
API Error: 400 ... client version
nodes.auto_repair: Own container: `ashley bootstrap --update` with CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION set to the newest npm version. Lab container: admin runs `ashley library publish` with the new version, then students adopt.
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lead to publish a container with a newer Claude Code.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic enforcing minimum client versions. The npm package moving to native-only distribution.

nodes.title: claude -p flags and stream-json shape
nodes.assumption: The daemon relies on the CLI surface: -p, --output-format stream-json --verbose, --permission-mode, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --max-turns, --model, --allowedTools, --append-system-prompt, --resume <uuid> and --session-id <uuid>. The final line must be {type:'result', is_error, subtype, result, session_id, total_cost_usd, duration_ms, num_turns, usage}, and --bare must never be used.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): `claude --help` lists every flag. A 1-turn plan-mode run ends with a result line that has those keys.
failure_signatures: error: unknown option '--max-turns'
claude exited 0 without a result
status error with subtype undefined
nodes.manual_fix: Update the daemon to the new flags, and keep the pinned version until then.
nodes.future_risk: CLI flag renames or changes to the stream-json schema.

nodes.title: Claude Code environment variables
nodes.assumption: Claude Code honours these variables. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR sets the account directory. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY select the credential. DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 prevents writes to the read-only shared prefix. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC and DISABLE_TELEMETRY also apply. The six auth and redirect variables are the complete set that can override the credential.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): with a scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and the token env, `claude auth status` reports the token auth method, and nothing is written to the npm prefix (mtime unchanged).
failure_signatures: auth status shows none with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set
EACCES writing to npm-claude-node22 (autoupdater)
nodes.manual_fix: Update the env lists in ashleyd.js and phone.js.
nodes.future_risk: New auth variables (for example a new token-file variable) that override Ashley's choice.

nodes.title: Transcript path and --resume scope
nodes.assumption: Transcripts live at <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/projects/<cwd with non-alphanumerics as ->/<uuid>.jsonl, and --resume searches only there (measured on 2.1.283). Claude Code follows the projects symlink to ~/.ashley/projects.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): after a run, the transcript exists under ~/.ashley/projects/<encoded cwd>/<sid>.jsonl, and a --resume in a second account dir finds it.
failure_signatures: No conversation found with session ID
transcript written into accounts/<n>/projects.before-sharing.*
nodes.auto_repair: Relink projects/ (share_transcripts, already in grid.accounts repair).
nodes.manual_fix: Update fake-claude.js and shareTranscripts to the new layout.
nodes.future_risk: Claude Code changing the storage path or its symlink handling.

nodes.title: Rate-limit text and reset time parse
nodes.assumption: Limit exhaustion shows up in result or stderr text that matches RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS, with 'resets <h>[:mm]am/pm' or 'try again in N unit'. The reset hour is read in the container's local time zone, which comes from the host's /etc/localtime bound by Apptainer and must match the zone Claude prints. overloaded_error is treated as a limit, which cools the account for an hour.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): `date +%Z` inside the container equals the host's (EDT/EST). Unit test parseResetTime on the latest real limit message saved in accounts/*/state.json last_error.
failure_signatures: cooldown_until off by 4-5 h
rate_limited during an Anthropic outage (overloaded_error)
limit not detected: status error instead of rate_limited
nodes.auto_repair: Clear a cooldown whose last_error is overloaded_error when svc.anthropic-status is operational (`ashley accounts enable`).
nodes.manual_fix: Update the patterns. Parse rate_limit_event from stream-json instead (see claude_swap_notes).
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic changing limit wording or the time zone in messages.

nodes.title: Remote Control and auth login behaviour
nodes.assumption: phone.js depends on this CLI behaviour. `claude auth login` in a pty prints a https://claude.(com|ai)/... URL containing oauth/authorize and reads the code from the pty ending in \r. A wrong code gets 'Invalid code'. `claude auth status` prints JSON with loggedIn. `claude remote-control` prints a session URL containing /code and refuses setup-tokens. The .claude.json keys hasCompletedOnboarding, theme and projects[p].hasTrustDialogAccepted suppress prompts. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC turn Remote Control off.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker, slow): run docs/research/rc_probe.sh. Pass = a sign-in URL matching URL_RE with oauth/authorize within 20 s, auth status JSON with a loggedIn key, and the expected 'must be logged in' text from remote-control without a login.
failure_signatures: phase stays 'login' (no URL matched)
three sign-in attempts did not work
phase error: unreadable auth status
nodes.manual_fix: Update URL_RE, pretrust keys and prompt handling in phone.js. Phone access stays off meanwhile.
nodes.future_risk: A new OAuth domain, device-code flow, changed onboarding keys, or Remote Control flags or subscription rules.

nodes.title: Lab CephFS volume mounted everywhere
nodes.assumption: /rs/rs_grp_oschome is mounted on the login node and every compute node, and the allocation (made 2026-09-21) is live.
nodes.check: grid: `stat -f -c %T /rs/rs_grp_oschome` reports ceph. The same holds inside the worker allocation.
failure_signatures: no shared library readable at /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared/ashley
Transport endpoint is not connected
No such file or directory
nodes.manual_fix: Lead checks the allocation with `df-ceph oschome` and contacts hpc@wayne.edu.
nodes.future_risk: Allocation term ending, path renamed (/rs to another prefix), mount method change.

nodes.title: Lab volume not full
nodes.assumption: The 20 TB oschome volume has room. Workspaces, npm caches, containers and every member's data share it, and CephFS quotas are per directory.
nodes.check: grid: `df-ceph oschome`, or `getfattr -n ceph.dir.rbytes` vs `ceph.quota.max_bytes` on /rs/rs_grp_oschome. Warn at 90 %, fail at 98 %.
failure_signatures: Disk quota exceeded
EDQUOT
nodes.manual_fix: Lead frees space or requests more.
nodes.future_risk: Dataset growth.

nodes.title: POSIX ACLs actually work on CephFS
nodes.assumption: setfacl on the lab volume takes effect. The mount has ACL support (kernel client acl option, or client_acl_type=posix_acl). grid.acl-tools only checks that the binaries exist; acl_revoke and path_traverse discard errors.
nodes.check: grid (admin, or a student in their own dir): create a temp file under /rs/rs_grp_oschome/$USER, `setfacl -m u:$USER:r--` it, confirm with `getfacl`, then delete it.
failure_signatures: setfacl: Operation not supported
approved, but N part(s) of the lab folder could not be opened
approved_unreadable
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu to mount with ACL support. Meanwhile, have C&IT add students to the oschome group.
nodes.future_risk: A CephFS remount or client change without ACLs.

nodes.title: library.json readable by the bash parser
nodes.assumption: lib_field, lib_default and lib_names parse library.json with grep and sed. That works only while every entry is a flat object (no nested {}) with string fields, in json.dump(indent=1) form.
nodes.check: grid: for each name in lib_names, lib_field sandbox and claude_bin are non-empty and match the python3 json parse inside the container.
failure_signatures: no library entry '<name>'
adopted with an empty sandbox
nodes.manual_fix: Keep entries flat, or parse with python3 in the container.
nodes.future_risk: Adding a nested field (env, gpu details) to an entry.

nodes.title: Library runtime path still exists
nodes.assumption: Each entry's runtime is an absolute module path baked in at publish time (/wsu/el7/gnu7/apptainer/1.2.2/bin/apptainer). adopt copies it into every student's RUNTIME, so a stale path comes back after each adopt even when grid.runtime repaired it.
nodes.check: grid: each entry's runtime is executable.
failure_signatures: REFUSING: runtime ... missing on <node>
configured runtime ... is gone
nodes.auto_repair: Admin: rewrite each entry's runtime to the discover_runtime path (python3 in the container, .part+rename), then `ashley access admin resync`.
nodes.manual_fix: Lead republishes the containers.
nodes.future_risk: An OS upgrade from el7 to el8/el9 changes the /wsu/el7 prefix, and a module is retired.

nodes.title: Every container file is readable
nodes.assumption: After publish (chmod -R g+rX, then resync ACLs), no file in a sandbox or npm prefix stays unreadable to approved students. Image files with mode 0600 or 0700 would otherwise fail at exec.
nodes.check: grid (admin, slow): `find <sandbox> <npm prefix> ! -perm -g+r -print -quit` finds nothing.
failure_signatures: Permission denied inside the container for an approved student
EACCES: node_modules/...
nodes.auto_repair: Admin: `chmod -R g+rX` on the tree, then `ashley access admin resync`.
nodes.manual_fix: Lead runs the repair.
nodes.future_risk: New images with restrictive modes.

nodes.title: Lab admin is the owner of shared/
nodes.assumption: The lab admin is whoever owns /rs/rs_grp_oschome/shared (stat -c %U). Every admin and student decision depends on it.
nodes.check: grid: the owner of shared/ exists in passwd and equals the expected lead (for example ASHLEY_ADMIN or the recorded admin).
failure_signatures: only the lab admin (<unknown>) can manage requests
student sees 'you are the lab admin'
nodes.manual_fix: Ask hpc@wayne.edu to restore ownership of shared/ to the lead.
nodes.future_risk: C&IT chowning the volume, or the lead leaving.

nodes.title: Access requests are not waiting unseen
nodes.assumption: Requests are ingested only when the admin runs an admin command (for example opening Ashley). Nothing runs on a schedule.
nodes.check: grid (admin): status files in state pending with 'requested' older than 3 days. Warn when any exist.
failure_signatures: student stuck at 'Waiting for lab access'
nodes.manual_fix: Lead opens Ashley: Lab access and decides.
nodes.future_risk: Lead turnover.

nodes.title: Anthropic token check semantics
nodes.assumption: GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models with Bearer <setup-token>, anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20 and anthropic-version 2023-06-01 answers 200 for a valid subscription token and 401 for an invalid one. If the beta header is retired or OAuth is refused on /v1/models, every valid token looks 'rejected' and lab access is blocked.
nodes.check: laptop or grid: send a request with a deliberately invalid token. Pass = HTTP 401 with error.type authentication_error. Any 400 or 404 mentioning oauth or beta means the contract changed.
failure_signatures: CLAUDE_TOKEN rejected for a token that works in claude -p
HTTP 400 OAuth authentication is currently not supported
nodes.manual_fix: Verify the token by a 1-turn claude -p on the worker instead, and update the check.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic changing the oauth beta header or endpoint policy.

nodes.title: Anthropic service health
nodes.assumption: Failures are attributed to Ashley only when Anthropic itself is up. An outage (529 overloaded_error) otherwise looks like a limit or a broken worker.
nodes.check: laptop: GET https://status.claude.com/api/v2/status.json. The indicator is 'none' (warn on minor, major or critical).
failure_signatures: overloaded_error
API Error: 529
api_error
nodes.manual_fix: Wait for the incident to clear.
nodes.future_risk: Status page URL changes.

nodes.title: Hugging Face whoami JSON as grepped
nodes.assumption: The grid parses https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2 with grep '"name":"[^"]*"' (no space after the colon). A reformatted response would make valid tokens look rejected and block lab access.
nodes.check: grid: whoami-v2 with the stored token. The grep yields a name iff python3 or node JSON parsing yields one.
failure_signatures: HF_TOKEN rejected or unreachable for a valid token
Hugging Face token missing or rejected
nodes.manual_fix: Use a whitespace-tolerant pattern ('"name": *"'), as the GitHub check already does.
nodes.future_risk: HF API response formatting or path deprecation (whoami-v2).

nodes.title: Base image pull from Docker Hub
nodes.assumption: `apptainer build --sandbox` can pull docker://node:22-bookworm anonymously from compute nodes. Many users share the grid's outbound IP, which counts toward Docker Hub's pull limits.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): GET https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/ answers 401 (reachable). A token fetch for library/node reports ratelimit-remaining > 0. Run before a publish or bootstrap.
failure_signatures: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit
FATAL: While making image from oci registry: error fetching image
nodes.auto_repair: Retry the job later (resubmit with --begin=now+1hour).
nodes.manual_fix: Lead authenticates pulls (APPTAINER_DOCKER_USERNAME/PASSWORD) or mirrors the image.
nodes.future_risk: Docker Hub policy changes. node:22 end of life (2027-04-30); Debian bookworm end of life.

nodes.title: Claude Code installable from npm
nodes.assumption: registry.npmjs.org serves @anthropic-ai/claude-code at the pinned version together with its linux-x64 native optional dependency, from the compute node.
nodes.check: grid (in the worker): `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.283 version` inside the container returns 2.1.283. `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code version` gives the newest version, used for an update repair.
failure_signatures: STOP: npm install failed
npm ERR! 404 Not Found
npm ERR! code ETIMEDOUT
nodes.auto_repair: On a 404 for the pin, bootstrap with CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=<latest> (own), or admin publish (lab).
nodes.manual_fix: Ask the lead to publish a new container.
nodes.future_risk: Anthropic deprecating npm distribution or unpublishing old versions. npm registry outages.
